docs.text: Driver PF1550 Driver ¶ A C++20 driver for the PF1550 power management IC. It starts the chip, checks the charger against limits you declare, writes a typed configuration with read-back, and controls the charger, the bucks, the LDOs and the power states, on any MCU. Quickstart API guide Source on GitHub The driver has no platform code. You give it a small class that brings the bus up and moves bytes; it does the rest: the limit and acknowledgement checks, the register framing, the write order the datasheet needs, the read-backs, the bounded waits and the error mapping. Power management IC PF1550 NXP Semiconductors Charger Linear single-cell charger with power path, 3.5 V to 4.44 V, 100 mA to 1 A, JEITA, watchdog, LED driver Regulators SW1 and SW2 buck with DVS, SW3 buck, LDO1 to LDO3, VREFDDR, VSNVS, coin cell charger Interface I2C up to 400 kHz; 7-bit address 0x08 to 0x0F set by OTP; single-register transfers States Run, Standby, Sleep, SHIP, CORE_OFF; power-up and power-down sequencer Interrupts INTB, 31 sources in 8 groups, each with a status, mask and sense register Supply Charger input 4.1 V to 6.0 V; I/O 1.7 V to 3.3 V What you get ¶ One object per chip. PF1550<YourPort> takes a reference to your port and a Config , and does no I/O until EnsureInitialized() . See API guide . Safety by construction. No public raw write; mandatory Limits ; acknowledgements for every downgrade; every write read back. See Contract and Configuration . Errors you can act on. Every call returns Result<T> with an Error such as Bus , Unsafe , OutOfLimits or Refused . See API guide . The whole chip. Charger, bucks, LDOs, VSNVS, coin cell, USBPHY, LED, power states, sequencer and interrupts; the coverage page lists what is modelled and what is not. Zero-overhead portability. The port is a CRTP class checked by a concept: the bus hooks and a delay, plus optional STANDBY, INTB, failure-report and logging hooks found at compile time. See Porting . No heap, no exceptions, no RTTI. The host tests build with -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti . Tested without hardware. Host tests run the driver against an independent register model of the chip. See Testing and CI . Nothing is verified on hardware yet. Datasheet ¶ Document Revision Get it Datasheet: PF1550 Power management integrated circuit (PMIC) for low power application processors (NXP Semiconductors PF1550) 7, 2021-09-29 vendor page Written against these revisions; the SHA-256 of each file is in docs/datasheets.yml . Where each part of the driver is in the datasheet: Datasheet map . Where to go next ¶ Quickstart Wire the chip, write the port, start the driver and read the charger. Hardware Pins, bus settings, the package and the power. Contract What the driver promises, what it needs, threading, errors and the open questions. API guide Start, configure, charge, control rails and handle errors, task by task. Porting Implement the port for your MCU. API reference Every class and member, generated from the headers.

docs.text: Ambiguities ¶ Places where the datasheet (Rev. 7) is silent, inconsistent or typed wrongly, and what the driver does about each. The driver is safe under every reading: each row is a documented behaviour, and where the chip could behave in more than one way the host-test model has a knob (a field of its Readings structure) that runs the other readings, or the row says that there is none and why. The numbers C1 to C59 are the ones the tests cite. A reading marked "Resolved" was decided against the safe side; the rest are open until someone measures the chip. Table, section and page numbers are the datasheet's own ( Table n , S for a section, p for the printed page). # Question (the datasheet is silent or inconsistent) Resolution, model knob and driver behaviour C1 OTP_SWx_DVS_SEL (Table 31) has no register: DVS mode of SW1/SW2 cannot be read (6.2.2, p28) Config declares Dvs::Enabled/Disabled per buck; voltage writes only when declared enabled; model runs both. C2 SW3 voltage registers "read only because DVS is not supported" (Table 122 to Table 124, 6.3.3): are writes ignored or stored? Model sw3_write_ignored ; driver never writes them. C3 Interrupt clearing: PMIC STAT bits "Read or Write 1 to clear" (Table 90 note); charger CHG_INT is RW1S in Table 150 and RW1C in the bitmap (Table 175) Model knob int_clear {WriteOne, OnRead, Both} (all groups); driver copies the value out first, writes 1 only to reported bits, bounded 3 passes. C4 RW1S (most charger and rail fields): footnote "Load from OTP fuse, Read, and Write" versus the name "write-1-to-set" Model rw1s_set_only (a written 0 does not clear); driver verifies after every write and returns VerifyFailed . C5 KEY1 is at 0x6F in the bitmap (Table 174 p125); Tables 148 and 149 both print ADDR 0x6B (RC_16MHZ is at 0x6B in the bitmap); CHGR_KEY2 "Reserved" at 0x9F (Table 173); no key sequence or OTP window is documented in Rev. 7 Resolved: KEY1 = 0x6F (two registers cannot share an address; the table of contents repeats the table error). The model decodes KEY1 at 0x6F and RC_16MHZ at 0x6B; none is exposed. C6 GOTO_SHIP : Table 138 "any state"; 10.2.3 "in REGS_DISABLE"; Table 83 G takes RUN/STANDBY/SLEEP to REGS_DISABLE on GOTO_SHIP=1, J enters SHIP only if VBUS < 1.0 V (footnote 10), footnote 4 "does not stay"; AN13554 "GOTO_SHIP = 1 and VBUSIN < 1 V". With VBUS valid the data sheet is silent (power-down happens, SHIP is not stated) Resolved to the safe reading: EnterShip needs state Run/Standby/Sleep and VBUS below UVLO, refuses with VBUS valid ( Contract ). Model knob ship_with_vbus {RegsDisableOnly, BitIgnored, ShipsAnyway} runs all three; the session test checks that EnterShip is refused with VBUS valid and writes nothing under each. C7 GOTO_CORE_OFF : Table 83 I needs VBUS_INVALID and ONKEY = 1; footnotes 8 and 9 say it is set "when system is ON" (secondary processor for other products) Model core_off_needs_run ; driver EnterCoreOff requires the token, VBUS invalid (VBUS_SNS), ONKEY sense high. C8 WD_TIME prints "0" for both 80 s and 32 s (Table 161); tWD 80 s typical with ±20 % (Table 12): the shortest possible period is 25.6 s Model wd_time_one_is_32s with accuracy; driver services at <= 16 s whichever reading holds and defaults to the reset value. C9 Watchdog expiry: 8.9.2 says CHG_SNS = 0x0B, Table 154 marks 0x0B Reserved and defines WDT_SNS b5 Model wdt_reports_0x0b ; driver treats either as expired. C10 OTP_FLAVOR values 4 to 9 not listed (Table 87 "continues"); A0 "internal validation only" (Table 1 footnote) Driver reports the raw byte, a named option only for listed values, never an error; A0 supported by reading with a contract note. C11 Table 116 is titled "SW1_SLP_VOLT" at 0x36 Treated as SW1_CTRL1 (consistent with 0x3C, 0x42); register-reference check in Table 04. C12 Table 141 is titled "SW2_PWRDN_SEQ" at 0x61; table 140 has the same title at 0x60 Treated as SW3_PWRDN_SEQ (bitmap order); not exposed. C13 Tables 148 and 149 share ADDR 0x6B See C5 (resolved to 0x6F). C14 Charger CHG_INT bits RW1S footnote versus ordinary status: the bit reset condition differs per field (VCOREDIG_RSTB, CHGPOK_RSTB, POR). VBUS_LIN_ILIM is the one driver-written field with CHGPOK_RSTB: an invalid VBUSIN (a cable removal) puts it back to its OTP value (Table 163) The model has two events: Reset() (VCOREDIG or POR: every register) and VbusRemoved() (only VBUS_LIN_ILIM ). The driver does not use VBUS_LIN_ILIM as evidence of a chip reset ( PartialResetBits ), so a cable removal is not DeviceReset ; the reverted limit is the OTP one: charging is refused when it is above Limits.input_max_ma , and the status reads, the interrupt service and the watchdog service write the configured limit again (once VBUSIN is valid: while it is invalid the model holds the field in reset, env.vbus_limit_held ) or switch the charger off ( input_limit_ok in SelfCheck() ). No other per-field reset condition of a written field is modelled apart from the whole-chip reset. Bench step: remove and restore VBUSIN and read VBUS_INLIM_CNFG. C15 Reset sources are stated only by the bitmap legend (p122: [1] invalid VCOREDIG, [2] PORB or RESETBMCU, [3] pulse to REGS_DISABLE) and charger "Reset condition" lines; whether an MCU reset leaves PMIC registers unchanged is not stated No assumption is made. No knob: the model's Reset() is the reset the chip applies (every register to its start-up value), and the driver sees a reset only by a register it changed reading back differently (C59); EnsureInitialized re-reads identity and the as-found check, Configure re-verifies. C16 Charge parameter change while charging: glitch-free? CHG_OPER 0 to 2 needed to re-latch? Model knob apply_delay_us (C49) is the delay before a parameter takes effect; no knob for the glitch; driver writes with the charger not in mode 2, CHG_OPER last, verifies (see C49). C17 PRECHGLB_THRS codes 1 to 3 Reserved, only 2.8 V documented Only code 0 encodable. C18 BOVRC_DISBATFET / BATFET_OC : Table 161 text versus 8.9.6 about what keeps the BATFET closed No knob: the driver writes BATFET_OC and BOVRC bits only with the acknowledgement, whichever text is right, and never writes the whole byte from one read (B1). C19 CHG_CC codes above 1000 mA are labelled Reserved while the feature list says 100 to 1000 mA Only documented codes encodable; model treats a forced reserved code as no change. C20 VBUS_LIN_ILIM codes 21 to 31 Reserved; low settings (10 to 50 mA) use the linear low-power mode (8.7.2) Reserved not encodable. C21 CHG_SNS reset 1000 (state 8) while the charger registers reset with VCOREDIG_RSTB: first read after reset Model initial value; driver never acts on a first read alone. C22 SILICON_REV : fields METAL 001, FULL 010 give 0x11 (Table 88) but the bitmap reset is 0x08 (FULL_LAYER_REV = 001); all fields "Unused" Stored raw, no decision made; model knob silicon_rev_reset {0x11, 0x08}. C23 USE_DEFAULT_ADDR (Table 147): effect undefined; address 0x08 to 0x0F set by fuses Not touched (no knob: the driver never writes the bit, so no reading of its effect is reachable). C24 DPM default: Table 5 says 4.4 V; Table 164 and Table 62 give reset 000 = 3.90 V; Table 85 gives 3.9 V or 4.5 V per option Driver always writes its configured dpm_mv and verifies; the model's default is the option's (Table 85); no knob. C25 EOC_MODE "Unused" in Table 158 but an option in Table 85 (done to linear mode) Not exposed (no knob: the driver has no way to write it). C26 Timer accuracy tacc and tSCIDG 0 to 2 ms: CHG_I and CHG_SNS after a state change Driver waits the datasheet maximum before trusting a status; no knob: the model's status registers follow a state change at once. C27 VBUS_SNS, CHG_SNS and BATT_SNS are separate transfers Documented non-atomic; consistent flag. C28 Interrupt category summary (INT_CATEGORY) versus charger page: CHG_INT summarised in b0 only Model derives the summary from the status bits at once (no knob); ServiceInterrupts loops at most three passes, so a lagging summary is read again. C29 UVDET and LOW_SYS_WARN are OTP-loaded and writable; Table 137 lists rising and falling thresholds (UVDET 2.65/2.55, 2.8/2.7, 3.0/2.9, 3.⅓.0 V; LOW_SYS_WARN 3.3/3.1 to 3.9/3.7 V). No ambiguity; a wrong UVDET resets the system (Table 83 G) UVDET guarded by undervoltage_threshold for that reason only. Model uses the table values. C30 POR_DLY code 001 not defined (Table 135); OTP-loaded Not exposed. C31 LDO load-switch mode (7.2.6): no current limit; does LDOx_FAULTI fire? Model ls_fault_interrupt ; load switch needs a token. C32 Low-power mode LPWR is for loads below 10 mA (7.x, Table 42); no register enforces it low_power requires the acknowledgement load_below_10ma . C33 SW1/SW2 non-DVS table: 3.30 V for every code 7 to 63 (Table 31) Driver writes only code 7 for 3.3 V; any code >= 7 decodes to 3.3 V. C34 DVS done interrupt and settle time (DVSSPEED) not bounded in the register text Driver waits the DVS-done event or DelayUs maximum; model dvs_done_delay_us . C35 STBY/SLP voltage registers in non-DVS mode: "read-only and must not be written" (6.2.5) yet marked RW Never written; model nondvs_write_accepted . C36 STATE_INFO has codes for WAIT, RUN, STANDBY, SLEEP, REGS_DISABLE only; CORE_OFF and SHIP have no I2C-visible state Decoded Unknown otherwise; the model reports no state when system off. C37 Table 83 lettering skips D Recorded here only; no matrix row. C38 PWRON level or edge sensitivity is OTP_PWRON_CFG , not a register Declared in Config ; model both columns of Table 83. C39 STANDBYDLY and STANDBYINV effects on pin handling (Table 76) StandbyPin hook optional; no knob (the model does not time the pin). C40 VCOIN 0111 is printed as 3.3 V (Table 111 p91) while the step is 100 mV per LSB from 1.8 V (0111 would be 2.5 V); Table 25 (p22) gives a valid range of 1.8 to 3.3 V, which 16 codes fill with 3.3 V = 1111 Adopted reading: step 100 mV, 3.3 V = 1111. Because the printed code differs, codes above 0 need Limits.coin_cell_max_mv >= 3300 . No knob: the model stores VCOIN and does not charge a cell; the literal reading is the bench step in docs/datasheet.md . C41 PWRONDBNC / ONKEYDBNC codes 00 and 01 are identical (Table 136) Enum offers 31.25 ms once; both codes decode the same. C42 TGRESET is a register (Table 135) but 10.4 calls it OTP_TGRESET Writing guarded (acknowledgement); no knob (the model accepts the write). C43 LED_PWM 6-bit field versus duty n/32 (values above 32 undefined) Driver encodes 0 to 32 only (no knob: no value above 32 is reachable). C44 LED_CURRENT only 01 = 6.0 mA valid Only 6 mA encodable. C45 Charger registers all "RW" in the LED/USB blocks but reserved bits RW: reserved bits written 0 or preserved? Preserved by read-modify-write; test Table 03. C46 REGTEMP code 3 Reserved (Table 162) Not encodable. C47 IO_DRV0 and IO_DRV1 appear only in the bitmap (Table 174 p125) Not exposed; model stores. C48 Multi-byte reads and auto-increment not described (9.7.2) Never used (no knob: no multi-byte transfer is reachable; the bus layer refuses one). C49 Does a charge parameter write take effect at once (C16 timing)? Model apply_delay ; driver verifies by read-back. C50 SW3_CTRL b4: Table 125 says UNUSED, the bitmap (Table 174 p124) says SW3_DVSSPEED, RW1S; PWRCTRL3 b7:2 and TEMP_INT_MASK0 b3 and b1: tables unused, bitmap RW or reset 1 Not exposed; reserved bits preserved by read-modify-write; model stores the bitmap type. C51 Table 112 (SW1_VOLT): VOLT[5:0] and UNUSED[7:5] overlap on bit 5; Table 147 (I2C_ADDR) has no row for bits 6:3; the bitmap prints PWRCTRL2 as "015A" and DEVICE_ID FAMILY as [3:7]; OTP_FLAVOR is [7:0] in Table 87 but [5:0] in the bitmap Typos recorded; field rows use the table; row FLD-68.GAP_6_3 added; knob none. C52 Feature list (p2) "battery discharge overcurrent up to 3.0 A" and "6.5 V input operating range" versus Table 14 (2.2, 2.8, 3.2 A typical, 2.0 to 4.0 A range) and Table 5 (VBUS valid from UVLO rising 3.8 to 4.2 V up to OVLO rising 6.0 to 7.0 V: a 6.0 V supply can already be in OVLO) Driver reports VBUS_OVLO_SNS; the contract states the Table 14 and Table 5 numbers and that a 6.0 V input is not guaranteed valid. C53 Table 160 CHGCV is not one-to-one: codes 0 to 8 all 3.50 V, 9 to 55 = 3.52 to 4.44 V in 20 mV steps, 56 to 63 all 4.44 V Only codes 8 to 55 encodable. C54 Power-up sequencer (section 10.6, Table 85): the slot of a regulator with PWRUP_SEQ = n is not stated; is the number 1 the first slot, and does 0 start in the first slot or never? Reading: n starts (n - 1) slots after the first one, 0 starts in the first slot. Model seq0_starts_first ; PowerUpDelayUs() follows the reading. C55 Power-down sequencer (section 10.7): regulators with the same PWRDN_SEQ number: one after the other or together? Reading: together, (highest - own) steps of 2 ms (Table 84, tD5). Model and PowerDownDelayUs() follow it. C56 Power-down sequencer: a regulator with PWRDN_SEQ = 0 while others are non-zero Reading: it turns off last, after the highest number's delay. Model seq_order_zero_last ; all zero bypasses the sequencer. C57 Table 85 OTP_SW1_DVS_SEL and OTP_SW2_DVS_SEL are printed in merged cells of a wide table; which option column each value belongs to is read from a text extraction of the PDF, not from the table's grid. The flavour byte of options A4 to A9 is not listed (C10) The driver trusts the profile only for the listed options A1 to A3 and refuses a declaration that contradicts it for a block it configures; for any other part (including A0) the declaration stands and a DVS declaration needs Acknowledgements::dvs_on_unlisted_part . Model: the option table. Bench step: read SW1 and SW2 in both modes. C58 WDTCLR (Table 161) is typed plain RW, "writing 01 clears the watchdog": does the field hold the written value, and does a clear need a 0 to 01 edge? The driver writes WDTCLR = 01 and, when it reads 01 back before a service, writes 00 first, so each service is an edge either way; the two bits are not compared in the read-back. Model wdtclr_holds . Bench step: service twice at 8 s and watch CHG_SNS WDT . C59 PWRUP_I: Table 108 and section 10.6 define it as the completion of the STANDBY to RUN and SLEEP to RUN transitions; no text says that a power-on or a reset sets it, and no other bit is defined as a reset flag The driver does not use PWRUP_I as a reset flag (it is an ordinary event, also set by a standby wake-up). A reset is seen as hardware lessons 12a asks: after a verified write that changed a register bit, the driver remembers the value, and a changing call first reads the recorded registers back; a difference twice in a row is DeviceReset . A reset that leaves every driver-written bit at its start-up value shows nothing, and needs nothing (the chip holds what the driver wrote). Model knob pwrup_flag_at_reset (default off) runs the reading in which a reset sets PWRUP_I as well; a STANDBY to RUN transition is raised with Raise(0x28, 0) . Bench step: read MISC_INT_STAT0 after a power-up and a UVDET reset. C60 VBUS_LIN_ILIM default: Table 163 gives the reset value 01101 (code 13, 400 mA); the OTP table (OTP_CHG_CFG5) says OTP_CHGR_VBUS_LIN_ILIM "VBUS ILIM = 1500 mA" (code 20). A cable removal puts the field back to its reset condition (CHGPOK_RSTB, C14), so which value comes back is open The model uses the OTP value of the option (1500 mA, above the 1 A Limits of the tests), which is the harder case for the driver: the configured limit is written again, or the charger is switched off ( OutOfLimits ). Under the Table 163 reading (400 mA) the reverted limit is below Limits and the same restore applies. Bench step: remove and restore VBUSIN and read VBUS_INLIM_CNFG. How to change a reading ¶ The knob of a row is a field of pf1550_test::Readings in tests/mock_pf1550.hpp . A test that sets it runs the driver against the other reading. When a bench measurement settles a row, change the model's default, keep the knob for the other reading, and say so in the changelog . Nothing here is verified on hardware.

No knob: the model's Reset() is the reset the chip applies (every register to its start-up value), and the driver sees a reset only by a register it changed reading back differently (C59); EnsureInitialized re-reads identity and the as-found check, Configure re-verifies. C16 Charge parameter change while charging: glitch-free? CHG_OPER 0 to 2 needed to re-latch? Model knob apply_delay_us (C49) is the delay before a parameter takes effect; no knob for the glitch; driver writes with the charger not in mode 2, CHG_OPER last, verifies (see C49). C17 PRECHGLB_THRS codes 1 to 3 Reserved, only 2.8 V documented Only code 0 encodable. C18 BOVRC_DISBATFET / BATFET_OC : Table 161 text versus 8.9.6 about what keeps the BATFET closed No knob: the driver writes BATFET_OC and BOVRC bits only with the acknowledgement, whichever text is right, and never writes the whole byte from one read (B1). C19 CHG_CC codes above 1000 mA are labelled Reserved while the feature list says 100 to 1000 mA Only documented codes encodable; model treats a forced reserved code as no change. C20 VBUS_LIN_ILIM codes 21 to 31 Reserved; low settings (10 to 50 mA) use the linear low-power mode (8.7.2) Reserved not encodable. C21 CHG_SNS reset 1000 (state 8) while the charger registers reset with VCOREDIG_RSTB: first read after reset Model initial value; driver never acts on a first read alone. C22 SILICON_REV : fields METAL 001, FULL 010 give 0x11 (Table 88) but the bitmap reset is 0x08 (FULL_LAYER_REV = 001); all fields "Unused" Stored raw, no decision made; model knob silicon_rev_reset {0x11, 0x08}. C23 USE_DEFAULT_ADDR (Table 147): effect undefined; address 0x08 to 0x0F set by fuses Not touched (no knob: the driver never writes the bit, so no reading of its effect is reachable). C24 DPM default: Table 5 says 4.4 V; Table 164 and Table 62 give reset 000 = 3.90 V; Table 85 gives 3.9 V or 4.5 V per option Driver always writes its configured dpm_mv and verifies; the model's default is the option's (Table 85); no knob. C25 EOC_MODE "Unused" in Table 158 but an option in Table 85 (done to linear mode) Not exposed (no knob: the driver has no way to write it). C26 Timer accuracy tacc and tSCIDG 0 to 2 ms: CHG_I and CHG_SNS after a state change Driver waits the datasheet maximum before trusting a status; no knob: the model's status registers follow a state change at once. C27 VBUS_SNS, CHG_SNS and BATT_SNS are separate transfers Documented non-atomic; consistent flag. C28 Interrupt category summary (INT_CATEGORY) versus charger page: CHG_INT summarised in b0 only Model derives the summary from the status bits at once (no knob); ServiceInterrupts loops at most three passes, so a lagging summary is read again. C29 UVDET and LOW_SYS_WARN are OTP-loaded and writable; Table 137 lists rising and falling thresholds (UVDET 2.65/2.55, 2.8/2.7, 3.0/2.9, 3.⅓.0 V; LOW_SYS_WARN 3.3/3.1 to 3.9/3.7 V). No ambiguity; a wrong UVDET resets the system (Table 83 G) UVDET guarded by undervoltage_threshold for that reason only. Model uses the table values. C30 POR_DLY code 001 not defined (Table 135); OTP-loaded Not exposed. C31 LDO load-switch mode (7.2.6): no current limit; does LDOx_FAULTI fire? Model ls_fault_interrupt ; load switch needs a token. C32 Low-power mode LPWR is for loads below 10 mA (7.x, Table 42); no register enforces it low_power requires the acknowledgement load_below_10ma . C33 SW1/SW2 non-DVS table: 3.30 V for every code 7 to 63 (Table 31) Driver writes only code 7 for 3.3 V; any code >= 7 decodes to 3.3 V. C34 DVS done interrupt and settle time (DVSSPEED) not bounded in the register text Driver waits the DVS-done event or DelayUs maximum; model dvs_done_delay_us . C35 STBY/SLP voltage registers in non-DVS mode: "read-only and must not be written" (6.2.5) yet marked RW Never written; model nondvs_write_accepted . C36 STATE_INFO has codes for WAIT, RUN, STANDBY, SLEEP, REGS_DISABLE only; CORE_OFF and SHIP have no I2C-visible state Decoded Unknown otherwise; the model reports no state when system off. C37 Table 83 lettering skips D Recorded here only; no matrix row. C38 PWRON level or edge sensitivity is OTP_PWRON_CFG , not a register Declared in Config ; model both columns of Table 83. C39 STANDBYDLY and STANDBYINV effects on pin handling (Table 76) StandbyPin hook optional; no knob (the model does not time the pin). C40 VCOIN 0111 is printed as 3.3 V (Table 111 p91) while the step is 100 mV per LSB from 1.8 V (0111 would be 2.5 V); Table 25 (p22) gives a valid range of 1.8 to 3.3 V, which 16 codes fill with 3.3 V = 1111 Adopted reading: step 100 mV, 3.3 V = 1111. Because the printed code differs, codes above 0 need Limits.coin_cell_max_mv >= 3300 . No knob: the model stores VCOIN and does not charge a cell; the literal reading is the bench step in docs/datasheet.md . C41 PWRONDBNC / ONKEYDBNC codes 00 and 01 are identical (Table 136) Enum offers 31.25 ms once; both codes decode the same. C42 TGRESET is a register (Table 135) but 10.4 calls it OTP_TGRESET Writing guarded (acknowledgement); no knob (the model accepts the write). C43 LED_PWM 6-bit field versus duty n/32 (values above 32 undefined) Driver encodes 0 to 32 only (no knob: no value above 32 is reachable). C44 LED_CURRENT only 01 = 6.0 mA valid Only 6 mA encodable. C45 Charger registers all "RW" in the LED/USB blocks but reserved bits RW: reserved bits written 0 or preserved? Preserved by read-modify-write; test Table 03. C46 REGTEMP code 3 Reserved (Table 162) Not encodable. C47 IO_DRV0 and IO_DRV1 appear only in the bitmap (Table 174 p125) Not exposed; model stores. C48 Multi-byte reads and auto-increment not described (9.7.2) Never used (no knob: no multi-byte transfer is reachable; the bus layer refuses one). C49 Does a charge parameter write take effect at once (C16 timing)? Model apply_delay ; driver verifies by read-back. C50 SW3_CTRL b4: Table 125 says UNUSED, the bitmap (Table 174 p124) says SW3_DVSSPEED, RW1S; PWRCTRL3 b7:2 and TEMP_INT_MASK0 b3 and b1: tables unused, bitmap RW or reset 1 Not exposed; reserved bits preserved by read-modify-write; model stores the bitmap type. C51 Table 112 (SW1_VOLT): VOLT[5:0] and UNUSED[7:5] overlap on bit 5; Table 147 (I2C_ADDR) has no row for bits 6:3; the bitmap prints PWRCTRL2 as "015A" and DEVICE_ID FAMILY as [3:7]; OTP_FLAVOR is [7:0] in Table 87 but [5:0] in the bitmap Typos recorded; field rows use the table; row FLD-68.GAP_6_3 added; knob none. C52 Feature list (p2) "battery discharge overcurrent up to 3.0 A" and "6.5 V input operating range" versus Table 14 (2.2, 2.8, 3.2 A typical, 2.0 to 4.0 A range) and Table 5 (VBUS valid from UVLO rising 3.8 to 4.2 V up to OVLO rising 6.0 to 7.0 V: a 6.0 V supply can already be in OVLO) Driver reports VBUS_OVLO_SNS; the contract states the Table 14 and Table 5 numbers and that a 6.0 V input is not guaranteed valid. C53 Table 160 CHGCV is not one-to-one: codes 0 to 8 all 3.50 V, 9 to 55 = 3.52 to 4.44 V in 20 mV steps, 56 to 63 all 4.44 V Only codes 8 to 55 encodable. C54 Power-up sequencer (section 10.6, Table 85): the slot of a regulator with PWRUP_SEQ = n is not stated; is the number 1 the first slot, and does 0 start in the first slot or never? Reading: n starts (n - 1) slots after the first one, 0 starts in the first slot. Model seq0_starts_first ; PowerUpDelayUs() follows the reading. C55 Power-down sequencer (section 10.7): regulators with the same PWRDN_SEQ number: one after the other or together? Reading: together, (highest - own) steps of 2 ms (Table 84, tD5). Model and PowerDownDelayUs() follow it. C56 Power-down sequencer: a regulator with PWRDN_SEQ = 0 while others are non-zero Reading: it turns off last, after the highest number's delay. Model seq_order_zero_last ; all zero bypasses the sequencer. C57 Table 85 OTP_SW1_DVS_SEL and OTP_SW2_DVS_SEL are printed in merged cells of a wide table; which option column each value belongs to is read from a text extraction of the PDF, not from the table's grid. The flavour byte of options A4 to A9 is not listed (C10) The driver trusts the profile only for the listed options A1 to A3 and refuses a declaration that contradicts it for a block it configures; for any other part (including A0) the declaration stands and a DVS declaration needs Acknowledgements::dvs_on_unlisted_part . Model: the option table. Bench step: read SW1 and SW2 in both modes. C58 WDTCLR (Table 161) is typed plain RW, "writing 01 clears the watchdog": does the field hold the written value, and does a clear need a 0 to 01 edge? The driver writes WDTCLR = 01 and, when it reads 01 back before a service, writes 00 first, so each service is an edge either way; the two bits are not compared in the read-back. Model wdtclr_holds . Bench step: service twice at 8 s and watch CHG_SNS WDT . C59 PWRUP_I: Table 108 and section 10.6 define it as the completion of the STANDBY to RUN and SLEEP to RUN transitions; no text says that a power-on or a reset sets it, and no other bit is defined as a reset flag The driver does not use PWRUP_I as a reset flag (it is an ordinary event, also set by a standby wake-up). A reset is seen as hardware lessons 12a asks: after a verified write that changed a register bit, the driver remembers the value, and a changing call first reads the recorded registers back; a difference twice in a row is DeviceReset . A reset that leaves every driver-written bit at its start-up value shows nothing, and needs nothing (the chip holds what the driver wrote). Model knob pwrup_flag_at_reset (default off) runs the reading in which a reset sets PWRUP_I as well; a STANDBY to RUN transition is raised with Raise(0x28, 0) . Bench step: read MISC_INT_STAT0 after a power-up and a UVDET reset. C60 VBUS_LIN_ILIM default: Table 163 gives the reset value 01101 (code 13, 400 mA); the OTP table (OTP_CHG_CFG5) says OTP_CHGR_VBUS_LIN_ILIM "VBUS ILIM = 1500 mA" (code 20). A cable removal puts the field back to its reset condition (CHGPOK_RSTB, C14), so which value comes back is open The model uses the OTP value of the option (1500 mA, above the 1 A Limits of the tests), which is the harder case for the driver: the configured limit is written again, or the charger is switched off ( OutOfLimits ). Under the Table 163 reading (400 mA) the reverted limit is below Limits and the same restore applies. Bench step: remove and restore VBUSIN and read VBUS_INLIM_CNFG.

docs.text: The knob of a row is a field of pf1550_test::Readings in tests/mock_pf1550.hpp . A test that sets it runs the driver against the other reading. When a bench measurement settles a row, change the model's default, keep the knob for the other reading, and say so in the changelog . Nothing here is verified on hardware.

docs.text: API guide ¶ How to use the driver task by task. Every call returns pf1550::Result<T> : check it before you use value . Datasheet sections this page relies on From NXP Semiconductors PF1550 7: SWx output voltage setting and DVS-done: 6.2.5 Output voltage setting in SWx, p. 28 LDO1 and LDO3: 7.2 LDO1 and LDO3 detailed description, p. 35 LDO load switch mode: 7.2.7 LDOy load switch mode, p. 38 Charger operating modes: 8.1 Operating modes and behavioral description, p. 43 Charger input source detection: 8.2 Charger input source detection, p. 45 Charger state diagram: 8.4 Charger state diagram, p. 46 Charger faults and restart: 8.9 Fault states, p. 64 Charger watchdog: 8.9.2 Watchdog timer state, p. 65 PWRON: 9.1 PWRON, p. 68 STANDBY pin: 9.2 STANDBY, p. 69 RESETBMCU: 9.3 RESETBMCU, p. 69 INTB and the interrupt registers: 9.4 INTB, p. 70 ONKEY: 9.6 ONKEY, p. 71 State machine and transitions: 10 PF1550 state machine, p. 72 System ON, OFF, SHIP and CORE_OFF: 10.2 System OFF states, p. 74 Regulator power-up sequencer: 10.6 Regulator power-up sequencer, p. 77 Regulator power-down sequencer: 10.7 Regulator power-down sequencer, p. 78 Device start-up timing and pre-programmed options: 11 Device start up, p. 78 Device ID, silicon revision and OTP flavour: 12.1 Specific PMIC Registers (Offset is 0x00), p. 80 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The shape of the API ¶ Group Calls Writes the chip Lifecycle EnsureInitialized() , IsInitialized() , GetConfig() , Configure() Configure() only Identity and state ReadVariant() , ReadPowerState() , ReadSnapshot() , SelfCheck() , CheckChargerAgainstLimits() no Charger ReadChargerStatus() , SetChargerMode() , RestartCharger() , ServiceChargerWatchdog() yes Rails ReadRail() , SetRailModes() , SetRailVoltage() , EnableLoadSwitch() yes, except ReadRail() Power states RequestStandby() , EnterShip() , EnterCoreOff() , CancelShutdownRequest() , ReadPowerDownSequence() , SetPowerDownSequence() yes, except the read Interrupts SetIrqMask() , ReadCategories() , ReadSense() , ServiceInterrupts() , GetLatchedEvents() , ClearLatchedEvents() , IntbAsserted() masks and clears only Bench ReadRegister() no, read only There is no raw register write. ReadRegister() reads one documented register for bench work and writes nothing. The settings are typed ( Config and its blocks), checked against the datasheet grids and your Limits , and every register written is read back ( Contract ). Dangerous calls need a token. EnterShip(ShipConfirm{}) , EnterCoreOff(CoreOffConfirm{}) and EnableLoadSwitch(rail, LoadSwitchConfirm{.input_mv = 1800}) take a struct that you write out, so the call site says what it does; the load switch token carries the input voltage of the LDO, which the driver checks against Limits . Time is yours: the driver has no timer. The one wait it makes is bounded and goes through DelayUs() . Initialise and configure ¶ Start and configure pf1550 :: Error Start ( Pmic & pmic ) { if ( auto r = pmic . EnsureInitialized (); ! r ) { // validates, identifies, checks the charger as found return r . error ; } return pmic . Configure (). error ; // writes the blocks whose `apply` is true, charger last } EnsureInitialized() validates the stored Config , checks DEVICE_ID, checks your DVS declarations against Table 85 and reads the charger as found. It writes nothing, except that when AsFoundPolicy::MakeSafe is set and an unsafe charge is found on, one write that puts the charger in linear-only mode. A start-up that fails on an unsafe charger leaves the driver uninitialised, but SetChargerMode(Off) still works. Configure() writes every block whose apply flag is true, in this order: the rails (in Config::rail_order ), VSNVS, the coin cell, USBPHY, the LED, power control, the power-down order, the interrupt masks and, last, the charger. A block with apply = false is left as the chip holds it. The driver does not know the chip's OTP option. Read it with ReadVariant() and decide what your board needs: const auto v = pmic . ReadVariant (); // v.value.option is Option::A1 .. A9, A0 (not programmed) or Unknown; v.value.flavor_raw is always the raw byte. Charge ¶ The charger is parked before it is changed and is switched on only by the mode, written last. A configuration with charger.mode = ChargerMode::Charge writes the parameters in linear-only mode and enables charging at the end, unless the charger reports a fault ( ChargerFault : the parameters are written, charging is not enabled). Watch the charger pf1550 :: Error WatchCharger ( Pmic & pmic ) { const auto s = pmic . ReadChargerStatus (); if ( ! s ) { return s . error ; } if ( s . value . fault == pf1550 :: Fault :: TimerFault ) { return pmic . RestartCharger (). error ; // off, then on; at most three tries in a row } return pmic . ServiceChargerWatchdog (). error ; // every 16 s or less when the watchdog is on } ReadChargerStatus() makes four reads: VBUS_SNS, CHG_SNS, BATT_SNS and CHG_SNS again ( consistent says the two CHG_SNS reads agree). fault is classified: None , TimerFault , ThermistorSuspend , ThermalShutdown , BatteryOvervoltage , BatteryOvercurrent , WatchdogExpired , BatteryMissing or UnknownState . The reads are not atomic with each other (ambiguity C27). SetChargerMode(Off) and LinearOnly are allowed as soon as DEVICE_ID has passed, even after a failed start-up. Charge checks the charger's registers against Limits and the acknowledgements first, so a charge that was configured outside your limits by something else (a start-up option, another master) is refused with OutOfLimits or Unsafe . RestartCharger() leaves a latched fault state: off, verify, charge. Three attempts in a row without the charger reaching a charging state return Refused : find the cause (a cold or hot battery, a timer, a shorted cell). With watchdog.enable call ServiceChargerWatchdog() at least every 16 s. The datasheet reads 80 s or 32 s with 20 % accuracy; 16 s covers every reading. The call reads BATFET_CNFG until two reads agree and refuses with Unsafe if the battery overcurrent protection reads as off without allow_batfet_oc_off : a stuck line reads zero. Whether WDTCLR holds what is written is open (C58); the driver writes it as an edge either way. The input limit check does not need watchdog.enable : a cable removal puts VBUS_LIN_ILIM back to its OTP value (Table 163). With the charger in Charge (or LinearOnly, when the charger block is applied) ReadChargerStatus() , ServiceInterrupts() (when a charger interrupt is set) and ServiceChargerWatchdog() all read the limit. A limit that is not the configured one is written again once VBUSIN is valid (while it is invalid the field is held in reset and nothing is written; SelfCheck() reports input_limit_ok false). A limit above Limits that cannot be restored (the charger block is not applied) switches the charger off and returns OutOfLimits . A failed check returns its error and not the status: an application that needs the status regardless calls ReadSnapshot() , which reads it without the check. The check is not written over a chip that reset meanwhile ( DeviceReset ), and a charger interrupt that ServiceInterrupts() read owes the check until one has passed: a call that fails after the status byte was read (a later pass, the clear write), or a ClearLatchedEvents() in between, does not drop it, and the next call makes it again. Rails ¶ Change an LDO pf1550 :: Error Rails ( Pmic & pmic ) { if ( auto r = pmic . SetRailVoltage ( pf1550 :: Rail :: Ldo1 , pf1550 :: FromMillivolts ( 2800 )); ! r ) { return r . error ; // OutOfLimits when your Limits window does not allow it } return pmic . SetRailModes ( pf1550 :: Rail :: Ldo1 , { true , true , false , false }). error ; } Every rail needs a window in Limits::rail[...] ; SetRailVoltage() and SetRailModes() return OutOfLimits for a rail without one or a voltage outside it. SW1 and SW2: the run voltage can be written only when you declared Dvs::Enabled in BuckConfig::dvs ; otherwise ReadOnlyRail . The standby and sleep voltages are set in Configure() through standby_uv and sleep_uv . After a change of the run voltage of an enabled rail the call waits for the DVS-done flag (at most 256 us) and returns Timeout if it does not rise. SW3's voltage is read only (ambiguity C2): SetRailVoltage(Rail::Sw3, ...) returns ReadOnlyRail . SetRailModes() sets EN, STBY_EN, OMODE and LPWR. Low-power mode ( low_power ) needs ack.load_below_10ma : the datasheet specifies it for loads up to 10 mA. EnableLoadSwitch(Rail::Ldo1 or Ldo3, LoadSwitchConfirm{.input_mv}) is irreversible. It turns an LDO into a switch: the output is the input voltage, with no current limit, and it cannot be undone until the next power cycle (LS_EN 1 to 0 is not allowed). input_mv is the voltage of the rail that feeds the LDO; it must lie inside the rail's Limits window, and the rail must not be in low-power mode ( Refused ). An enable ( SetRailModes() , or a block in Configure() ) first reads the voltage registers it brings into effect and checks them against Limits ( OutOfLimits ): a rail never comes on at a voltage the load does not tolerate. Standby and sleep need run ( InvalidArgument otherwise): EN gates both (Table 42). ReadRail() reports the enables, the load-switch flag and the programmed run voltage, decoded in the DVS mode the part has (Table 85 for A1 to A3, else your declaration). Power states ¶ ReadPowerState() decodes STATE_INFO: Wait , Run , Standby , Sleep , RegsDisable , or Unknown (SHIP and CORE_OFF have no I2C-visible state because the chip is not powered, ambiguity C36). RequestStandby(bool) drives the STANDBY pin through your GpioSet() ; Unsupported without it. EnterShip() and EnterCoreOff() are guarded: Ship mode pf1550 :: Error ShipMode ( Pmic & pmic ) { // Cuts every supply, VSNVS included; recovery is a charger or a battery attach. return pmic . EnterShip ( pf1550 :: ShipConfirm {}). error ; } EnterShip() returns Refused unless the chip is in Run, Standby or Sleep and VBUS reads invalid and below UVLO. Everything is cut, VSNVS included; recovery is a charger or a battery attach. The chip enters SHIP only with VBUSIN below 1.0 V, which the driver cannot measure (ambiguity C6): with VBUSIN between 1 V and UVLO it ends in REGS_DISABLE. EnterCoreOff() needs VBUS invalid and ONKEY not pushed, and arms GOTO_CORE_OFF: it takes effect at the next REGS_DISABLE, not at once. Both requests stay set in PWRCTRL3 until CancelShutdownRequest() clears them; call it when the request is no longer wanted. It is not refused after DEVICE_ID has passed. - ReadPowerDownSequence() and SetPowerDownSequence() read and write the seven *_PWRDN_SEQ registers. The order decides which supply drops first, and a wrong order can damage a processor: the write needs ack.power_down_order_reviewed . All zero bypasses the sequencer (section 10.7). The sequencer ¶ The power-up order is fixed by OTP and cannot be read back over I2C, so the driver reports it only for the pre-programmed options A1 to A9 that Table 85 lists. The helpers are constexpr and have no I/O: When does each rail turn on void Sequencer () { // Table 85: the start-up order of option A4 and when each rail turns on (microseconds). const auto profile = pf1550 :: StartupProfileOf ( pf1550 :: Option :: A4 ); if ( profile ) { const uint32_t ldo1_us = pf1550 :: PowerUpDelayUs ( profile . value , pf1550 :: Rail :: Ldo1 ); const uint32_t total_us = pf1550 :: PowerUpDurationUs ( profile . value ); std :: printf ( "LDO1 at %u us of %u us \n " , static_cast < unsigned > ( ldo1_us ), static_cast < unsigned > ( total_us )); } } Helper Gives StartupProfileOf(Option) The PWRUP_SEQ order of each rail, the slot length (500 us for A1, else 2000 us) and whether PWRON is edge sensitive (A8); InvalidArgument for A0 and Unknown PowerUpDelayUs() , PowerUpDurationUs() When a rail starts, and when the last one does, from the start of the first slot ResetReleaseDelayMs() , ColdStartToResetReleaseUs() RESETBMCU's delay from POR_DLY (code 1 is undefined) and the whole cold-start time to its release PowerDownDelayUs() , PowerDownDurationUs() , IsPowerDownBypassed() The power-down schedule of a PowerDownSequence : (highest - own) steps of 2 ms MirrorOf(profile) The power-down order the registers hold after reset (section 10.7: it mirrors the power-up order) Where the datasheet is silent the readings are C54 to C56 in Ambiguities . Interrupts ¶ Service INTB pf1550 :: Error OnIntb ( Pmic & pmic ) { const auto e = pmic . ServiceInterrupts (); // reads, copies out, clears if ( ! e ) { return e . error ; } if ( pf1550 :: Has ( e . value , pf1550 :: IrqSource :: Onkey3s )) { std :: printf ( "ONKEY held for 3 s \n " ); } return e . value . fault_class ? pf1550 :: Error :: DeviceFault : pf1550 :: Error :: Ok ; } 31 sources in 8 groups ( IrqGroup ): charger, SW low side, SW high side, SW DVS, LDO, temperature, ONKEY and miscellaneous. Has(events, IrqSource::X) tests one; IsFaultSource() and fault_class mark rail, die and system-overvoltage faults. A source is masked by default ( IrqMask{} masks all). Config::apply_irq_mask writes Config::irq_mask ; UnmaskOnly(std::array{...}) builds one from a list of sources. A masked source still sets its status bit, but does not drive INTB. ServiceInterrupts() copies each status byte out before it clears it (read-then-clear, at most three passes). Its result holds the bytes as read, plus the status bits that other calls read in the meantime (the driver latches them; GetLatchedEvents() shows them). With GpioGet() , INTB high, every source unmasked through SetIrqMask() and an empty latch it returns at once without a transfer; otherwise it reads the chip. PWRUP_I is reported like any other event (it is the standby wake-up flag, not a reset flag). ReadCategories() and ReadSense() are the live views (not latched): use them to poll without clearing. A DVS step that the driver waits for ( SetRailVoltage() , Configure() of SW1 or SW2) reads SW_INT_STAT2 and clears the awaited rail's DVS-done bit, so that rail's own event is consumed by the wait and never reaches the latch; the other rail's bit is kept in the latch. Use ReadSense(IrqGroup::SwDvs) to watch DVS done without consuming it. Diagnostics ¶ ReadSnapshot() reads about 60 registers: identity, state, the charger, every sense register, the rails, the power-down order and POR_DLY . It is for logs and bring-up, not for a control loop. SelfCheck() answers four questions without writing: DEVICE_ID, state Run, every configured rail enabled as configured, and no latched fault. CheckChargerAgainstLimits() repeats the as-found check at any time. Handle errors ¶ Explain an error const char * Explain ( pf1550 :: Error e ) { switch ( e ) { case pf1550 :: Error :: OutOfLimits : return "the value is valid for the chip but outside your Limits" ; case pf1550 :: Error :: Unsafe : return "a safety downgrade needs its Acknowledgements flag" ; case pf1550 :: Error :: Refused : return "a precondition of a dangerous call is not met" ; case pf1550 :: Error :: NoDevice : return "nothing acknowledged the address" ; default : return pf1550 :: ToString ( e ); } } Error Usually means Do NotInitialized EnsureInitialized() has not succeeded Call it, and check its error InvalidArgument Off the grid, reserved, or Limits unset Fix the value; nothing was sent OutOfLimits Valid for the chip, outside your Limits Fix the value or, if the hardware allows it, the limit Unsafe A downgrade without its acknowledgement Set the flag in Config::ack only if you mean it ReadOnlyRail SW3, or a buck not declared DVS Declare Dvs::Enabled if the OTP says so Refused A precondition of SHIP, CORE_OFF or a restart limit Read the state with ReadPowerState() and ReadChargerStatus() ChargerFault The charger reports a fault Read ReadChargerStatus() ; RestartCharger() after the cause is gone VerifyFailed A register read back differently, or a read that is not stable or reads all ones Retry once; if it repeats, suspect a noisy line, a reset or another master DeviceReset A register the driver changed is back at its start-up value: the chip reset EnsureInitialized() and Configure() , see Troubleshooting Timeout DVS-done did not rise Check the load and the rail's enable; the step may be slow under a heavy load NoDevice Nothing acknowledged the address Power, SDA, SCL, the address ( Troubleshooting ) Bus , DeviceIdMismatch A bus fault; another chip Troubleshooting Unsupported An optional hook is missing Add GpioSet() or GpioGet() to your port Shut down ¶ There is no Deinitialize() : the chip is a supply, and the driver never switches it off. To stop using it, drop the object. Use RequestStandby() , EnterShip() or EnterCoreOff() to change the chip's own state.

docs.text: How to use the driver task by task. Every call returns pf1550::Result<T> : check it before you use value . Datasheet sections this page relies on From NXP Semiconductors PF1550 7: SWx output voltage setting and DVS-done: 6.2.5 Output voltage setting in SWx, p. 28 LDO1 and LDO3: 7.2 LDO1 and LDO3 detailed description, p. 35 LDO load switch mode: 7.2.7 LDOy load switch mode, p. 38 Charger operating modes: 8.1 Operating modes and behavioral description, p. 43 Charger input source detection: 8.2 Charger input source detection, p. 45 Charger state diagram: 8.4 Charger state diagram, p. 46 Charger faults and restart: 8.9 Fault states, p. 64 Charger watchdog: 8.9.2 Watchdog timer state, p. 65 PWRON: 9.1 PWRON, p. 68 STANDBY pin: 9.2 STANDBY, p. 69 RESETBMCU: 9.3 RESETBMCU, p. 69 INTB and the interrupt registers: 9.4 INTB, p. 70 ONKEY: 9.6 ONKEY, p. 71 State machine and transitions: 10 PF1550 state machine, p. 72 System ON, OFF, SHIP and CORE_OFF: 10.2 System OFF states, p. 74 Regulator power-up sequencer: 10.6 Regulator power-up sequencer, p. 77 Regulator power-down sequencer: 10.7 Regulator power-down sequencer, p. 78 Device start-up timing and pre-programmed options: 11 Device start up, p. 78 Device ID, silicon revision and OTP flavour: 12.1 Specific PMIC Registers (Offset is 0x00), p. 80 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map .

docs.text: Group Calls Writes the chip Lifecycle EnsureInitialized() , IsInitialized() , GetConfig() , Configure() Configure() only Identity and state ReadVariant() , ReadPowerState() , ReadSnapshot() , SelfCheck() , CheckChargerAgainstLimits() no Charger ReadChargerStatus() , SetChargerMode() , RestartCharger() , ServiceChargerWatchdog() yes Rails ReadRail() , SetRailModes() , SetRailVoltage() , EnableLoadSwitch() yes, except ReadRail() Power states RequestStandby() , EnterShip() , EnterCoreOff() , CancelShutdownRequest() , ReadPowerDownSequence() , SetPowerDownSequence() yes, except the read Interrupts SetIrqMask() , ReadCategories() , ReadSense() , ServiceInterrupts() , GetLatchedEvents() , ClearLatchedEvents() , IntbAsserted() masks and clears only Bench ReadRegister() no, read only There is no raw register write. ReadRegister() reads one documented register for bench work and writes nothing. The settings are typed ( Config and its blocks), checked against the datasheet grids and your Limits , and every register written is read back ( Contract ). Dangerous calls need a token. EnterShip(ShipConfirm{}) , EnterCoreOff(CoreOffConfirm{}) and EnableLoadSwitch(rail, LoadSwitchConfirm{.input_mv = 1800}) take a struct that you write out, so the call site says what it does; the load switch token carries the input voltage of the LDO, which the driver checks against Limits . Time is yours: the driver has no timer. The one wait it makes is bounded and goes through DelayUs() .
docs.title: The shape of the API

docs.text: Start and configure pf1550 :: Error Start ( Pmic & pmic ) { if ( auto r = pmic . EnsureInitialized (); ! r ) { // validates, identifies, checks the charger as found return r . error ; } return pmic . Configure (). error ; // writes the blocks whose `apply` is true, charger last } EnsureInitialized() validates the stored Config , checks DEVICE_ID, checks your DVS declarations against Table 85 and reads the charger as found. It writes nothing, except that when AsFoundPolicy::MakeSafe is set and an unsafe charge is found on, one write that puts the charger in linear-only mode. A start-up that fails on an unsafe charger leaves the driver uninitialised, but SetChargerMode(Off) still works. Configure() writes every block whose apply flag is true, in this order: the rails (in Config::rail_order ), VSNVS, the coin cell, USBPHY, the LED, power control, the power-down order, the interrupt masks and, last, the charger. A block with apply = false is left as the chip holds it. The driver does not know the chip's OTP option. Read it with ReadVariant() and decide what your board needs: const auto v = pmic . ReadVariant (); // v.value.option is Option::A1 .. A9, A0 (not programmed) or Unknown; v.value.flavor_raw is always the raw byte.
docs.title: Initialise and configure

docs.text: The charger is parked before it is changed and is switched on only by the mode, written last. A configuration with charger.mode = ChargerMode::Charge writes the parameters in linear-only mode and enables charging at the end, unless the charger reports a fault ( ChargerFault : the parameters are written, charging is not enabled). Watch the charger pf1550 :: Error WatchCharger ( Pmic & pmic ) { const auto s = pmic . ReadChargerStatus (); if ( ! s ) { return s . error ; } if ( s . value . fault == pf1550 :: Fault :: TimerFault ) { return pmic . RestartCharger (). error ; // off, then on; at most three tries in a row } return pmic . ServiceChargerWatchdog (). error ; // every 16 s or less when the watchdog is on } ReadChargerStatus() makes four reads: VBUS_SNS, CHG_SNS, BATT_SNS and CHG_SNS again ( consistent says the two CHG_SNS reads agree). fault is classified: None , TimerFault , ThermistorSuspend , ThermalShutdown , BatteryOvervoltage , BatteryOvercurrent , WatchdogExpired , BatteryMissing or UnknownState . The reads are not atomic with each other (ambiguity C27). SetChargerMode(Off) and LinearOnly are allowed as soon as DEVICE_ID has passed, even after a failed start-up. Charge checks the charger's registers against Limits and the acknowledgements first, so a charge that was configured outside your limits by something else (a start-up option, another master) is refused with OutOfLimits or Unsafe . RestartCharger() leaves a latched fault state: off, verify, charge. Three attempts in a row without the charger reaching a charging state return Refused : find the cause (a cold or hot battery, a timer, a shorted cell). With watchdog.enable call ServiceChargerWatchdog() at least every 16 s. The datasheet reads 80 s or 32 s with 20 % accuracy; 16 s covers every reading. The call reads BATFET_CNFG until two reads agree and refuses with Unsafe if the battery overcurrent protection reads as off without allow_batfet_oc_off : a stuck line reads zero. Whether WDTCLR holds what is written is open (C58); the driver writes it as an edge either way. The input limit check does not need watchdog.enable : a cable removal puts VBUS_LIN_ILIM back to its OTP value (Table 163). With the charger in Charge (or LinearOnly, when the charger block is applied) ReadChargerStatus() , ServiceInterrupts() (when a charger interrupt is set) and ServiceChargerWatchdog() all read the limit. A limit that is not the configured one is written again once VBUSIN is valid (while it is invalid the field is held in reset and nothing is written; SelfCheck() reports input_limit_ok false). A limit above Limits that cannot be restored (the charger block is not applied) switches the charger off and returns OutOfLimits . A failed check returns its error and not the status: an application that needs the status regardless calls ReadSnapshot() , which reads it without the check. The check is not written over a chip that reset meanwhile ( DeviceReset ), and a charger interrupt that ServiceInterrupts() read owes the check until one has passed: a call that fails after the status byte was read (a later pass, the clear write), or a ClearLatchedEvents() in between, does not drop it, and the next call makes it again.
docs.title: Charge

docs.text: Change an LDO pf1550 :: Error Rails ( Pmic & pmic ) { if ( auto r = pmic . SetRailVoltage ( pf1550 :: Rail :: Ldo1 , pf1550 :: FromMillivolts ( 2800 )); ! r ) { return r . error ; // OutOfLimits when your Limits window does not allow it } return pmic . SetRailModes ( pf1550 :: Rail :: Ldo1 , { true , true , false , false }). error ; } Every rail needs a window in Limits::rail[...] ; SetRailVoltage() and SetRailModes() return OutOfLimits for a rail without one or a voltage outside it. SW1 and SW2: the run voltage can be written only when you declared Dvs::Enabled in BuckConfig::dvs ; otherwise ReadOnlyRail . The standby and sleep voltages are set in Configure() through standby_uv and sleep_uv . After a change of the run voltage of an enabled rail the call waits for the DVS-done flag (at most 256 us) and returns Timeout if it does not rise. SW3's voltage is read only (ambiguity C2): SetRailVoltage(Rail::Sw3, ...) returns ReadOnlyRail . SetRailModes() sets EN, STBY_EN, OMODE and LPWR. Low-power mode ( low_power ) needs ack.load_below_10ma : the datasheet specifies it for loads up to 10 mA. EnableLoadSwitch(Rail::Ldo1 or Ldo3, LoadSwitchConfirm{.input_mv}) is irreversible. It turns an LDO into a switch: the output is the input voltage, with no current limit, and it cannot be undone until the next power cycle (LS_EN 1 to 0 is not allowed). input_mv is the voltage of the rail that feeds the LDO; it must lie inside the rail's Limits window, and the rail must not be in low-power mode ( Refused ). An enable ( SetRailModes() , or a block in Configure() ) first reads the voltage registers it brings into effect and checks them against Limits ( OutOfLimits ): a rail never comes on at a voltage the load does not tolerate. Standby and sleep need run ( InvalidArgument otherwise): EN gates both (Table 42). ReadRail() reports the enables, the load-switch flag and the programmed run voltage, decoded in the DVS mode the part has (Table 85 for A1 to A3, else your declaration).
docs.title: Rails

docs.text: ReadPowerState() decodes STATE_INFO: Wait , Run , Standby , Sleep , RegsDisable , or Unknown (SHIP and CORE_OFF have no I2C-visible state because the chip is not powered, ambiguity C36). RequestStandby(bool) drives the STANDBY pin through your GpioSet() ; Unsupported without it. EnterShip() and EnterCoreOff() are guarded: Ship mode pf1550 :: Error ShipMode ( Pmic & pmic ) { // Cuts every supply, VSNVS included; recovery is a charger or a battery attach. return pmic . EnterShip ( pf1550 :: ShipConfirm {}). error ; } EnterShip() returns Refused unless the chip is in Run, Standby or Sleep and VBUS reads invalid and below UVLO. Everything is cut, VSNVS included; recovery is a charger or a battery attach. The chip enters SHIP only with VBUSIN below 1.0 V, which the driver cannot measure (ambiguity C6): with VBUSIN between 1 V and UVLO it ends in REGS_DISABLE. EnterCoreOff() needs VBUS invalid and ONKEY not pushed, and arms GOTO_CORE_OFF: it takes effect at the next REGS_DISABLE, not at once. Both requests stay set in PWRCTRL3 until CancelShutdownRequest() clears them; call it when the request is no longer wanted. It is not refused after DEVICE_ID has passed. - ReadPowerDownSequence() and SetPowerDownSequence() read and write the seven *_PWRDN_SEQ registers. The order decides which supply drops first, and a wrong order can damage a processor: the write needs ack.power_down_order_reviewed . All zero bypasses the sequencer (section 10.7).
docs.title: Power states

docs.text: The power-up order is fixed by OTP and cannot be read back over I2C, so the driver reports it only for the pre-programmed options A1 to A9 that Table 85 lists. The helpers are constexpr and have no I/O: When does each rail turn on void Sequencer () { // Table 85: the start-up order of option A4 and when each rail turns on (microseconds). const auto profile = pf1550 :: StartupProfileOf ( pf1550 :: Option :: A4 ); if ( profile ) { const uint32_t ldo1_us = pf1550 :: PowerUpDelayUs ( profile . value , pf1550 :: Rail :: Ldo1 ); const uint32_t total_us = pf1550 :: PowerUpDurationUs ( profile . value ); std :: printf ( "LDO1 at %u us of %u us \n " , static_cast < unsigned > ( ldo1_us ), static_cast < unsigned > ( total_us )); } } Helper Gives StartupProfileOf(Option) The PWRUP_SEQ order of each rail, the slot length (500 us for A1, else 2000 us) and whether PWRON is edge sensitive (A8); InvalidArgument for A0 and Unknown PowerUpDelayUs() , PowerUpDurationUs() When a rail starts, and when the last one does, from the start of the first slot ResetReleaseDelayMs() , ColdStartToResetReleaseUs() RESETBMCU's delay from POR_DLY (code 1 is undefined) and the whole cold-start time to its release PowerDownDelayUs() , PowerDownDurationUs() , IsPowerDownBypassed() The power-down schedule of a PowerDownSequence : (highest - own) steps of 2 ms MirrorOf(profile) The power-down order the registers hold after reset (section 10.7: it mirrors the power-up order) Where the datasheet is silent the readings are C54 to C56 in Ambiguities .
docs.title: The sequencer

docs.text: Service INTB pf1550 :: Error OnIntb ( Pmic & pmic ) { const auto e = pmic . ServiceInterrupts (); // reads, copies out, clears if ( ! e ) { return e . error ; } if ( pf1550 :: Has ( e . value , pf1550 :: IrqSource :: Onkey3s )) { std :: printf ( "ONKEY held for 3 s \n " ); } return e . value . fault_class ? pf1550 :: Error :: DeviceFault : pf1550 :: Error :: Ok ; } 31 sources in 8 groups ( IrqGroup ): charger, SW low side, SW high side, SW DVS, LDO, temperature, ONKEY and miscellaneous. Has(events, IrqSource::X) tests one; IsFaultSource() and fault_class mark rail, die and system-overvoltage faults. A source is masked by default ( IrqMask{} masks all). Config::apply_irq_mask writes Config::irq_mask ; UnmaskOnly(std::array{...}) builds one from a list of sources. A masked source still sets its status bit, but does not drive INTB. ServiceInterrupts() copies each status byte out before it clears it (read-then-clear, at most three passes). Its result holds the bytes as read, plus the status bits that other calls read in the meantime (the driver latches them; GetLatchedEvents() shows them). With GpioGet() , INTB high, every source unmasked through SetIrqMask() and an empty latch it returns at once without a transfer; otherwise it reads the chip. PWRUP_I is reported like any other event (it is the standby wake-up flag, not a reset flag). ReadCategories() and ReadSense() are the live views (not latched): use them to poll without clearing. A DVS step that the driver waits for ( SetRailVoltage() , Configure() of SW1 or SW2) reads SW_INT_STAT2 and clears the awaited rail's DVS-done bit, so that rail's own event is consumed by the wait and never reaches the latch; the other rail's bit is kept in the latch. Use ReadSense(IrqGroup::SwDvs) to watch DVS done without consuming it.
docs.title: Interrupts

docs.text: ReadSnapshot() reads about 60 registers: identity, state, the charger, every sense register, the rails, the power-down order and POR_DLY . It is for logs and bring-up, not for a control loop. SelfCheck() answers four questions without writing: DEVICE_ID, state Run, every configured rail enabled as configured, and no latched fault. CheckChargerAgainstLimits() repeats the as-found check at any time.
docs.title: Diagnostics

docs.text: Explain an error const char * Explain ( pf1550 :: Error e ) { switch ( e ) { case pf1550 :: Error :: OutOfLimits : return "the value is valid for the chip but outside your Limits" ; case pf1550 :: Error :: Unsafe : return "a safety downgrade needs its Acknowledgements flag" ; case pf1550 :: Error :: Refused : return "a precondition of a dangerous call is not met" ; case pf1550 :: Error :: NoDevice : return "nothing acknowledged the address" ; default : return pf1550 :: ToString ( e ); } } Error Usually means Do NotInitialized EnsureInitialized() has not succeeded Call it, and check its error InvalidArgument Off the grid, reserved, or Limits unset Fix the value; nothing was sent OutOfLimits Valid for the chip, outside your Limits Fix the value or, if the hardware allows it, the limit Unsafe A downgrade without its acknowledgement Set the flag in Config::ack only if you mean it ReadOnlyRail SW3, or a buck not declared DVS Declare Dvs::Enabled if the OTP says so Refused A precondition of SHIP, CORE_OFF or a restart limit Read the state with ReadPowerState() and ReadChargerStatus() ChargerFault The charger reports a fault Read ReadChargerStatus() ; RestartCharger() after the cause is gone VerifyFailed A register read back differently, or a read that is not stable or reads all ones Retry once; if it repeats, suspect a noisy line, a reset or another master DeviceReset A register the driver changed is back at its start-up value: the chip reset EnsureInitialized() and Configure() , see Troubleshooting Timeout DVS-done did not rise Check the load and the rail's enable; the step may be slow under a heavy load NoDevice Nothing acknowledged the address Power, SDA, SCL, the address ( Troubleshooting ) Bus , DeviceIdMismatch A bus fault; another chip Troubleshooting Unsupported An optional hook is missing Add GpioSet() or GpioGet() to your port
docs.title: Handle errors

docs.text: There is no Deinitialize() : the chip is a supply, and the driver never switches it off. To stop using it, drop the object. Use RequestStandby() , EnterShip() or EnterCoreOff() to change the chip's own state.

docs.text: Architecture ¶ How the driver is built: three layers, one of them yours, and what happens in each when you change a setting. Datasheet sections this page relies on From NXP Semiconductors PF1550 7: I2C address, clock and register framing: 9.7 Control interface I2C block description, p. 71 I2C operation: single-register transfers: 9.7.2 I2C operation, p. 72 State machine and transitions: 10 PF1550 state machine, p. 72 Register map and access types: 12 Register map, p. 80 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources Top to bottom, each arrow is a call. Your application calls one object, whose public calls are listed from the umbrella header in inc/. The core turns each call into register reads and writes and hands them to the port contract (the CRTP base in inc/*_interface.hpp), which forwards them, at compile time, to the hooks of the port class you write; your port moves the bytes on the bus. The notes on the right say which layers stay the same on every MCU and which one you write. A library without a port contract has only the first two layers. Drawn from: inc/pf1550.hpp public calls ; inc/pf1550_i2c_interface.hpp I2cInterface ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . Layers ¶ Layer Files Owns Core inc/pf1550.hpp , src/pf1550.ipp Lifecycle, the typed calls, the guards, the read-back, the bounded waits, errors Configuration inc/pf1550_config.hpp , inc/pf1550_codec.hpp Limits , Acknowledgements , every block of Config , Validate() ; the datasheet grids as constexpr codecs Plans inc/pf1550_plan.hpp A block turned into a list of {register, mask, value} writes, as pure constexpr functions Types and registers inc/pf1550_types.hpp , inc/pf1550_registers.hpp Error , Result<T> , the enumerations; the register map with each register's access type Interrupts inc/pf1550_irq.hpp The 31 sources: where each lives, the categories, fault classification Sequencer inc/pf1550_sequencer.hpp The start-up options of Table 85 and the power-up and power-down timing, as constexpr data Port contract inc/pf1550_i2c_interface.hpp The CRTP base, CtrlPin , GpioSignal , I2cFailure , the I2cPort concept, the register framing Platform port Your class Bus bring-up and byte transfers, the delay, optionally STANDBY, INTB, the failure report and logging Kconfig layer inc/pf1550_kconfig.hpp Optional: the limits from ESP-IDF menuconfig One call through the layers ¶ sequenceDiagram participant App as Your code participant Core as PF1550<Port> participant Port as Your port App->>Core: SetRailVoltage(Ldo1, 2.8 V) Note over Core: grid code, Limits window, rail declared Core->>Port: WriteRead(read LDO1_VOLT) Port-->>Core: true, byte Note over Core: read-modify-write, IsWritable() Core->>Port: Write(LDO1_VOLT, new byte) Core->>Port: WriteRead(read LDO1_VOLT) Port-->>Core: true, byte Note over Core: equal? else VerifyFailed Core-->>App: Result<void>{Ok} A write is always a read, a masked change, a write and a read. Configure() is the same, applied to the plan of each block, with the charger last: a plan is a short list of {register, mask, value} entries that a test can check without a bus. Design choices ¶ No raw write. A byte reaches the chip only through one private function that refuses a register the datasheet does not document as writable. The public API is typed: enumerations, grids and codecs, so a value is on the datasheet's table before it becomes a register field. Limits first. The application states what its cell, supply and loads tolerate; the driver refuses what exceeds it ( OutOfLimits ) and what lowers a protection without an acknowledgement ( Unsafe ). Plans, not branches. Each block is a pure function to a list of writes. The code that applies them is one loop, so the guards and the read-back are in one place and the complexity stays low. Charger parked. The charger is set to "linear only" before its parameters change and its mode is written last, because the datasheet does not say whether a parameter change is glitch-free (ambiguities C16 and C49). CRTP, not virtual functions. The port is a template parameter constrained by the I2cPort concept, so every call is resolved at compile time and a missing hook is a compile error that names it. Optional hooks by named concepts. GpioSet , GpioGet , GetLastFailure and Log are detected with C++20 concepts in one place. A hook that is declared with the wrong signature is a compile error; one that is absent changes the call's result ( Unsupported ), never silently skips a step. DelayUs() is required. No I/O in the constructor. Construction cannot fail, so the driver can be a static or a member of a handler. One error type. Result<T> carries a value and an Error ; nothing throws and nothing returns a bare bool . No heap, no exceptions, no RTTI, no std::function , no printf . The driver is a header-only template with no mutable static state. docs.text: Changelog ¶ What changed in each release of the driver. Entries under Breaking need source changes in code that used the affected API. [Unreleased] ¶ Added ¶ First version of the PF1550 driver (NXP PF1550 PMIC, I2C): typed, limit-checked and read-back configuration of the charger, the three buck regulators, the three LDOs, VREFDDR, VSNVS, the coin cell charger, the USBPHY LDO and the charger LED; the state machine, SHIP and CORE_OFF behind confirmation tokens; the power-down order behind an acknowledgement; the interrupt groups with clear-after-copy; and the power-up and power-down sequencer as constexpr data for the pre-programmed options A1 to A9. Mandatory Limits and Acknowledgements ; no public raw register write. A host-test model of the chip, a fuzz target, compile-fail tests, a host example and ESP-IDF examples (configure and charge, interrupts and the charger watchdog). Not verified on hardware. Ninth review: a CHG_INT byte read by ReadRegister() also owes the input limit check (the flag is raised where every status byte is noted, so the next ServiceInterrupts() restores the limit; tests/test_round10.cpp ); the fuzz target drops its last exemption (a raw CHG_INT read) and owes the check for every charger byte the latch shows; the round-9 sweeps take their bound from a clean run of the same call; a corpus input walks charging, a cable removal with its interrupt, a failure at the second-pass INT_CATEGORY read, ClearLatchedEvents() and a clean service, so the corpus replay finds a lost pending check; contract and testing pages list the INTB shortcut's pending-check condition and every fuzz promise. Eighth review: a charger interrupt read by a ServiceInterrupts() call that then failed (a later pass, the clear write) owes the input limit check, so the next successful call restores a limit that went back to its OTP value, with or without ClearLatchedEvents() between; tests/test_round9.cpp fails each transfer of the call in turn and pins the five untested guards (mask write failure, latch kept after an error, failed switch-off is Bus , ClearLatchedEvents() empties the latch, a failed VBUS_SNS read is an error); the fuzz target calls ClearLatchedEvents() and no longer exempts a failed service from the limit invariant. Fuzz finding after the seventh review: the reset-seen invariant armed bits the driver had not changed (a rail mode bit left alone is no sentinel); it now arms only the changed bits (all mode bits for a switch-off), documented and pinned by tests/test_round8.cpp ; the input is in the corpus. Seventh review: the idle shortcut of ServiceInterrupts() is not taken while an input limit check is pending (a ClearLatchedEvents() between a failed and the next call no longer drops it); the ServiceInterrupts() header says "no source masked"; the VBUS operating range follows Table 5 (UVLO rising 3.8 to 4.2 V); the unseen-reset behaviour of the status and interrupt paths is documented; the fuzz target asserts the input limit invariant after ReadChargerStatus() and ServiceInterrupts() with its own VBUS_SNS decode, and no limit write in a call that returns DeviceReset ; its invariants ignore a line that was stuck during the call. Sixth review: the input limit restore of ReadChargerStatus() and ServiceInterrupts() looks for a chip reset first ( DeviceReset , nothing written); a failed check in ServiceInterrupts() stays pending until it passes; the (void) casts of results in the tests are static_cast<void> ; the remaining comparisons under && and || in the examples and compile-fail tests are parenthesised; ambiguity C60 (Table 163 default 400 mA against OTP 1500 mA). Fifth review: the input limit check after a cable removal also runs from ReadChargerStatus() and ServiceInterrupts() (on a charger interrupt), so it does not need watchdog.enable , and from ServiceChargerWatchdog() before the BATFET_CNFG checks; while VBUSIN is invalid the limit field is held in reset and the restore waits for a valid supply (no VerifyFailed on every call); a configured limit is kept with LinearOnly too; a DEVICE_ID line stuck at 0x00 is a Bus error and does not take the switch-off away; tests for a limit inside Limits that is not the configured one, for a refused charge start with an unacknowledged protection off and for single reads; the error-name test covers every enumerator. Fourth review: with the charger in Charge, ServiceChargerWatchdog() reads the input limit a cable removal reverts and writes the configured one again, or switches the charger off with OutOfLimits ; SelfCheck() reports input_limit_ok ; a refused charge start leaves the charger off; DEVICE_ID is read twice before another device is assumed; the fuzz target injects cable removals; comparisons under && and || are parenthesised; the examples show the DeviceReset recovery. Third review: a cable removal ( VBUS_LIN_ILIM reverts, Table 163) is not reported as a chip reset ( VbusRemoved() in the model); a switch-off is sent even after a re-start that failed on a bus error; the register transfer buffers are members of the driver object; the shutdown gates read twice; argument errors send nothing; a rail the driver switched off is remembered as off; Configure() looks for a reset before the charger block; the fuzz target checks that a reset of the chip is seen by SelfCheck() . Safety fixes from the independent review, each with a model mode and a test: a read that is written back must be stable (two reads agree, no all-ones) and every typed write is compared over the whole byte; ServiceChargerWatchdog() refuses when BATFET_CNFG reads with the overcurrent protection off; status bits read by any call are kept in a latch and reported by ServiceInterrupts() ( GetLatchedEvents() , ClearLatchedEvents() ); a rail is enabled only at a held voltage inside its Limits window; the DVS declaration is checked against Table 85 ( Acknowledgements::dvs_on_unlisted_part for other parts); an unsafe charger found at start-up can be switched off ( SetChargerMode(Off) , CheckChargerAgainstLimits() work once DEVICE_ID has passed); CancelShutdownRequest() clears GOTO_SHIP and GOTO_CORE_OFF, and the CORE_OFF documentation now says it is armed, not immediate; LoadSwitchConfirm{.input_mv} carries the LDO's input voltage and is checked against Limits ; a chip reset in the session is detected (a changed register reads at its start-up value again; PWRUP_I is not a reset flag, C59) and reported as Error::DeviceReset ; switching off is never refused for a reset, a failed start or an unreadable register; DISBATFET found at start-up is reported. PowerConfig writes its unguarded fields only with their own flags ( write_standby , write_debounce , write_regscp , write_low_sys_warn ); BatfetConfig::oc_without_vbus defaults to true and false needs allow_batfet_oc_off ; standby or sleep without run is InvalidArgument . The coverage matrix (1090 rows) is in the repository as docs/coverage-matrix.csv with a generated page and a check ( tools/coverage_matrix.py , CTest pf1550_coverage_matrix ). Ambiguities C57 and C58 added. The fuzz target also checks that no write newly switches off a protection (BATFET_OC, the fast-charge timer, the thermistor, DISBATFET), that guarded power fields change only with their acknowledgements, that a rail enabled by a write held a voltage inside its window, and it runs with read corruption.
