docs.text: Configuration ¶ Every setting the driver writes lives in one pf1550::Config . The constructor stores it, EnsureInitialized() checks it ( Validate() ), and Configure() writes the blocks you marked apply . Datasheet sections this page relies on From NXP Semiconductors PF1550 7: Electrical limits and supply ranges: 5.3 Electrical characteristics, p. 12 SW1 and SW2: DVS and non-DVS operation: 6.2.2 SWx DVS and non-DVS operation, p. 26 SWx output voltage setting and DVS-done: 6.2.5 Output voltage setting in SWx, p. 28 SW3: 6.3 SW3 detailed description, p. 31 LDO1 and LDO3: 7.2 LDO1 and LDO3 detailed description, p. 35 LDO low-power mode: 7.2.5 LDOy low-power mode operation, p. 37 LDO2: 7.3 LDO2 detailed description, p. 38 VREFDDR: 7.4 VREFDDR reference, p. 40 VSNVS and the coin cell charger: 7.5 VSNVS LDO/switch, p. 41 Charger operating modes: 8.1 Operating modes and behavioral description, p. 43 Charging profile: 8.5 Charging profile, p. 46 Power path: VSYS regulation and input current limit: 8.7 Power path features, p. 55 Thermal regulation and foldback: 8.8 Thermal, p. 57 Input voltage regulation (DPM): 8.8.3 Input voltage regulation mode, p. 59 JEITA thermal control: 8.8.4 JEITA thermal control, p. 62 Battery overcurrent limit and BATFET: 8.9.6 Battery overcurrent limit, p. 66 Charger LED: 8.10 LED indicator, p. 67 Register OTP bitmap: 12.5 Register OTP bitmap, p. 128 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Limits ¶ Limits is the application's own description of what its cell, supply and loads tolerate. It has no defaults : an unset limit is rejected ( InvalidArgument ) before anything is sent, and a value outside a limit is OutOfLimits . The numbers come from the data sheets of your cell, supply and processor, not from the PF1550's. Field Range Meaning cell_max_mv 3500 to 4440 Highest charge voltage the cell allows cell_max_charge_ma 100 to 1000 Highest charge current the cell allows input_max_ma 10 to 1500 What the supply on VBUS can deliver coin_cell_max_mv 0 or up to 3300 Highest voltage the coin cell tolerates; 0 when there is no coin cell. A charge voltage above 1.8 V needs 3300 or more (ambiguity C40) rail[Rail] {min_mv, max_mv, max_load_ma} The window the rail's load tolerates. All zero means "not set": the rail is never enabled or set ( OutOfLimits ) SingleCellLimits() returns 4.2 V, 500 mA and 1 A for a typical single cell: a starting point whose numbers you must check, with no rail windows. Acknowledgements ¶ A safety downgrade is accepted only with its flag in Config::ack . Every flag defaults to false, so the downgrade is visible in your source and in review. A downgrade without its flag is Unsafe , with nothing sent. Flag Needed for allow_untimed_charge FastChargeTimer::Disabled battery_has_own_ntc_protection Thermistor::Ignore allow_batfet_closed_on_fault Any FaultPolicy::keep_closed_on_* allow_batfet_oc_off BatfetOc::Disabled , oc_keeps_closed or oc_without_vbus = false (BOVRC_NOVBUS = 0 disables the protection without VBUS, Table 161); also the watchdog service, when BATFET_CNFG reads with the protection off eoc_accuracy_accepted Termination current 5 mA or 10 mA (wide accuracy band) load_below_10ma RailModes::low_power (specified for loads up to 10 mA) coin_cell_is_rechargeable CoinCell::charge_enable hard_reset_paths PowerConfig::write_reset_paths (ONKEY, PWRON, restart and global reset paths) undervoltage_threshold PowerConfig::write_uvdet allow_batfet_off BatfetConfig::disable (DISBATFET: the battery path is forced off) power_down_order_reviewed PowerDownConfig::apply and SetPowerDownSequence() dvs_on_unlisted_part Dvs::Enabled on a part that Table 85 does not list (A0, A4 to A9, unknown flavour), where the driver cannot cross-check the declaration (C57) Blocks ¶ A block with apply = false is left as the chip holds it. Fields with a unit carry it in the name. The defaults are the chip's reset values, except where the table says the driver chose another. Charger ( ChargerConfig ) ¶ Field Default Range Register mode LinearOnly Off , LinearOnly , Charge CHG_OPER, written last charge_voltage_mv none (set it) 3500 to 4440 in 20 mV steps, at most cell_max_mv CHGCV charge_current_ma none (set it) 100 to 1000 in 50 mA steps, at most cell_max_charge_ma CHG_CC termination_ma 50 5, 10, 20, 30, 50 IEOC input_limit_ma none (set it) 21 documented values, at most input_max_ma VBUS_LIN_ILIM vsys_min 4.3 V SystemMin VSYSMIN (the reset value is 3.5 V) restart 150 mV Restart CHG_RESTART fast_timer 4 h FastChargeTimer FCHGTIME ( Disabled needs an acknowledgement) eoc_timer , precharge_timer 10 min, 30 min EocTimer , PrechargeTimer EOCTIME, TPRECHG thermistor Suspend Suspend , Ignore , ... THM_CNFG thermal_reg , thermal_foldback 95 C, on ThermalRegTemp REGTEMP, TEMP_FB_EN (the reset value is off) watchdog off, 80 s WatchdogConfig{enable, time} WDTEN, WD_TIME; service within 16 s batfet reset values, oc_without_vbus true BatfetConfig BATFET_OC, BOVRC_DISBATFET, BOVRC_NOVBUS (true keeps the overcurrent protection on without VBUS; the reset value is off), DISBATFET, FAULT_BATFET_CNFG vbus reset values VbusOptions DPM, DPM stop, debounces, wake-up delay, VBUS2SYS jeita reset values JeitaConfig THM_COLD, THM_HOT, THM_COOL, THM_WARM, CV_ADJ, CC_ADJ interrupts off ChargerInterrupts CHG_INT_CNFG A value off the grid is InvalidArgument ; one outside Limits is OutOfLimits . Codes the datasheet marks reserved are not encodable. The charge voltage grid has no code for 3.50 V alone: codes 0 to 8 all mean 3.50 V and 56 to 63 all mean 4.44 V, so the driver encodes codes 8 to 55 (ambiguity C53). Bucks ( BuckConfig : sw1 , sw2 , sw3 ) ¶ Field Default Meaning dvs Disabled You declare the OTP DVS mode ( OTP_SWx_DVS_SEL ); the chip cannot report it (C1). The voltage fields need Enabled run_uv , standby_uv , sleep_uv 0 keeps The three DVS voltages, on the datasheet grid and inside the rail's window; SW1 and SW2 only modes all off RailModes{run, standby, sleep, low_power} : EN, STBY_EN, OMODE, LPWR current_limit 1.0 A SwCurrentLimit dvs_speed 2 us DvsSpeed , SW1 and SW2 fpwm , fpwm_in_dvs off Forced PWM output_discharge true Discharge resistor when the rail is disabled LDOs, VREFDDR, VSNVS, coin cell, USBPHY, LED ¶ Block Fields ldo1 , ldo2 , ldo3 volt (0 keeps), modes ; LDO1 and LDO3 can become load switches only through EnableLoadSwitch() vrefddr modes vsnvs local_bandgap_disable (LIBGDIS) coin charge_enable (needs coin_cell_is_rechargeable ), voltage_mv 1800 to 3300 in 100 mV steps (above 1800 needs Limits::coin_cell_max_mv of at least 3300; residual risk: Table 111 prints code 7 as 3.3 V with 100 mV steps, which does not agree, so the codes above 0 are not proven safe for a 3.6 V cell, C40) usbphy enable , voltage , active_discharge led enable , duty_32nds 0 to 32, ramp , frequency , mode , software_override Power control ( PowerConfig , PowerDownConfig ) ¶ Field Meaning write_standby , standby_delay , standby_inverted STANDBYDLY and STANDBYINV, written only with write_standby : STANDBYINV flips Run and Standby with the pin at a steady level, so change it only together with your port's GpioSet() write_debounce , pwron_debounce , onkey_debounce PWRONDBNC, ONKEYDBNC (codes 00 and 01 are identical, C41), written only with write_debounce write_regscp , ldo_off_on_current_limit REGSCPEN, written only with write_regscp write_low_sys_warn , low_sys_warn LOW_SYS_WARN threshold, written only with write_low_sys_warn write_reset_paths and the four fields after it PWRONRSTEN, RESTARTEN, ONKEY_RST_EN, TGRESET: need hard_reset_paths write_uvdet , uvdet UVDET: needs undervoltage_threshold ; a wrong value resets the system power_down.sequence Order 0 to 7 per rail; needs power_down_order_reviewed Interrupts and the rest ¶ Field Default Meaning apply_irq_mask , irq_mask off, all masked Writes the masks; 1 masks a source rail_order SW1, SW2, SW3, LDO1, LDO2, LDO3, VREFDDR The order in which Configure() writes the rails: put a buck before the LDO it feeds as_found_policy Report What EnsureInitialized() does with an unsafe charger found on: Report returns the error and writes nothing, MakeSafe switches it to linear-only Example ¶ A board pf1550 :: Config MyBoard () { pf1550 :: Config c {}; // What the hardware tolerates: no defaults, Validate() rejects an unset limit. c . limits . cell_max_mv = 4200 ; c . limits . cell_max_charge_ma = 500 ; c . limits . input_max_ma = 1000 ; c . limits . rail [ static_cast < std :: size_t > ( pf1550 :: Rail :: Sw1 )] = { 1000 , 1200 , 800 }; // mV, mV, mA c . limits . rail [ static_cast < std :: size_t > ( pf1550 :: Rail :: Ldo1 )] = { 1700 , 3300 , 100 }; // The charger: voltage, current and input limit have no default. c . charger . apply = true ; c . charger . mode = pf1550 :: ChargerMode :: Charge ; c . charger . charge_voltage_mv = 4200 ; c . charger . charge_current_ma = 300 ; c . charger . input_limit_ma = 500 ; // SW1 runs from the OTP value of your option; you declare that its voltage is a DVS table. c . sw1 = { true , pf1550 :: Dvs :: Enabled , pf1550 :: FromMillivolts ( 1100 ), {}, {}, { true , true , false , false }}; c . ldo1 = { true , pf1550 :: FromMillivolts ( 1800 ), { true , true , false , false }}; return c ; } Validation ¶ pf1550::Validate(config) checks a configuration without touching the chip, and EnsureInitialized() calls it before any I/O. It is constexpr , so a fixed board configuration can be checked at compile time: Check at compile time static_assert ( pf1550 :: Validate ( pf1550 :: Config {}) == pf1550 :: Error :: InvalidArgument , "no Limits: rejected" ); static_assert ( pf1550 :: Validate ( pf1550 :: Config {. limits = pf1550 :: SingleCellLimits ()}) == pf1550 :: Error :: Ok , "a 4.2 V cell, 500 mA, 1 A supply" ); It returns InvalidArgument for unset limits, a value off the grid, a reserved code, a value that is not an enumerator or a rail order that is not a permutation; OutOfLimits for a valid value outside Limits ; ReadOnlyRail for a buck voltage on SW3 or on a buck not declared Dvs::Enabled ; InvalidArgument also for standby or sleep enabled without run (EN gates both); Unsafe for a downgrade without its acknowledgement. The first failure is returned, in this order: limits, rail order, charger, rails, peripherals, power. Kconfig ¶ Under ESP-IDF, idf.py menuconfig shows PF1550 power management IC when the driver is a component of the project ( Installation ); the menu is _config/Kconfig . The options are only the limits and the as-found policy, and they reach the code only through inc/pf1550_kconfig.hpp , never through a driver signature: Option Default Range Sets PF1550_CELL_MAX_MV 4200 3500 to 4440 Limits::cell_max_mv PF1550_CELL_MAX_CHARGE_MA 500 100 to 1000 Limits::cell_max_charge_ma PF1550_INPUT_MAX_MA 1000 10 to 1500 Limits::input_max_ma PF1550_AS_FOUND_MAKE_SAFE n AsFoundPolicy::MakeSafe Limits from menuconfig pf1550 :: Config FromMenuconfig () { pf1550 :: Config c = pf1550 :: KconfigDefaults (); // the cell and supply limits, blocks unapplied c . charger . apply = true ; c . charger . charge_voltage_mv = c . limits . cell_max_mv ; c . charger . charge_current_ma = 300 ; c . charger . input_limit_ma = 500 ; return c ; } The defaults are a starting point for a 4.2 V cell: set them from your cell's data sheet before the first run.

docs.text: A board pf1550 :: Config MyBoard () { pf1550 :: Config c {}; // What the hardware tolerates: no defaults, Validate() rejects an unset limit. c . limits . cell_max_mv = 4200 ; c . limits . cell_max_charge_ma = 500 ; c . limits . input_max_ma = 1000 ; c . limits . rail [ static_cast < std :: size_t > ( pf1550 :: Rail :: Sw1 )] = { 1000 , 1200 , 800 }; // mV, mV, mA c . limits . rail [ static_cast < std :: size_t > ( pf1550 :: Rail :: Ldo1 )] = { 1700 , 3300 , 100 }; // The charger: voltage, current and input limit have no default. c . charger . apply = true ; c . charger . mode = pf1550 :: ChargerMode :: Charge ; c . charger . charge_voltage_mv = 4200 ; c . charger . charge_current_ma = 300 ; c . charger . input_limit_ma = 500 ; // SW1 runs from the OTP value of your option; you declare that its voltage is a DVS table. c . sw1 = { true , pf1550 :: Dvs :: Enabled , pf1550 :: FromMillivolts ( 1100 ), {}, {}, { true , true , false , false }}; c . ldo1 = { true , pf1550 :: FromMillivolts ( 1800 ), { true , true , false , false }}; return c ; }

docs.text: pf1550::Validate(config) checks a configuration without touching the chip, and EnsureInitialized() calls it before any I/O. It is constexpr , so a fixed board configuration can be checked at compile time: Check at compile time static_assert ( pf1550 :: Validate ( pf1550 :: Config {}) == pf1550 :: Error :: InvalidArgument , "no Limits: rejected" ); static_assert ( pf1550 :: Validate ( pf1550 :: Config {. limits = pf1550 :: SingleCellLimits ()}) == pf1550 :: Error :: Ok , "a 4.2 V cell, 500 mA, 1 A supply" ); It returns InvalidArgument for unset limits, a value off the grid, a reserved code, a value that is not an enumerator or a rail order that is not a permutation; OutOfLimits for a valid value outside Limits ; ReadOnlyRail for a buck voltage on SW3 or on a buck not declared Dvs::Enabled ; InvalidArgument also for standby or sleep enabled without run (EN gates both); Unsafe for a downgrade without its acknowledgement. The first failure is returned, in this order: limits, rail order, charger, rails, peripherals, power.

docs.text: Under ESP-IDF, idf.py menuconfig shows PF1550 power management IC when the driver is a component of the project ( Installation ); the menu is _config/Kconfig . The options are only the limits and the as-found policy, and they reach the code only through inc/pf1550_kconfig.hpp , never through a driver signature: Option Default Range Sets PF1550_CELL_MAX_MV 4200 3500 to 4440 Limits::cell_max_mv PF1550_CELL_MAX_CHARGE_MA 500 100 to 1000 Limits::cell_max_charge_ma PF1550_INPUT_MAX_MA 1000 10 to 1500 Limits::input_max_ma PF1550_AS_FOUND_MAKE_SAFE n AsFoundPolicy::MakeSafe Limits from menuconfig pf1550 :: Config FromMenuconfig () { pf1550 :: Config c = pf1550 :: KconfigDefaults (); // the cell and supply limits, blocks unapplied c . charger . apply = true ; c . charger . charge_voltage_mv = c . limits . cell_max_mv ; c . charger . charge_current_ma = 300 ; c . charger . input_limit_ma = 500 ; return c ; } The defaults are a starting point for a 4.2 V cell: set them from your cell's data sheet before the first run.

docs.text: Contract ¶ What the PF1550 driver promises, what it needs, and the rules a caller follows. The driver inherits the Kokeb Labs driver contract ; this page states only what is specific to it. A change to anything here is a breaking change, listed under Breaking in the changelog . Datasheet sections this page relies on From NXP Semiconductors PF1550 7: Electrical limits and supply ranges: 5.3 Electrical characteristics, p. 12 SW1 and SW2: DVS and non-DVS operation: 6.2.2 SWx DVS and non-DVS operation, p. 26 LDO load switch mode: 7.2.7 LDOy load switch mode, p. 38 Battery overcurrent limit and BATFET: 8.9.6 Battery overcurrent limit, p. 66 System ON, OFF, SHIP and CORE_OFF: 10.2 System OFF states, p. 74 State transition conditions (Table 83): 10.5 State diagram and transition conditions, p. 76 Regulator power-down sequencer: 10.7 Regulator power-down sequencer, p. 78 Register map and access types: 12 Register map, p. 80 Register OTP bitmap: 12.5 Register OTP bitmap, p. 128 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Promises ¶ Lifecycle ¶ The constructor is noexcept , stores the configuration, does no I/O and cannot fail. EnsureInitialized() is the only way to start the driver. It validates the stored Config first ( InvalidArgument , OutOfLimits or Unsafe , nothing sent), brings the bus up, checks that DEVICE_ID reads 0x7C , checks your DVS declaration against Table 85 and checks the charger as found against your Limits . Once it has succeeded, later calls return Ok with no I/O. After a failure the driver stays uninitialised and the call can be repeated. Every call that touches the chip returns Error::NotInitialized before EnsureInitialized() succeeds, and sends nothing. No call starts or resets the chip as a side effect. Some calls work as soon as DEVICE_ID has passed, even when start-up then failed (an unsafe charger found on, for example): SetChargerMode(Off) or LinearOnly , SetRailModes() with every state off, the off step of RestartCharger() , CheckChargerAgainstLimits() and CancelShutdownRequest() . An unsafe charger can always be switched off. The chip can reset in the middle of a session (UVDET, a watchdog, a REGS_DISABLE pulse): it then starts in its OTP state, which may be a charger on with no timer, and the driver's Configure() is gone. The datasheet defines no reset flag (PWRUP_I is the STANDBY or SLEEP to RUN completion flag, Table 108, ambiguity C59), so the driver remembers the bits it changed and verified (at most four registers, the newest ones) and every call that switches something on or changes the chip reads those registers first (up to four extra reads); a difference twice in a row returns DeviceReset , writes nothing, and leaves the driver uninitialised until EnsureInitialized() and Configure() run again. SelfCheck() reports it the same way, and Configure() looks once more before it writes the charger block. A rail the driver switched off is remembered as off, so a reset that brings it back on is seen. A reset that leaves every bit the driver wrote at its start-up value is not seen, and does no harm; a reset in the middle of a call that writes several registers is seen by the next check, not by the writes in between. EnsureInitialized() on a driver that already is initialised returns at once and checks nothing: to look for a reset, call SelfCheck() . A cable removal is not a chip reset. VBUS_LIN_ILIM goes back to its OTP value when VBUSIN becomes invalid (Table 163, reset condition CHGPOK_RSTB, ambiguity C14), so it is never kept as evidence of a reset. The charger keeps its mode through a cable removal, so a charger that was charging goes on charging at the OTP limit until the next watchdog service: ServiceChargerWatchdog() reads the limit while the charger is in Charge, writes the configured one again when the charger block is applied (a warning is logged), and otherwise switches the charger off and returns OutOfLimits when the limit is above Limits.input_max_ma . SelfCheck() reports it as input_limit_ok . Service the watchdog at least every kWatchdogServiceMaxS seconds (16 s) to bound that window. A charge start refused with OutOfLimits or Unsafe leaves the charger off, also when it was found charging. A switch-off is never refused for a reset report or a failed re-start: SetRailModes() with every state off, SetChargerMode(Off or LinearOnly) , the off step of RestartCharger() and CancelShutdownRequest() need only a chip that answered with DEVICE_ID once (a bus error during a re-start does not take that back; another device answering does), and the write goes out even when the register cannot be read. The bits other than the switched ones then go out as zero: for CHG_OPER that is also WDTEN and an acknowledged DISBATFET, which the application sets again with Configure() . Only the switched bits are read back. InvalidArgument , ReadOnlyRail , Unsupported and the OutOfLimits or Unsafe that come from the arguments and the Config mean nothing was sent: they are decided before the reset check reads the chip. An OutOfLimits , Unsafe or Refused found by reading the chip (the as-found charger, a held voltage, a protection that reads off, the shutdown preconditions) comes after reads and before any write. Every port failure propagates: a transfer that returns false is Error::Bus , or Error::NoDevice when your port's GetLastFailure() says the address was not acknowledged. Safety ¶ There is no public raw register write. Every write is a typed call, goes through one private function that refuses any register the datasheet does not document as writable (read-only, status, key and undocumented registers), and is a read-modify-write that preserves reserved bits. The typed setter reaches configuration and mask registers only; status registers are cleared by the interrupt service and PWRCTRL3 is written by the shutdown calls. A value that is written back must be one the chip holds. The read of a read-modify-write is repeated until two reads agree (at most three), and a register other than an interrupt mask that reads all ones is VerifyFailed (a floating or stuck line). ServiceChargerWatchdog() refuses with Unsafe when BATFET_CNFG reads with the battery overcurrent protection off and allow_batfet_oc_off is not set: a stuck line reads zero. Limits has no defaults. A configuration without cell_max_mv , cell_max_charge_ma and input_max_ma is rejected. A rail the application did not give a window is never enabled or set by the driver ( OutOfLimits ). The charge voltage and current written never exceed Limits , and the input current limit never exceeds input_max_ma . Limits::coin_cell_max_mv must be at least 3300 mV for a coin cell charge voltage above 1.8 V (ambiguity C40). A safety downgrade is accepted only with its acknowledgement in Config::ack , so that it is visible in the application's source: no fast-charge timer, thermistor ignored, BATFET kept closed on a fault, battery overcurrent protection reduced or off, 5 mA or 10 mA termination, a low-power mode on a rail, a coin cell charger, a changed hard-reset path, a changed undervoltage threshold, DISBATFET, a changed power-down order. Every typed write is read back, and the whole byte is compared (bits the chip changes by itself, such as the watchdog clear bits, are excluded). A register that reads back differently is VerifyFailed ; the value is not trusted. A rail enable that the chip clears on its own after an overcurrent ( REGSCPEN , Table 136) reads back differently and reports VerifyFailed as well. This deviates from the handbook's per-call Verify argument (see Deviations). Not read back: the watchdog service's WDTCLR bits, the interrupt status clears and PWRCTRL3. A rail is enabled only at a voltage inside its Limits window: the voltage registers that the enable brings into effect and the call does not write are read and decoded first ( OutOfLimits ). The same applies to Configure() . The charger is parked before it is changed: Configure() writes CHG_OPER to "linear regulator only", then every charger parameter, then the watchdog and BATFET bits, and the mode last. Charging is enabled only by a charger block in Configure() that asks for Charge , or by SetChargerMode(Charge) . SetChargerMode(Charge) re-checks the charger's registers against Limits and refuses with ChargerFault while the charger reports a fault. The as-found check runs in EnsureInitialized() . With AsFoundPolicy::Report (the default) an unsafe charger found on leaves the driver uninitialised and writes nothing; with MakeSafe the driver writes CHG_OPER to "linear only" and checks again. A charger found off or in linear-only mode is not checked. EnterShip() needs a ShipConfirm , state Run, Standby or Sleep, VBUS not valid and below UVLO. EnterCoreOff() needs a CoreOffConfirm , VBUS not valid and ONKEY not pushed. Otherwise Refused , with nothing written. The driver cannot measure VBUSIN below 1.0 V, which SHIP needs (ambiguity C6): with VBUS between 1 V and UVLO the chip ends in REGS_DISABLE instead of SHIP. GOTO_SHIP and GOTO_CORE_OFF are plain read/write bits that stay set (Table 138). A request is armed, not a command that is over once it is sent: GOTO_CORE_OFF acts only when the chip is in REGS_DISABLE (VBUS invalid, ONKEY high; Table 83 footnotes 8 and 9, section 10.2.2), so in Run, Standby or Sleep nothing happens and the bit stays armed until the next REGS_DISABLE. A request that did not end in SHIP can fire at a later charger attach or battery cycle. CancelShutdownRequest() clears both bits and reads PWRCTRL3 back; it is not refused after DEVICE_ID has passed. Each request writes one command bit and clears the other, so a bad read cannot turn SHIP into CORE_OFF. EnableLoadSwitch() is irreversible: the chip cannot leave the mode until the next power cycle (LS_EN 1 to 0 is not allowed, Tables 130 and 134), and the output is the input rail voltage with no current limit (7.2.7). It needs a LoadSwitchConfirm{.input_mv} with the input voltage of the LDO, which must lie inside the rail's Limits window, and refuses ( Refused ) while the rail is in low-power mode. SetPowerDownSequence() and the PowerDownConfig block need ack.power_down_order_reviewed . Reserved bits and reserved codes are never written; a code the datasheet marks reserved is not encodable ( InvalidArgument ). Timing and waits ¶ Every wait is bounded. The only wait is the DVS-done wait of SetRailVoltage() : at most kDvsWaitMaxUs (256 us), polled in 16 us steps through DelayUs() , and only when the run voltage changes and the rail is enabled ( Timeout otherwise). The charger watchdog, when WatchdogConfig::enable is set, must be serviced by the application every kWatchdogServiceMaxS (16 s) or less (the datasheet reads 80 s or 32 s with 20 % accuracy, ambiguity C8). The driver has no timer: ServiceChargerWatchdog() is yours to call. The input limit check after a cable removal does not depend on it: ReadChargerStatus() and ServiceInterrupts() (on a charger interrupt, also one read by a call that failed afterwards) run it too, with the charger in Charge (or LinearOnly, when the charger block is applied). While VBUSIN is invalid the limit field is held in reset: the restore waits for a valid supply and SelfCheck() reports input_limit_ok false meanwhile. After an unseen chip reset the status and interrupt paths write nothing and return DeviceReset : a charger that the reset left at an OTP limit above Limits stays in that OTP state until EnsureInitialized() , whose as-found check handles it (a switch-off by SetChargerMode(Off) is never refused). RestartCharger() makes at most kMaxChargerRestarts (3) attempts in a row without the charger reaching a charging state and then returns Refused . Interrupts ¶ ServiceInterrupts() reads INT_CATEGORY, copies each flagged group's status byte out, then writes the same bits back to clear them, at most three passes. A bit that sets between the copy and the clear is not lost: it is read in the next pass or the next call. The event bytes are returned as read, before the clear. The status registers are "Read or Write 1 to clear" (Tables 90 to 110, C3): a read by another call may clear a bit. The driver keeps every status bit that any of its calls reads ( ReadRegister() , SelfCheck() , the reset check, the DVS wait) in a latch; ServiceInterrupts() reports them with the events and empties the latch, and GetLatchedEvents() and ClearLatchedEvents() give access without bus traffic. With GpioGet() and INTB not asserted the call returns an empty result without bus traffic, but only when the latch is empty, SetIrqMask() left no source masked (a masked source does not pull INTB, and its status bit still sets) and no input limit check is pending (one is owed from the moment a charger status byte was read, by the service or by ReadRegister() , until a service has passed it). With the power-up mask (every source masked) the call reads the chip. Residual risk: a status bit is one flag. An event of the same source that occurs again between the status read and the clear write is merged with the first and reported once, in either reading of C3 (write-one-to-clear, clear-on-read, or both). An event of another source in the same group is not lost: only the bits that were read are written back. Not verified on hardware. The DVS-done wait of SetRailVoltage() polls and clears SW_INT_STAT2; the interrupt service clears the same register. Use one of them for the DVS-done bits of a rail: a call to ServiceInterrupts() from another task during a voltage step can swallow the event, and the wait then returns Timeout . The status bytes of the charger and the PMIC groups are not atomic with each other; ChargerStatus::consistent says whether CHG_SNS read twice with equal values (ambiguity C27). Data ¶ Config{} holds no limits and is rejected; SingleCellLimits() gives a starting point (4.2 V, 500 mA, 1 A) that the application must check against its own cell and supply. ReadVariant() never returns an error for an option the datasheet does not list: it reports the raw bytes and Option::Unknown . A0 parts ("not programmed") are supported by reading only: the driver assumes nothing about their start-up values, StartupProfileOf(Option::A0) is InvalidArgument , and the as-found check still applies. SILICON_REV is stored raw; the driver makes no decision on it (ambiguity C22). The DVS mode of SW1 and SW2 is an OTP fuse ( OTP_SWx_DVS_SEL ) that no register reports (ambiguity C1). You declare it in BuckConfig::dvs . The driver writes a buck's voltage registers only when you declared Dvs::Enabled , and returns ReadOnlyRail otherwise. SW3 is never written. For the listed options A1 to A3 the declaration is checked against Table 85 in EnsureInitialized() : a block you configure with the wrong mode is Refused (a rail written in the wrong mode ends at 3.3 V, Table 31), and the part's mode decides how an unconfigured buck is read. For a part Table 85 does not list, DVS needs ack.dvs_on_unlisted_part ( Unsafe without it, ambiguity C57). The OTP image is not read back: the public datasheet documents no read window (ambiguity C5). docs/datasheet.md says so under "What is not covered". Depends on ¶ Dependency Version Why A C++20 compiler GCC 10, Clang 13 or later Concepts constrain the port CMake 3.16 or later Generates pf1550_version.h Your port The bus, within the bus requirements; the delay (the DVS-done wait needs DelayUs() ); optionally STANDBY, INTB, a failure report and logging ( Porting ) Nothing else: no RTOS, no SDK, no other repository of the org. Threading ¶ The driver is not thread-safe and takes no lock. Use each driver object from one task at a time, or guard every call on it with one mutex; the layer that owns the driver owns that lock, and the bus lock when several chips share a bus. Nothing may run in an ISR: every call can block for a bus transfer or a delay. Separate objects share no state. Errors ¶ pf1550::Error inside pf1550::Result<T> . Values 0 to 9 are the shared base set; the chip-specific values start at 16 and each one is returned by some call ( tests/test_errors.cpp checks it). Error Value Returned when Ok 0 The call succeeded NotInitialized 1 EnsureInitialized() has not succeeded InvalidArgument 2 A value is off the datasheet grid, reserved, not an enumerator, or Limits is unset; nothing was sent Bus 3 A port hook returned false Timeout 4 The DVS-done flag did not rise within kDvsWaitMaxUs DeviceIdMismatch 5 DEVICE_ID is not 0x7C Crc 6 Not returned: I2C transfers carry no CRC Busy 7 Not returned: the chip has no busy state DeviceFault 8 Not returned: faults are reported as ChargerFault or in the status types Unsupported 9 The optional port hook the call needs is absent ( GpioSet() , GpioGet() ) OutOfLimits 16 A valid value outside your Limits , or a charger found on outside them; nothing was sent ReadOnlyRail 17 SW3, or SW1 or SW2 not declared Dvs::Enabled : its voltage is not written Unsafe 18 A safety downgrade without its acknowledgement; nothing was sent Refused 19 A precondition of a dangerous call is not met (state, VBUS, ONKEY, restart count) ChargerFault 20 The charger reports a fault state; charging is not enabled VerifyFailed 21 A register read back differently from what was just written NoDevice 22 Nothing acknowledged the address (needs the optional GetLastFailure() hook) DeviceReset 23 A register the driver changed reads at its start-up value again: the chip reset in the session; run EnsureInitialized() and Configure() Three base values ( Crc , Busy , DeviceFault ) are never returned: the chip's bus has no CRC, no busy state and no fault bit that the driver reports as an error. They stay in the enumeration for the shared base set. The API guide says what to do about each. Memory ¶ No heap, no exceptions, no RTTI, no std::function , no std::string , no printf and no static mutable state. A driver object holds a reference to the port, the Config (296 bytes), the status latch (eight bytes) and a few flags: 336 bytes on a 64-bit host. The largest stack objects are the diagnostic Snapshot (120 bytes) and the Config copies you make yourself. A transfer moves one data byte, so no buffer is larger than two bytes. Platform ¶ Platform-free: the same code runs on any target with a C++20 compiler, including the host tests. The ESP-IDF port in examples/esp32 is an example, not part of the driver. Deviations from the standard ¶ Rule Deviation Why KB-ARCH-041 (read-back only on request, per call) Every typed write is followed by a read-back and VerifyFailed is returned on a mismatch The chip controls a battery charger and the supply of a processor. The datasheet describes registers whose writes are loaded from OTP, reset by events that the I2C interface does not report and "write-1-to-set" (ambiguity C4). A write that did not take effect cannot be allowed to pass silently. The cost is one extra single-register transfer per register written. Optional hooks by requires None: the driver detects them with named concepts as the standard asks MISRA C++:2023 rules 6.9.2, 15.1.4 and 0.0.2 (CodeQL advisories, expected) Rule 6.9.2: the parameter of the _u8 , _u16 and _u32 literal operators is unsigned long long , the type the language fixes. Rule 15.1.4: the PF1550 constructor leaves the register bus without a default member initialiser (it holds a reference). Rule 0.0.2: cppcheck's knownConditionTrueFalse on a port whose hooks are constants Not code defects; no waiver is recorded (see below) Deviations are proposed here, not waived: .kokeb/handbook.yml carries no waiver and docs/deviations.yml does not exist for this driver. The maintainer decides whether the read-back becomes a waiver (the entry would name rule KB-ARCH-041, this page as the place, and the one-transfer cost) or a per-call argument. No typed write targets a write-1-to-clear or self-clearing bit: the typed setter refuses status and command registers. Open questions ¶ Ambiguities lists every place where the datasheet is silent or inconsistent (C1 to C59), the reading the driver takes, and the model knob that runs the other reading. Nothing in the driver has been verified on hardware; each bench step that would settle a row is named in Datasheet map .

An unsafe charger can always be switched off. The chip can reset in the middle of a session (UVDET, a watchdog, a REGS_DISABLE pulse): it then starts in its OTP state, which may be a charger on with no timer, and the driver's Configure() is gone. The datasheet defines no reset flag (PWRUP_I is the STANDBY or SLEEP to RUN completion flag, Table 108, ambiguity C59), so the driver remembers the bits it changed and verified (at most four registers, the newest ones) and every call that switches something on or changes the chip reads those registers first (up to four extra reads); a difference twice in a row returns DeviceReset , writes nothing, and leaves the driver uninitialised until EnsureInitialized() and Configure() run again. SelfCheck() reports it the same way, and Configure() looks once more before it writes the charger block. A rail the driver switched off is remembered as off, so a reset that brings it back on is seen. A reset that leaves every bit the driver wrote at its start-up value is not seen, and does no harm; a reset in the middle of a call that writes several registers is seen by the next check, not by the writes in between. EnsureInitialized() on a driver that already is initialised returns at once and checks nothing: to look for a reset, call SelfCheck() . A cable removal is not a chip reset. VBUS_LIN_ILIM goes back to its OTP value when VBUSIN becomes invalid (Table 163, reset condition CHGPOK_RSTB, ambiguity C14), so it is never kept as evidence of a reset. The charger keeps its mode through a cable removal, so a charger that was charging goes on charging at the OTP limit until the next watchdog service: ServiceChargerWatchdog() reads the limit while the charger is in Charge, writes the configured one again when the charger block is applied (a warning is logged), and otherwise switches the charger off and returns OutOfLimits when the limit is above Limits.input_max_ma . SelfCheck() reports it as input_limit_ok . Service the watchdog at least every kWatchdogServiceMaxS seconds (16 s) to bound that window. A charge start refused with OutOfLimits or Unsafe leaves the charger off, also when it was found charging. A switch-off is never refused for a reset report or a failed re-start: SetRailModes() with every state off, SetChargerMode(Off or LinearOnly) , the off step of RestartCharger() and CancelShutdownRequest() need only a chip that answered with DEVICE_ID once (a bus error during a re-start does not take that back; another device answering does), and the write goes out even when the register cannot be read. The bits other than the switched ones then go out as zero: for CHG_OPER that is also WDTEN and an acknowledged DISBATFET, which the application sets again with Configure() . Only the switched bits are read back. InvalidArgument , ReadOnlyRail , Unsupported and the OutOfLimits or Unsafe that come from the arguments and the Config mean nothing was sent: they are decided before the reset check reads the chip. An OutOfLimits , Unsafe or Refused found by reading the chip (the as-found charger, a held voltage, a protection that reads off, the shutdown preconditions) comes after reads and before any write. Every port failure propagates: a transfer that returns false is Error::Bus , or Error::NoDevice when your port's GetLastFailure() says the address was not acknowledged.
docs.title: Lifecycle

docs.text: There is no public raw register write. Every write is a typed call, goes through one private function that refuses any register the datasheet does not document as writable (read-only, status, key and undocumented registers), and is a read-modify-write that preserves reserved bits. The typed setter reaches configuration and mask registers only; status registers are cleared by the interrupt service and PWRCTRL3 is written by the shutdown calls. A value that is written back must be one the chip holds. The read of a read-modify-write is repeated until two reads agree (at most three), and a register other than an interrupt mask that reads all ones is VerifyFailed (a floating or stuck line). ServiceChargerWatchdog() refuses with Unsafe when BATFET_CNFG reads with the battery overcurrent protection off and allow_batfet_oc_off is not set: a stuck line reads zero. Limits has no defaults. A configuration without cell_max_mv , cell_max_charge_ma and input_max_ma is rejected. A rail the application did not give a window is never enabled or set by the driver ( OutOfLimits ). The charge voltage and current written never exceed Limits , and the input current limit never exceeds input_max_ma . Limits::coin_cell_max_mv must be at least 3300 mV for a coin cell charge voltage above 1.8 V (ambiguity C40). A safety downgrade is accepted only with its acknowledgement in Config::ack , so that it is visible in the application's source: no fast-charge timer, thermistor ignored, BATFET kept closed on a fault, battery overcurrent protection reduced or off, 5 mA or 10 mA termination, a low-power mode on a rail, a coin cell charger, a changed hard-reset path, a changed undervoltage threshold, DISBATFET, a changed power-down order. Every typed write is read back, and the whole byte is compared (bits the chip changes by itself, such as the watchdog clear bits, are excluded). A register that reads back differently is VerifyFailed ; the value is not trusted. A rail enable that the chip clears on its own after an overcurrent ( REGSCPEN , Table 136) reads back differently and reports VerifyFailed as well. This deviates from the handbook's per-call Verify argument (see Deviations). Not read back: the watchdog service's WDTCLR bits, the interrupt status clears and PWRCTRL3. A rail is enabled only at a voltage inside its Limits window: the voltage registers that the enable brings into effect and the call does not write are read and decoded first ( OutOfLimits ). The same applies to Configure() . The charger is parked before it is changed: Configure() writes CHG_OPER to "linear regulator only", then every charger parameter, then the watchdog and BATFET bits, and the mode last. Charging is enabled only by a charger block in Configure() that asks for Charge , or by SetChargerMode(Charge) . SetChargerMode(Charge) re-checks the charger's registers against Limits and refuses with ChargerFault while the charger reports a fault. The as-found check runs in EnsureInitialized() . With AsFoundPolicy::Report (the default) an unsafe charger found on leaves the driver uninitialised and writes nothing; with MakeSafe the driver writes CHG_OPER to "linear only" and checks again. A charger found off or in linear-only mode is not checked. EnterShip() needs a ShipConfirm , state Run, Standby or Sleep, VBUS not valid and below UVLO. EnterCoreOff() needs a CoreOffConfirm , VBUS not valid and ONKEY not pushed. Otherwise Refused , with nothing written. The driver cannot measure VBUSIN below 1.0 V, which SHIP needs (ambiguity C6): with VBUS between 1 V and UVLO the chip ends in REGS_DISABLE instead of SHIP. GOTO_SHIP and GOTO_CORE_OFF are plain read/write bits that stay set (Table 138). A request is armed, not a command that is over once it is sent: GOTO_CORE_OFF acts only when the chip is in REGS_DISABLE (VBUS invalid, ONKEY high; Table 83 footnotes 8 and 9, section 10.2.2), so in Run, Standby or Sleep nothing happens and the bit stays armed until the next REGS_DISABLE. A request that did not end in SHIP can fire at a later charger attach or battery cycle. CancelShutdownRequest() clears both bits and reads PWRCTRL3 back; it is not refused after DEVICE_ID has passed. Each request writes one command bit and clears the other, so a bad read cannot turn SHIP into CORE_OFF. EnableLoadSwitch() is irreversible: the chip cannot leave the mode until the next power cycle (LS_EN 1 to 0 is not allowed, Tables 130 and 134), and the output is the input rail voltage with no current limit (7.2.7). It needs a LoadSwitchConfirm{.input_mv} with the input voltage of the LDO, which must lie inside the rail's Limits window, and refuses ( Refused ) while the rail is in low-power mode. SetPowerDownSequence() and the PowerDownConfig block need ack.power_down_order_reviewed . Reserved bits and reserved codes are never written; a code the datasheet marks reserved is not encodable ( InvalidArgument ).
docs.title: Safety

docs.text: Every wait is bounded. The only wait is the DVS-done wait of SetRailVoltage() : at most kDvsWaitMaxUs (256 us), polled in 16 us steps through DelayUs() , and only when the run voltage changes and the rail is enabled ( Timeout otherwise). The charger watchdog, when WatchdogConfig::enable is set, must be serviced by the application every kWatchdogServiceMaxS (16 s) or less (the datasheet reads 80 s or 32 s with 20 % accuracy, ambiguity C8). The driver has no timer: ServiceChargerWatchdog() is yours to call. The input limit check after a cable removal does not depend on it: ReadChargerStatus() and ServiceInterrupts() (on a charger interrupt, also one read by a call that failed afterwards) run it too, with the charger in Charge (or LinearOnly, when the charger block is applied). While VBUSIN is invalid the limit field is held in reset: the restore waits for a valid supply and SelfCheck() reports input_limit_ok false meanwhile. After an unseen chip reset the status and interrupt paths write nothing and return DeviceReset : a charger that the reset left at an OTP limit above Limits stays in that OTP state until EnsureInitialized() , whose as-found check handles it (a switch-off by SetChargerMode(Off) is never refused). RestartCharger() makes at most kMaxChargerRestarts (3) attempts in a row without the charger reaching a charging state and then returns Refused .
docs.title: Timing and waits

docs.text: ServiceInterrupts() reads INT_CATEGORY, copies each flagged group's status byte out, then writes the same bits back to clear them, at most three passes. A bit that sets between the copy and the clear is not lost: it is read in the next pass or the next call. The event bytes are returned as read, before the clear. The status registers are "Read or Write 1 to clear" (Tables 90 to 110, C3): a read by another call may clear a bit. The driver keeps every status bit that any of its calls reads ( ReadRegister() , SelfCheck() , the reset check, the DVS wait) in a latch; ServiceInterrupts() reports them with the events and empties the latch, and GetLatchedEvents() and ClearLatchedEvents() give access without bus traffic. With GpioGet() and INTB not asserted the call returns an empty result without bus traffic, but only when the latch is empty, SetIrqMask() left no source masked (a masked source does not pull INTB, and its status bit still sets) and no input limit check is pending (one is owed from the moment a charger status byte was read, by the service or by ReadRegister() , until a service has passed it). With the power-up mask (every source masked) the call reads the chip. Residual risk: a status bit is one flag. An event of the same source that occurs again between the status read and the clear write is merged with the first and reported once, in either reading of C3 (write-one-to-clear, clear-on-read, or both). An event of another source in the same group is not lost: only the bits that were read are written back. Not verified on hardware. The DVS-done wait of SetRailVoltage() polls and clears SW_INT_STAT2; the interrupt service clears the same register. Use one of them for the DVS-done bits of a rail: a call to ServiceInterrupts() from another task during a voltage step can swallow the event, and the wait then returns Timeout . The status bytes of the charger and the PMIC groups are not atomic with each other; ChargerStatus::consistent says whether CHG_SNS read twice with equal values (ambiguity C27).
docs.title: Interrupts

docs.text: Config{} holds no limits and is rejected; SingleCellLimits() gives a starting point (4.2 V, 500 mA, 1 A) that the application must check against its own cell and supply. ReadVariant() never returns an error for an option the datasheet does not list: it reports the raw bytes and Option::Unknown . A0 parts ("not programmed") are supported by reading only: the driver assumes nothing about their start-up values, StartupProfileOf(Option::A0) is InvalidArgument , and the as-found check still applies. SILICON_REV is stored raw; the driver makes no decision on it (ambiguity C22). The DVS mode of SW1 and SW2 is an OTP fuse ( OTP_SWx_DVS_SEL ) that no register reports (ambiguity C1). You declare it in BuckConfig::dvs . The driver writes a buck's voltage registers only when you declared Dvs::Enabled , and returns ReadOnlyRail otherwise. SW3 is never written. For the listed options A1 to A3 the declaration is checked against Table 85 in EnsureInitialized() : a block you configure with the wrong mode is Refused (a rail written in the wrong mode ends at 3.3 V, Table 31), and the part's mode decides how an unconfigured buck is read. For a part Table 85 does not list, DVS needs ack.dvs_on_unlisted_part ( Unsafe without it, ambiguity C57). The OTP image is not read back: the public datasheet documents no read window (ambiguity C5). docs/datasheet.md says so under "What is not covered".

docs.text: The driver is not thread-safe and takes no lock. Use each driver object from one task at a time, or guard every call on it with one mutex; the layer that owns the driver owns that lock, and the bus lock when several chips share a bus. Nothing may run in an ISR: every call can block for a bus transfer or a delay. Separate objects share no state.
docs.title: Threading

docs.text: pf1550::Error inside pf1550::Result<T> . Values 0 to 9 are the shared base set; the chip-specific values start at 16 and each one is returned by some call ( tests/test_errors.cpp checks it). Error Value Returned when Ok 0 The call succeeded NotInitialized 1 EnsureInitialized() has not succeeded InvalidArgument 2 A value is off the datasheet grid, reserved, not an enumerator, or Limits is unset; nothing was sent Bus 3 A port hook returned false Timeout 4 The DVS-done flag did not rise within kDvsWaitMaxUs DeviceIdMismatch 5 DEVICE_ID is not 0x7C Crc 6 Not returned: I2C transfers carry no CRC Busy 7 Not returned: the chip has no busy state DeviceFault 8 Not returned: faults are reported as ChargerFault or in the status types Unsupported 9 The optional port hook the call needs is absent ( GpioSet() , GpioGet() ) OutOfLimits 16 A valid value outside your Limits , or a charger found on outside them; nothing was sent ReadOnlyRail 17 SW3, or SW1 or SW2 not declared Dvs::Enabled : its voltage is not written Unsafe 18 A safety downgrade without its acknowledgement; nothing was sent Refused 19 A precondition of a dangerous call is not met (state, VBUS, ONKEY, restart count) ChargerFault 20 The charger reports a fault state; charging is not enabled VerifyFailed 21 A register read back differently from what was just written NoDevice 22 Nothing acknowledged the address (needs the optional GetLastFailure() hook) DeviceReset 23 A register the driver changed reads at its start-up value again: the chip reset in the session; run EnsureInitialized() and Configure() Three base values ( Crc , Busy , DeviceFault ) are never returned: the chip's bus has no CRC, no busy state and no fault bit that the driver reports as an error. They stay in the enumeration for the shared base set. The API guide says what to do about each.
docs.title: Errors

docs.text: No heap, no exceptions, no RTTI, no std::function , no std::string , no printf and no static mutable state. A driver object holds a reference to the port, the Config (296 bytes), the status latch (eight bytes) and a few flags: 336 bytes on a 64-bit host. The largest stack objects are the diagnostic Snapshot (120 bytes) and the Config copies you make yourself. A transfer moves one data byte, so no buffer is larger than two bytes.
docs.title: Memory

docs.text: Platform-free: the same code runs on any target with a C++20 compiler, including the host tests. The ESP-IDF port in examples/esp32 is an example, not part of the driver.
docs.title: Platform

docs.text: Rule Deviation Why KB-ARCH-041 (read-back only on request, per call) Every typed write is followed by a read-back and VerifyFailed is returned on a mismatch The chip controls a battery charger and the supply of a processor. The datasheet describes registers whose writes are loaded from OTP, reset by events that the I2C interface does not report and "write-1-to-set" (ambiguity C4). A write that did not take effect cannot be allowed to pass silently. The cost is one extra single-register transfer per register written. Optional hooks by requires None: the driver detects them with named concepts as the standard asks MISRA C++:2023 rules 6.9.2, 15.1.4 and 0.0.2 (CodeQL advisories, expected) Rule 6.9.2: the parameter of the _u8 , _u16 and _u32 literal operators is unsigned long long , the type the language fixes. Rule 15.1.4: the PF1550 constructor leaves the register bus without a default member initialiser (it holds a reference). Rule 0.0.2: cppcheck's knownConditionTrueFalse on a port whose hooks are constants Not code defects; no waiver is recorded (see below) Deviations are proposed here, not waived: .kokeb/handbook.yml carries no waiver and docs/deviations.yml does not exist for this driver. The maintainer decides whether the read-back becomes a waiver (the entry would name rule KB-ARCH-041, this page as the place, and the one-transfer cost) or a per-call argument. No typed write targets a write-1-to-clear or self-clearing bit: the typed setter refuses status and command registers.

docs.title: Coverage matrix

docs.text: One row per datasheet (Rev. 7) parameter: register, bit field, interrupt source, state, electrical or timing parameter, pin, OTP value. Each row names the driver API, the model behaviour and the test suite with its files; the status says whether the behaviour is covered. The source is coverage-matrix.csv ; this page is generated from it by python3 tools/coverage_matrix.py write , and python3 tools/coverage_matrix.py check verifies the totals against Coverage . Totals: 1090 rows; OK 729, INFO 360, TODO 1. The test suite ids ( T01 to T28 ) name groups of tests; the files column lists where they live. A suite is not one test case: it is the set of cases in those files that exercise the behaviour. Suite Test cases Files T01 every I/O call returns NotInitialized before EnsureInitialized tests/test_config.cpp; inc/pf1550_codec.hpp (static_assert) T02 EnsureInitialized reads DEVICE_ID and the charger, writes nothing; Config without Limits is rejected before any I/O; failures of the bus and of identity T03 Limits are mandatory and must be sane; charger values are on the grid and inside Limits tests/test_configure.cpp T04 every safety downgrade needs its acknowledgement; rails: windows, grids, DVS declaration, low power tests/test_model.cpp; tests/test_configure.cpp T05 coin cell, power block and power-down order need their acknowledgements T06 an enumerator that is not one is rejected; codecs: grids, anchors and reserved codes T07 charger block writes the documented bytes and leaves the mode last; charger mode LinearOnly leaves charging off; reserved bits and fields the block does not own are preserved; JEITA, DPM, debounce and interrupt options reach their fields tests/test_charger.cpp T08 the BATFET fault policy and DISBATFET are written when acknowledged tests/test_charger.cpp T09 buck and LDO blocks: enables, voltages, current limit, forced PWM; the rail order is the caller's; a DVS step waits for the done flag, and an unchanged voltage does not; a DVS step that never finishes times out tests/test_charger.cpp T10 coin cell, USB PHY, LED and power control reach their registers; reset paths and UVDET are written only when asked and acknowledged tests/test_configure.cpp; tests/test_charger.cpp T11 Configure refuses charging while the charger reports a fault tests/test_charger.cpp T12 a write that does not hold is reported; a bus error in the middle of Configure stops it tests/test_irq.cpp T13 no write reaches a register that is not meant to be written tests/test_power.cpp T14 the interrupt mask block writes defined bits and preserves reserved ones tests/test_rails.cpp; tests/test_configure.cpp T15 charger states decode from CHG_SNS, including reserved codes; battery states, flags and the watchdog readings; VBUS flags decode tests/test_irq.cpp; tests/test_rails.cpp T16 a charger state that changes between the two reads is flagged tests/test_power.cpp; tests/test_rails.cpp; tests/test_review.cpp T17 charging is enabled only with limits-covered registers and no fault; charging with unsafe registers is refused whatever Configure did; SetChargerMode(Charge) checks the as-found values and reports them tests/test_configure.cpp T18 RestartCharger cycles off and on, a bounded number of times tests/test_power.cpp; tests/test_configure.cpp T19 the watchdog is serviced by WDTCLR = 1 and the other bits are kept; as found: option A1 starts the charger with no fast-charge timer; as found: MakeSafe writes CHG_OPER = linear only and verifies; as found: acknowledgements make an untimed charger acceptable; as found: limits below the OTP charge values give OutOfLimits; as found: a charger that is off is not checked; as found: each OTP option reads back its identity tests/test_lifecycle.cpp; tests/test_model.cpp T20 ReadRail decodes each option's start-up values; load switch and low power flags read back T21 SetRailVoltage: LDOs, DVS bucks and the refusals; a rail with no window is never driven tests/test_lifecycle.cpp; tests/test_errors.cpp T22 variants: A0 and unlisted flavour bytes are reported, never an error; SILICON_REV and the address code are reported raw; power states decode and a reserved code is Unknown; SetRailModes writes the four enables and checks the low power rule tests/test_irq.cpp T23 the load switch is one way and needs a window and a token T27 the STANDBY pin goes through the port, or the call is Unsupported

docs.text: Coverage ¶ How much of the PF1550 the driver implements, models and tests. The datasheet (Rev. 7) is covered feature by feature in a per-parameter matrix of 1090 rows; this page gives its totals and what each status means. Every row has a status: Status Meaning OK The API decision, the model's behaviour and a test are all present for the behaviour INFO An explicit decision that there is nothing to model or test beyond storage or documentation: an analog value, a bit the driver never programs, a reserved field TODO A gap: the datasheet does not support it, or the driver does not do it yet Totals: 1090 rows; OK 729, INFO 360, TODO 1; covered (OK + INFO) 1089 of 1090. Group Rows OK INFO TODO Registers (the 90 documented registers) 90 85 5 0 Bit fields 357 248 109 0 Interrupt sources 31 31 0 0 PMIC and charger states, transitions, status codes 42 42 0 0 Electrical characteristics and ratings (Tables 3 to 26, per parameter) 272 109 163 0 Start-up and power-down timing (Table 84) 10 5 5 0 Digital pin levels, debounce and polarity (Tables 73 to 82) 25 13 12 0 Pins (Table 2) 41 7 34 0 OTP start-up values (Table 85, per parameter) 46 46 0 0 OTP image registers (Table 176) 28 28 0 0 OTP image fields (Table 176) 102 75 26 1 Functional-chapter tables (Tables 27 to 72) 46 40 6 0 What changed since the first matrix ¶ The first matrix left 43 rows as TODO: the power-up and power-down sequencer and the start-up timing were not modelled, the power-down order registers were stored only, and the coin cell charge had no effect in the model. The datasheet defines behaviour for all of them, so they are now implemented, modelled and tested: Rows Now *_PWRDN_SEQ registers and fields (14) ReadPowerDownSequence() , SetPowerDownSequence() (acknowledgement), PowerDownDelayUs() ; the model mirrors the power-up order after reset (section 10.7) and runs the schedule OTP_*_PWRUP_SEQ , OTP_SEQ_CLK_SPEED and their image fields (16) StartupProfileOf(Option) for A1 to A9, from Table 85; the model's option table is its own copy Table 84 timing (10) kVsnvsTurnOnDelayUs , kSlotFastUs , kSlotSlowUs , kPowerDownStepUs , ColdStartToResetReleaseUs() ; the rise times and the user-determined delay tD2 are analog or the application's and are INFO rows COINCELL_CONTROL , COINCHEN (2) CoinCell , with the model charging LICELL to VCOIN while COINCHEN is set The one row left is the OTP image read-back window ( OF-RB ): the public datasheet does not document it, so the driver cannot read the fuses over I2C. Datasheet map says how to close it. Where the rows are ¶ The per-parameter matrix (register, bit field, interrupt source, state, electrical parameter, timing, pin, OTP value) names for each row the datasheet table and page, the driver API, the model behaviour, the test suite and the test files. It is in this repository as coverage-matrix.csv , with a generated page, Coverage matrix . python3 tools/coverage_matrix.py check (also a CTest, pf1550_coverage_matrix ) verifies that its totals equal the ones on this page, that every API name in it exists in inc/ or src/ , and that every test file it names exists. docs.text: Examples ¶ One folder per platform under examples/ , each with its own port, built by CI on every pull request. The driver itself has no platform code; Platforms lists what exists. Host ¶ examples/host/ runs the driver on any PC against a simulated PF1550, through the host port host_pf1550_port.hpp . No hardware: cmake -S examples/host -B build-example && cmake --build build-example && ./build-example/pf1550_host_example The host tests build it with warnings as errors and run it (CTest pf1550_host_example ). ESP32 ¶ ESP-IDF applications that run the driver on an ESP32-C6 DevKitC-1; the wiring is in the example folder's README and the port in esp32_pf1550_port.hpp . The project points EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS at the repository root, which is the driver's ESP-IDF component. The apps ¶ App What it shows Source CI pf1550_basic_example Start the PF1550, write the configuration, log the charger state and LDO1 once a second pf1550_basic_example.cpp yes pf1550_interrupt_example Charge with the charger watchdog serviced every 10 s and react to INTB events pf1550_interrupt_example.cpp yes Build and flash one (from examples/esp32 , ESP-IDF environment loaded): ./scripts/build_app.sh pf1550_basic_example Release ./scripts/flash_app.sh flash_monitor pf1550_basic_example Release Source of this table: examples/esp32/app_config.yml . docs.text: Hardware ¶ The PF1550's package, pins, bus settings and power, as the driver uses them. The driver reaches the chip through the I2C bus and two optional pins, STANDBY and INTB; everything else on the package is wired by the board, as the datasheet's example schematic shows (section 13.1, p. 133). Datasheet sections this page relies on From NXP Semiconductors PF1550 7: Pins and package: 4.2 Pin definitions, p. 8 I2C address, clock and register framing: 9.7 Control interface I2C block description, p. 71 Example schematic: 13.1 Example schematic, p. 133 Package outline: 14 Package outline, p. 139 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Package ¶ HVQFN-40, 5.0 mm x 5.0 mm with an exposed pad (data sheet section 14, p. 139). The exposed pad is ground. The body size is the only dimension the datasheet text gives; the pitch and the height are on its drawing and are not drawn here. Pins ¶ PF1550 pinout, HVQFN-40 Figure description and sources The PF1550 seen from the top, in its HVQFN-40 package. Pin 1 is marked by the dot; the numbers run counter-clockwise from it. Each pad is coloured by the pin's electrical type (legend below). Next to it is the pin's name and, in mono, the hook of the driver's port that drives or reads it; a pin without a hook is not used by the driver. The dashed square is the exposed pad. Drawn from: docs/hardware.yml ; inc/pf1550_i2c_interface.hpp . HVQFN-40, 40 pins and an exposed pad (4.1 Pinning, p. 7). The driver uses SDA and SCL through the port, STANDBY through GpioSet(CtrlPin::Standby, ...) and INTB through GpioGet(CtrlPin::Intb, ...) . It never touches the other pins: PWRON, ONKEY, WDI and RESETBMCU belong to the board and the state machine. The driver reads their effect (state, interrupts) and configures their debounce and polarity where the datasheet makes them registers. Blocks ¶ Inside the PF1550 Figure description and sources The PF1550's function blocks inside its outline. Arrows between blocks carry signals or data in the direction they point (both ways where they have two heads). The package pins stand on the left and right edges with their numbers, each wired to the block it reaches. Drawn from: docs/hardware.yml ; inc/pf1550_i2c_interface.hpp . The register map is split in two pages by address: the PMIC registers 0x00 to 0x6F and the charger registers 0x80 to 0x9F , both on the same I2C address. Control pins ¶ STANDBY is an input of the chip. RequestStandby(true) calls your GpioSet(CtrlPin::Standby, GpioSignal::ACTIVE) ; ACTIVE means "request STANDBY" and your port maps the polarity ( STANDBYINV = 0 is active high). The driver never writes STANDBYINV unless PowerConfig::apply is set: change the polarity only together with the port. Without the hook RequestStandby() returns Unsupported . INTB is an open-drain output, low when an unmasked interrupt is pending. With GpioGet() , ServiceInterrupts() returns an empty result without bus traffic while INTB is high. Without it, every call reads INT_CATEGORY . PWRON, ONKEY, WDI, RESETBMCU are not driver pins. PWRON level or edge sensitivity is an OTP option ( OTP_PWRON_CFG , option A8 is edge sensitive) and the driver cannot read it. Bus settings ¶ Setting Value Clock Up to 400 kHz ( kMaxClockHz ), fast mode Address 7-bit, 0x08 to 0x0F set by OTP ( kI2cAddress = 0x08 ); pass it to the constructor Write START, address + W, register, one data byte, STOP Read START, address + W, register, repeated START, address + R, one data byte, STOP Burst Not used: the datasheet does not describe auto-increment (ambiguity C48) I/O levels Set by VDDIO, 1.7 V to 3.3 V sequenceDiagram participant Host participant PF1550 Host->>PF1550: START, 0x08 + W, 0x00 (DEVICE_ID) Host->>PF1550: repeated START, 0x08 + R PF1550-->>Host: 0x7C Host->>PF1550: NACK, STOP An address that nothing acknowledges (no chip, no power, a wrong address) is reported as Error::NoDevice when your port has the optional GetLastFailure() hook; without it the driver cannot tell it from another bus fault and returns Bus . Power ¶ The PF1550 powers itself from VSYS and VBUSIN; the driver has no supply of its own to manage. The limits the driver needs from you describe what the cell and the loads tolerate ( Configuration ). Rail What the datasheet gives Driver VBUSIN VUVLO rising 3.8 V to 4.2 V (valid above it) up to OVLO rising 6.0 V to 7.0 V (Table 5; ambiguity C52) Status only ( VbusFlags ) VBATT Single Li-ion cell, charge voltage 3.5 V to 4.44 V Limits::cell_max_mv VDDIO 1.7 V to 3.3 V The port's concern SW1, SW2, SW3 Programmable bucks Limits::rail[...] LDO1 to LDO3, VREFDDR Programmable LDOs, fixed reference Limits::rail[...] LICELL Coin cell, charged to 1.8 V to 3.3 V Limits::coin_cell_max_mv Reference application circuit ¶ The datasheet's example schematic (section 13.1, p. 133) shows the power connections: the charger input, the battery, the three bucks with their inductors, the LDOs and their capacitors, the thermistor, the LED and the coin cell. It is not redrawn here. The figure below is only the control connections of a host, as the driver uses them; the resistor values are typical and marked as not confirmed. PF1550: Control connections to a host processor Figure description and sources A schematic. The MCU is on the left, each of its pins level with the chip pin it connects to; above each wire is the hook of the driver's port that drives or reads it. Supply pins point up to their supply and decoupling, ground pins down. Pins on the right carry the loads and the pins tied to a supply or ground; a cross marks a pin left open. A dot is a junction; wires that cross without a dot are not connected. Drawn from: docs/hardware.yml ; inc/pf1550_i2c_interface.hpp . Part Kind Value Connects Datasheet U2 Host - VIO: VIO, GND: GND, SDA: SDA, SCL: SCL, STBY: STANDBY, IRQ: INTB 13.1, p. 133 R1 resistor 2.2 kΩ (not confirmed: typical value for 400 kHz; size it for the bus) VIO, SDA 13.1, p. 133 R2 resistor 2.2 kΩ (not confirmed: typical value for 400 kHz; size it for the bus) VIO, SCL 13.1, p. 133 R3 resistor 10 kΩ (not confirmed: INTB is open drain; any value that suits the host input) VIO, INTB 13.1, p. 133 Export a circuit for a schematic or PCB tool: kokeb-docs hardware --kicad-netlist OUT.net --circuit typical . Silicon and options ¶ ReadVariant() returns DEVICE_ID, OTP_FLAVOR , SILICON_REV and the address code. The ten orderable options A0 to A9 differ in their OTP start-up values (Table 85): output voltages, the power-up order, the charger's start-up mode, the input current limit and whether DVS is enabled. The driver reports the option and the sequencer helpers model the power-up order of A1 to A9 ( API guide ). A0 parts are "not programmed, internal validation only" (Table 1 footnote). The OTP image itself is not readable over I2C in the public datasheet, so the driver cannot read the fuses back; it asks you for the two OTP facts it needs ( BuckConfig::dvs , the declared DVS mode) and reports the rest from the option byte. docs.text: STANDBY is an input of the chip. RequestStandby(true) calls your GpioSet(CtrlPin::Standby, GpioSignal::ACTIVE) ; ACTIVE means "request STANDBY" and your port maps the polarity ( STANDBYINV = 0 is active high). The driver never writes STANDBYINV unless PowerConfig::apply is set: change the polarity only together with the port. Without the hook RequestStandby() returns Unsupported . INTB is an open-drain output, low when an unmasked interrupt is pending. With GpioGet() , ServiceInterrupts() returns an empty result without bus traffic while INTB is high. Without it, every call reads INT_CATEGORY . PWRON, ONKEY, WDI, RESETBMCU are not driver pins. PWRON level or edge sensitivity is an OTP option ( OTP_PWRON_CFG , option A8 is edge sensitive) and the driver cannot read it.

docs.text: Installation ¶ Add the driver to a CMake project on any MCU or on your PC, or to an ESP-IDF project. It is a header-only C++20 library with no dependencies, and one root CMakeLists.txt serves every build. Requirements ¶ A C++20 compiler: GCC 10+, Clang 13+ or a current MSVC. The driver uses concepts and requires . CMake 3.16 or later: it generates the version header the driver includes ( pf1550_version.h ). No RTOS, heap, exceptions or RTTI: every call is noexcept and returns a Result . Get the source ¶ A git submodule keeps the driver pinned to the version you chose: git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-pf1550.git external/driver-pf1550 git submodule update --init external/driver-pf1550 Only inc/ , src/ , cmake/ , _config/ and CMakeLists.txt are needed to build. The examples are not; the ESP32 example even has its own submodule ( examples/esp32/scripts ). CMake (any MCU, any host) ¶ This is the MCU-neutral path: the same two lines work for a host build, STM32 (CubeMX CMake projects), RP2040 (Pico SDK), nRF (nRF Connect SDK) or any other CMake toolchain. Platforms lists what has a port today. add_subdirectory ( external/driver-pf1550 ) target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE pf1550::pf1550 ) pf1550::pf1550 is an alias of the pf1550 INTERFACE target. It carries the include directories (the headers and the generated version header) and requires C++20, so your target does not need to set either. Option Default Effect PF1550_ENABLE_WARNINGS OFF -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic on every target that links the driver PF1550_BUILD_TESTS OFF Builds the host tests in tests/ and the host example ( Testing and CI ) Installed package ¶ To use the driver without adding its source tree to your build, install it and find the package: cmake -S external/driver-pf1550 -B build-pf1550 cmake --install build-pf1550 --prefix /opt/sdk find_package ( pf1550 0.1 REQUIRED ) # with CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/opt/sdk target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE pf1550::pf1550 ) The target is pf1550::pf1550 in both cases ( EXPORT_NAME ), so a project can switch between add_subdirectory() and find_package() without changing its target_link_libraries() . The headers and the generated pf1550_version.h go to include/pf1550/inc/ , the template implementation to include/pf1550/src/pf1550.ipp . The host CI installs the package and builds a consumer against it on every pull request ( Testing and CI ). ESP-IDF ¶ Under ESP-IDF the root CMakeLists.txt registers the repository itself as a component: with ESP_PLATFORM set it calls idf_component_register() from the same build settings, with the menu in _config/Kconfig . There is no wrapper to copy. ESP-IDF names a component after its folder, so the name in your REQUIRES is the name of the folder the repository is in. Pick one of these: How What to write Component name Folder of extra components list(APPEND EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS external/driver-pf1550) in the project CMakeLists.txt , before project.cmake driver-pf1550 (the folder) Submodule under components/ git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-pf1550.git components/pf1550 pf1550 (the folder) Component manager, from git The dependency below in main/idf_component.yml pf1550 (the key) # main/idf_component.yml of your project dependencies : pf1550 : git : https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-pf1550.git version : v0.1.0 # a release tag Your component then declares REQUIRES pf1550 (or the folder name), and idf.py menuconfig shows the driver's menu ( Configuration ). The ESP32 example uses the first way, with EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS pointing at the repository root, and works out the folder name in main/CMakeLists.txt ; CI builds it on every pull request. The repository has no idf_component.yml . The component manager does not need one for a git dependency; the manifest is only required to publish to the ESP Component Registry, which these releases do not use. If registry publishing is chosen, the manifest is added at the root then. How the build is organised ¶ Layer File Role Settings cmake/pf1550_build_settings.cmake Target name, include directories, sources, version: the single source of truth Library CMakeLists.txt INTERFACE target, alias, install rules and the package export, or the ESP-IDF component Tool configuration _config/ Doxyfile, the docs site, Kconfig, clang-format, clang-tidy and the linters Version ¶ The version is set once in the settings file and written into pf1550_version.h in the build tree at configure time. The Doxyfile ( _config/Doxyfile ) carries a copy; a host test fails when it differs. Read it at run time: const char * v = pf1550 :: GetDriverVersion (); // "0.1.0" Next ¶ Quickstart runs the driver on your PC, then on your MCU; Porting writes the port for your MCU.

docs.text: Mechanization policy ¶ Where each defect class of the catalogue is caught, and how a class moves to a cheaper catch. The goal: a defect is found by the cheapest check that can find it, and reviewers spend their time on judgement, not on what a script can do. Decision rule ¶ Catch a class at the first level that can decide it without judgement, in order of cost: Lint ( tools/preflight.sh , runs in seconds, on every builder's machine). Use it when the defect is a pattern in text or syntax: a forbidden include, a MISRA rule CodeQL reports, a missing else , a parameter name, a symbol named in docs that does not exist, a missing gitlink. Test, model or mutation (host tests, the chip model's fault knobs, fuzz properties, compile-fail cases, mutants of a fix). Use it when the defect is behaviour: what the driver sends or returns when the chip or the bus misbehaves. A test is the right level when the model can be made to misbehave in exactly that way. Independent review question (a reviewer who did not write the code). Use it only for what needs judgement: whether the datasheet was read correctly, whether a state machine is complete, whether the model is independent of the driver, whether a doc claim is true. Every catalogue entry names its level under DETECTION. A class with no lint or test is a review class and costs reviewer time every round; it is a candidate for promotion. Promotion ¶ A defect that reached a reviewer or the CI of a second driver is promoted one level up: review to test, test to lint where a pattern exists. The reviewer who finds the second occurrence writes the promotion item in the round's report; the template maintainer (the agent or person that owns the template branch) implements it before the next driver's first push, or records why it cannot be mechanised in the catalogue entry. A defect that reached a third driver after its promotion means the check is wrong: fix the check first, then look at the driver. Demotion never happens by silence: a check is removed only with a catalogue note saying what replaced it. What a lint may and may not do ¶ It reports file:line , the catalogue id, and the fix. docs.text: Where each defect class of the catalogue is caught, and how a class moves to a cheaper catch. The goal: a defect is found by the cheapest check that can find it, and reviewers spend their time on judgement, not on what a script can do.
docs.title: Mechanization policy

docs.text: Catch a class at the first level that can decide it without judgement, in order of cost: Lint ( tools/preflight.sh , runs in seconds, on every builder's machine). Use it when the defect is a pattern in text or syntax: a forbidden include, a MISRA rule CodeQL reports, a missing else , a parameter name, a symbol named in docs that does not exist, a missing gitlink. Test, model or mutation (host tests, the chip model's fault knobs, fuzz properties, compile-fail cases, mutants of a fix). Use it when the defect is behaviour: what the driver sends or returns when the chip or the bus misbehaves. A test is the right level when the model can be made to misbehave in exactly that way. Independent review question (a reviewer who did not write the code). Use it only for what needs judgement: whether the datasheet was read correctly, whether a state machine is complete, whether the model is independent of the driver, whether a doc claim is true. Every catalogue entry names its level under DETECTION. A class with no lint or test is a review class and costs reviewer time every round; it is a candidate for promotion.

A platform is three optional pieces around it, and only examples/<platform>/ holds platform code. Piece Where What it is Port examples/<platform>/ The class that implements the bus hooks for that MCU or OS ( Porting ) Example examples/<platform>/ A program that runs the driver there, built by CI Build integration the root CMakeLists.txt How that platform's build system finds the driver What exists today ¶ Platform Port Example Build integration Built by CI Host (Linux, macOS, Windows) examples/host/host_pf1550_port.hpp (simulated chip) examples/host/ Plain CMake yes, run as a test ESP32 (ESP-IDF) examples/esp32/main/esp32_pf1550_port.hpp examples/esp32/ Root CMakeLists.txt under ESP_PLATFORM (component) yes STM32, RP2040, nRF, other MCUs write one ( Porting ) none yet Plain CMake no Plain CMake ( add_subdirectory() or find_package() , see Installation ) covers STM32, RP2040, nRF and host builds.
