docs.text: Porting ¶ Write the one class that connects the driver to your MCU's I2C bus, and optionally to two pins. Datasheet sections this page relies on From NXP Semiconductors PF1550 7: STANDBY pin: 9.2 STANDBY, p. 69 INTB and the interrupt registers: 9.4 INTB, p. 70 I2C address, clock and register framing: 9.7 Control interface I2C block description, p. 71 I2C operation: single-register transfers: 9.7.2 I2C operation, p. 72 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The driver never calls your SDK. It calls hooks on a class you derive from pf1550::I2cInterface<Self> (in inc/pf1550_i2c_interface.hpp ). The base uses CRTP and declares no hook itself; the driver template is constrained by the pf1550::I2cPort concept, so calls are resolved at compile time (no virtual functions, nothing to allocate) and a missing or misdeclared hook is a compile error at the point of use. What you implement ¶ Method Required Contract bool EnsureInitialized() noexcept yes Bring the bus up on the first call; return true at once afterwards. false makes the driver's EnsureInitialized() return Bus bool Write(uint8_t addr, const uint8_t* data, std::size_t len) noexcept yes START, addr + W, len bytes (register, then one data byte), STOP. false on a NACK or any bus error bool WriteRead(uint8_t addr, const uint8_t* tx, std::size_t tx_len, uint8_t* rx, std::size_t rx_len) noexcept yes START, addr + W, tx (the register), repeated START, addr + R, rx_len (1) byte, STOP void DelayUs(uint32_t us) noexcept yes, for the DVS wait Wait at least us microseconds bool GpioSet(CtrlPin, GpioSignal) noexcept no Drive STANDBY; false if the pin write failed. Without it RequestStandby() returns Unsupported bool GpioGet(CtrlPin, bool& asserted) noexcept no Read INTB; asserted is true when the pin is low. Without it ServiceInterrupts() always reads the chip bool GetLastFailure(I2cFailure& why) noexcept no What the last failed transfer was: AddressNack , DataNack or Bus . Without it the driver cannot tell an absent chip from a bus fault void Log(LogLevel, const char* message) noexcept no Print one line; message is plain text, never a format string addr is the 7-bit address the driver was constructed with; shift it yourself if your SDK wants the 8-bit form. The port ¶ my_port.hpp class MyPort : public pf1550 :: I2cInterface < MyPort > { public : // Bring the bus up once; later calls return true at once. bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { if ( ! ready_ ) { ready_ = platform_i2c_init (); } return ready_ ; } // One write transaction: START, address + W, the bytes (register first), STOP. bool Write ( uint8_t addr , const uint8_t * data , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_i2c_write ( addr , data , len ); } // Write then read with a repeated START in between. bool WriteRead ( uint8_t addr , const uint8_t * tx , std :: size_t tx_len , uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t rx_len ) noexcept { return platform_i2c_write_read ( addr , tx , tx_len , rx , rx_len ); } // Wait at least `us` microseconds: the DVS-done wait depends on it. void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } private : bool ready_ = false ; }; Bus requirements ¶ The driver states what the chip needs as constexpr values; check your port against them with static_assert . Constant Value Why kI2cAddress 0x08 Default 7-bit address; OTP sets 0x08 to 0x0F kMaxClockHz 400 000 Fast mode (section 9.7.2) kRepeatedStart true A register read is a combined write-read with a repeated START; the port must not send a STOP between them kMinEdgeNs 20 Shortest SCL and SDA rise and fall time the chip accepts Transfers are one register at a time: the datasheet does not describe auto-increment (ambiguity C48), so the port never sees a burst of more than one data byte. Buffers. The pointers the driver hands to Write() and WriteRead() point into the driver object (the register bus owns a one-byte read buffer, the register-address byte and a two-byte write frame; no heap, never the caller's stack), so a DMA that reads or fills them reaches them. A port that needs DMA-capable memory places the whole PF1550 object there. The pull-ups on SDA and SCL go to VDDIO (1.7 V to 3.3 V). Size them for 400 kHz and your bus capacitance. An address NACK is the signature of an absent or unpowered chip. Implement GetLastFailure() if your SDK can tell it from a data NACK; the driver then reports NoDevice instead of Bus . Control pins ¶ STANDBY ( CtrlPin::Standby , output): GpioSignal::ACTIVE means "standby requested". With STANDBYINV = 0, the reset value, that is a high level. Drive the pin to its idle level (low) before you enable the output, so configuring it never requests STANDBY. INTB ( CtrlPin::Intb , input): open drain, active low. asserted is true when the pin reads low. Add a pull-up to VDDIO on the board. Optional hooks ¶ A hook that is declared must have exactly the signature above, including noexcept : a hook with a wrong signature is a compile error, never silently ignored. A hook that is absent is detected at compile time and its calls return Unsupported or log nothing. A port with every hook class FullPort : public pf1550 :: I2cInterface < FullPort > { public : bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { return platform_i2c_init (); } bool Write ( uint8_t addr , const uint8_t * data , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_i2c_write ( addr , data , len ); } bool WriteRead ( uint8_t addr , const uint8_t * tx , std :: size_t tx_len , uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t rx_len ) noexcept { return platform_i2c_write_read ( addr , tx , tx_len , rx , rx_len ); } // Required by the DVS wait. void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } // Optional: the STANDBY pin on a GPIO. ACTIVE means "standby requested"; with STANDBYINV = 0 (the // default) that is a high level. bool GpioSet ( pf1550 :: CtrlPin pin , pf1550 :: GpioSignal signal ) noexcept { if ( pin != pf1550 :: CtrlPin :: Standby ) { return false ; } return platform_gpio_write ( kStandbyGpio , signal == pf1550 :: GpioSignal :: ACTIVE ); } // Optional: INTB, open drain. "Asserted" means the pin is low. bool GpioGet ( pf1550 :: CtrlPin pin , bool & asserted ) noexcept { if ( pin != pf1550 :: CtrlPin :: Intb ) { return false ; } asserted = ! platform_gpio_read ( kIntbGpio ); return true ; } // Optional: tells an absent chip (nothing acknowledged the address) from a bus error. bool GetLastFailure ( pf1550 :: I2cFailure & why ) noexcept { why = platform_i2c_last_failure (); return true ; } // Optional: one line per lifecycle event or failure. The driver never formats; the port does. void Log ( pf1550 :: LogLevel level , const char * message ) noexcept { if ( level > pf1550 :: LogLevel :: Warning ) { return ; } platform_log ( message ); // plain text: never use it as a format string } private : static constexpr int kStandbyGpio = 7 ; static constexpr int kIntbGpio = 8 ; }; Using STANDBY pf1550 :: Error EnterStandby ( pf1550 :: PF1550 < FullPort >& pmic ) { // With GpioSet() this drives the STANDBY pin; a port without it gets Error::Unsupported. return pmic . RequestStandby ( true ). error ; } A GpioSet() that returns void is a compile error: the driver must see a failed pin write. The compile-fail tests check this rule, the DelayUs() signature, the noexcept rule and a configuration without limits. Reference implementations ¶ Every port lives with its example, in examples/<platform>/ ; the driver has none. Platforms lists them and how to add one. examples/host/host_pf1550_port.hpp : any PC, against a simulated chip. Start from it for a host build or a test bench; it is also the smallest complete port. examples/esp32/main/esp32_pf1550_port.hpp : ESP-IDF, with every hook. Start from it for any ESP-IDF target. Check your port ¶ Build it: the ports on this page are compiled by the host CI from tests/docs/ , with the driver instantiated over them. Call EnsureInitialized() : Ok proves that writes and reads work and that DEVICE_ID read 0x7C . NoDevice or Bus means the wiring or the address is wrong. Call ReadChargerStatus() and ReadPowerState() : they read only. With a supply on VBUSIN the VBUS flags change. If you added GpioGet() : IntbAsserted() follows INTB. If you added GpioSet() : probe the STANDBY pin while calling RequestStandby() . Threads ¶ The driver is not thread-safe. Give each driver object one owner task, or guard every call with one mutex. When several chips share a bus, the port must also serialise the bus. See Contract . Editor setup ¶ The clang-format and clang-tidy configuration is in _config/ , and the repository root has no copy of it. Tools that take a path use it directly; CI does the same: Tool Setting Command line clang-format --style=file:_config/.clang-format , clang-tidy --config-file=_config/.clang-tidy -p build VS Code (C/C++ extension) "C_Cpp.clang_format_style": "file:${workspaceFolder}/_config/.clang-format" and "C_Cpp.codeAnalysis.clangTidy.args": ["--config-file=${workspaceFolder}/_config/.clang-tidy"] clangd (VS Code clangd, Neovim, Emacs), CLion These find .clang-format and .clang-tidy only by name, from the file upwards: copy both to the root once ( cp _config/.clang-format _config/.clang-tidy . ). .gitignore lists the copies, so they never reach a commit; copy again after _config/ changes Configure with -DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON (clangd: --compile-commands-dir=build ) so the editor sees the same flags as the build.

"Asserted" means the pin is low. bool GpioGet ( pf1550 :: CtrlPin pin , bool & asserted ) noexcept { if ( pin != pf1550 :: CtrlPin :: Intb ) { return false ; } asserted = ! platform_gpio_read ( kIntbGpio ); return true ; } // Optional: tells an absent chip (nothing acknowledged the address) from a bus error. bool GetLastFailure ( pf1550 :: I2cFailure & why ) noexcept { why = platform_i2c_last_failure (); return true ; } // Optional: one line per lifecycle event or failure. The driver never formats; the port does. void Log ( pf1550 :: LogLevel level , const char * message ) noexcept { if ( level > pf1550 :: LogLevel :: Warning ) { return ; } platform_log ( message ); // plain text: never use it as a format string } private : static constexpr int kStandbyGpio = 7 ; static constexpr int kIntbGpio = 8 ; }; Using STANDBY pf1550 :: Error EnterStandby ( pf1550 :: PF1550 < FullPort >& pmic ) { // With GpioSet() this drives the STANDBY pin; a port without it gets Error::Unsupported. return pmic . RequestStandby ( true ). error ; } A GpioSet() that returns void is a compile error: the driver must see a failed pin write. The compile-fail tests check this rule, the DelayUs() signature, the noexcept rule and a configuration without limits.

docs.text: Build it: the ports on this page are compiled by the host CI from tests/docs/ , with the driver instantiated over them. Call EnsureInitialized() : Ok proves that writes and reads work and that DEVICE_ID read 0x7C . NoDevice or Bus means the wiring or the address is wrong. Call ReadChargerStatus() and ReadPowerState() : they read only. With a supply on VBUSIN the VBUS flags change. If you added GpioGet() : IntbAsserted() follows INTB. If you added GpioSet() : probe the STANDBY pin while calling RequestStandby() .

docs.text: The driver is not thread-safe. Give each driver object one owner task, or guard every call with one mutex. When several chips share a bus, the port must also serialise the bus. See Contract .
docs.title: Threads

docs.text: The clang-format and clang-tidy configuration is in _config/ , and the repository root has no copy of it. Tools that take a path use it directly; CI does the same: Tool Setting Command line clang-format --style=file:_config/.clang-format , clang-tidy --config-file=_config/.clang-tidy -p build VS Code (C/C++ extension) "C_Cpp.clang_format_style": "file:${workspaceFolder}/_config/.clang-format" and "C_Cpp.codeAnalysis.clangTidy.args": ["--config-file=${workspaceFolder}/_config/.clang-tidy"] clangd (VS Code clangd, Neovim, Emacs), CLion These find .clang-format and .clang-tidy only by name, from the file upwards: copy both to the root once ( cp _config/.clang-format _config/.clang-tidy . ). .gitignore lists the copies, so they never reach a commit; copy again after _config/ changes Configure with -DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON (clangd: --compile-commands-dir=build ) so the editor sees the same flags as the build.

docs.text: Quickstart ¶ Run the driver on your PC first, with no hardware; then start the PMIC from your MCU: wire the chip, write a small port class, declare what your cell and supply tolerate, and call three driver functions. Datasheet sections this page relies on From NXP Semiconductors PF1550 7: Pins and package: 4.2 Pin definitions, p. 8 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Try it on your PC ¶ examples/host/ runs the real driver against a simulated PF1550, through a host port. From the repository root, with CMake and a C++20 compiler: cmake -S examples/host -B build-example cmake --build build-example ./build-example/pf1550_host_example PF1550 driver 0.1.0 on the host pf1550: initialised charger state 1, fault 0, VBUS valid 1 LDO1 1800000 uV, run 1 0 interrupt passes The calls in main.cpp are the ones below; only the port differs on an MCU. CI builds and runs this example on every pull request. 1. Wire it ¶ MCU PF1550 Notes I2C SCL SCL Pull-up to VDDIO; up to 400 kHz I2C SDA SDA Pull-up to VDDIO GPIO output STANDBY Optional, for RequestStandby() GPIO input INTB Optional, open drain, active low 1.7 V to 3.3 V VDDIO The I/O supply The chip answers at 0x08 unless its OTP set another address ( 0x08 to 0x0F ); pass the address as the third constructor argument. The Hardware page has the full pin list, and the datasheet's example schematic the power connections (battery, supply, regulator outputs and capacitors). 2. Add the driver ¶ Add the repository as a submodule and link the pf1550::pf1550 CMake target. Installation covers CMake on any MCU, the installed package and ESP-IDF. git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-pf1550.git external/driver-pf1550 3. Write the port ¶ The port is the only platform code: it brings the bus up and moves bytes. Replace the platform_* calls with your SDK's. my_port.hpp class MyPort : public pf1550 :: I2cInterface < MyPort > { public : // Bring the bus up once; later calls return true at once. bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { if ( ! ready_ ) { ready_ = platform_i2c_init (); } return ready_ ; } // One write transaction: START, address + W, the bytes (register first), STOP. bool Write ( uint8_t addr , const uint8_t * data , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_i2c_write ( addr , data , len ); } // Write then read with a repeated START in between. bool WriteRead ( uint8_t addr , const uint8_t * tx , std :: size_t tx_len , uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t rx_len ) noexcept { return platform_i2c_write_read ( addr , tx , tx_len , rx , rx_len ); } // Wait at least `us` microseconds: the DVS-done wait depends on it. void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } private : bool ready_ = false ; }; Porting explains each method, the optional hooks and the transfer rules. 4. Declare your limits and start the chip ¶ main.cpp #include "pf1550.hpp" int start_pmic ( MyPort & port ) { pf1550 :: Config config {}; config . limits . cell_max_mv = 4200 ; // from your cell's data sheet config . limits . cell_max_charge_ma = 500 ; // from your cell's data sheet config . limits . input_max_ma = 1000 ; // what your supply delivers pf1550 :: PF1550 < MyPort > pmic ( port , config ); // no I/O yet if ( auto r = pmic . EnsureInitialized (); ! r ) { // 1. bus up, DEVICE_ID, charger as found return static_cast < int > ( r . error ); // NoDevice, DeviceIdMismatch, Unsafe, OutOfLimits ... } const auto status = pmic . ReadChargerStatus (); // 2. read only if ( ! status ) { return static_cast < int > ( status . error ); } return static_cast < int > ( status . value . fault ); // 3. 0 is Fault::None } What each step does: The constructor stores the configuration and does no I/O. Limits has no defaults: your cell's highest charge voltage and current, and what your supply can deliver. EnsureInitialized() rejects a configuration without them ( InvalidArgument ) before it sends anything. EnsureInitialized() calls your port's EnsureInitialized() , checks that DEVICE_ID reads 0x7C , then reads the charger as found. Some pre-programmed options start with the charger on and the fast-charge timer off; if the charger is on and not covered by your limits the call returns Unsafe or OutOfLimits , or, with AsFoundPolicy::MakeSafe , switches charging off. ReadChargerStatus() reads VBUS, the charger state (twice, to catch a change between reads) and the battery state, and classifies the fault. It writes nothing. Nothing was written to the chip in this example. Configure() writes what Config asks for; SetChargerMode() turns charging on. See the API guide . This example is built by the host CI, so it compiles against the current headers. If it does not work ¶ Symptom First thing to check EnsureInitialized() returns InvalidArgument Limits is unset or a value is off the datasheet grid ( Configuration ) EnsureInitialized() returns NoDevice Power, SDA, SCL and the address: nothing acknowledged ( Troubleshooting ) EnsureInitialized() returns Bus Your port's EnsureInitialized() or a bus fault EnsureInitialized() returns DeviceIdMismatch Another chip answered ( Troubleshooting ) EnsureInitialized() returns Unsafe or OutOfLimits The charger was found on outside your limits ( Troubleshooting ) Next ¶ API guide : configure, charge, rails, interrupts, power states, errors. Configuration : limits, acknowledgements, every block, Kconfig. Examples : the host example and the MCU examples. Platforms : which MCUs have a port and an example.

docs.text: Recurring defects ¶ The defects that reached an independent reviewer or the first CI run of more than one driver, one entry per class. Review skills cite these ids; the mechanization policy says where each class is caught and when it moves up a level. Append new findings to the entry they belong to, or add an entry (see the policy). Evidence names the driver, the review round ( reviews/<driver>-review<N>.md , finding id) or the CI run ( reports/<driver>-ci-*.txt ). Code examples are generic and minimal; none quotes a datasheet or a standard. Detection levels: lint (a script in the preflight or the gate, no judgement), test (a model knob, a mutation, a fuzz property or a compile-fail case that fails when the defect is present), review (a named reviewer asks one question). Status: enforced is in the template now; planned is the target, tracked in the policy's backlog, and until it lands the level below it (test, then review) is what protects the driver. Index ¶ Id Class Drivers Detection now Target RD-01 Write after an unseen device reset 4 review test RD-02 Decision from one unvalidated read 5 review test RD-03 Stuck or floating line accepted as data 3 review test RD-04 Invalid argument still sends something 2 test test RD-05 Stop, switch-off or release refused 4 review test RD-06 Transfer buffers on the stack 4 review test RD-07 Chip model shares the driver's misreading 2 review lint + review RD-08 False coverage matrix or fuzz claim 3 review lint RD-09 Docs promise behaviour the code lacks 6 review review (claims check) RD-10 Incomplete state-machine guard 5 review test RD-11 Header outside the library subset 2 lint lint RD-12 Rule 7.0.3 character arithmetic 3 CI lint RD-13 Rule 8.0.1 missing parentheses 2 CI lint RD-14 Rule 9.4.1 else-less chain 3 CI lint RD-15 Rule 0.1.2 unused return value 1 CI lint RD-16 Rule 13.3.3 parameter names differ 1 CI lint RD-17 Rule 7.0.6 literal argument type 4 review lint (partial) + review RD-18 Advisories 6.9.2, 15.1.4, 0.0.2 5 CI lint (known list) RD-19 Template drift 3 lint lint RD-20 ESP-IDF REQUIRES incomplete 1 CI lint RD-21 ESP32 example cannot start with its defaults 3 review test RD-22 Compile-fail regex wording differs by compiler 0 review lint RD-23 Tests are also scanned by MISRA 2 CI, review lint RD-24 Missing gitlink for the scripts submodule 2 lint lint RD-25 Guards no test kills (surviving mutants) 6 review test RD-26 Fuzz target does not check the safety rules 3 review test RD-27 Local tidy and format differ from CI 4 CI lint RD-28 Datasheet misread in a decode, clear or timing 6 review review RD-29 Hardware doc exceeds a datasheet limit 3 review review RD-30 Out-of-bounds or UB before a guard 3 test test RD-31 Clear-on-read flags lost by a diagnostic read 2 review test RD-32 Docs style: line length, merged bullets, stale text 3 lint lint RD-33 Another project's name or dated history 1 lint lint RD-34 Unspecified evaluation order in a test check 3 lint lint Chip-protocol and safety classes ¶ RD-01 Write after an unseen device reset ¶ Rule: every way the chip can reset itself is detected from evidence the chip leaves, and no cached value is written over a chip that may have reset. // bad: the chip browned out; shadow_ holds the old setpoint, the chip is at its reset value // bad: writes the whole shadow_ (the stale rest of it) over a chip that may have reset Result < void > SetLimit ( uint8_t v ) { shadow_ . limit = v ; return WriteReg ( kLimit , Pack ( shadow_ )); } // good: check the evidence first, refuse until the application re-initialises Result < void > SetLimit ( uint8_t v ) { if ( auto r = ResetCheck (); ! r ) { return r ; } // status read, sentinel compare; pending until it passes return WriteReg ( kLimit , Pack ( WithLimit ( shadow_ , v ))); } Hurts: stale state rewritten into a chip at reset values energises outputs or sets limits the application never chose; the call returns Ok. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J1), pf1550 (review1 M8, review2 F1, review3 N1, review4 R4-1, review5 R5-2), tmc5160 (review1 M5), fdo2 (review1 B1: abort during start-up leaves the driver initialised). 4 drivers. Detection: test : model knob "reset mid-session" (registers to reset values, reset flags set) plus a fuzz property "no write after a reset is seen"; mutate the sentinel compare and the pending-check latch, each must fail a test. review : hardware-lessons-review 12a. Question: "List every way this chip resets or reloads; for each, which bit or sentinel shows it, which function reads it, and what does a setter do between the reset and that read?" RD-02 Decision from one unvalidated read ¶ Rule: a read that decides a write, a state change or an identity is validated per the protocol (CRC, echo, length) and a read-modify-write uses only a validated read; a single bad read never clears state or masks a lost write. // bad: one flipped read clears identity, the next switch-off returns NotInitialized and sends nothing if ( ReadReg ( kId ) != kExpectedId ) { identified_ = false ; } // good: two agreeing reads before a state is dropped; switch-off ignores identified_ Hurts: a transient line error becomes "device reset" or "not initialised", a read-modify-write writes garbage bits back, a resync hides a lost write so the chip runs at the wrong current. Seen: pf1550 (review1 B1, M1; review4 R4-3), ads9324 (review1 J2), tmc5160 (review1 M1, lost-write masking by resync), sfm (review1 B1: any NACK after a first sample became DeviceReset), fdo2 (review1 B1). 5 drivers. Detection: test : model fault "one flipped reply at call k" swept over every call of every public function; the expected result is the call's own error, no state loss, no unsafe write. review : hardware-lessons-review 1, 12. Question: "Which reads in this driver decide something, and is there a mutant that removes each validation?" RD-03 Stuck or floating line accepted as data ¶ Rule: a reply a dead, shorted or floating line can produce (all zeros, all ones, the command echoed, one word repeated) is never a measurement or a ready status. // bad: an all-zero frame has a valid CRC for init 0x00, so 0 degC (or -200 degC after the offset) is returned auto t = DecodeTemperature ( words ); // good: reject by pattern before decoding, then plausibility-check the decoded value if ( IsStuck ( words )) { return Error :: NoDevice ; } Hurts: a wrong value is returned as data, which downstream control trusts. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J3), tmc5160 (review1 M8), sfm (review3 M-A: the temperature path had no stuck check while the sample path had one). 3 drivers. Detection: test : one model fault per pattern (zeros, ones, echo, repeat) applied to every read function; a table test lists each public read function and the fault, so a new read function without a row fails. review : hardware-lessons-review 4. Question: "For each read path, which of the four patterns does the CRC pass, and which line in the code refuses it?" RD-04 Invalid argument still sends something ¶ Rule: a call that returns InvalidArgument (or any precondition error) sent nothing and changed nothing; validate first, transfer second. // bad: reads the position first, then rejects the argument auto pos = ReadPos (); if ( steps > kMax ) { return Error :: InvalidArgument ; } // good if ( steps > kMax ) { return Error :: InvalidArgument ; } auto pos = ReadPos (); Hurts: a rejected call moves state or leaves the driver config invalid, and the next call sends from it. Seen: tmc5160 (review1 M2: three sites, found by a fuzz abort), ads9324 (review2 N2: a division by convst_hz before the state check). 2 drivers. Detection: test : the model counts frames; every InvalidArgument test asserts the count is unchanged, and the fuzz target asserts it for every call that returned InvalidArgument . review : hardware-lessons-review 11. Question: "For each early return of an argument error, what is the first line above it that touches the port?" RD-05 Stop, switch-off or release refused ¶ Rule: a switch-off, a release to input and Deinitialize() are never refused for any uncertainty (reset report, failed read, unknown mode, uninitialised after reset) and always send their writes, in the smallest atomic form. // bad Result < void > Off () { if ( ! identified_ ) { return Error :: NotInitialized ; } return Write ( kEnable , 0 ); } // good: acts first, reports after Result < void > Off () { auto r = Write ( kEnable , 0 ); MarkUnverified (); return r ; } Hurts: the one command that makes the system safe is the one that fails when the system is most in doubt. Seen: ads9324 (review2 N1), pf1550 (review2 F2, review3 N2, review4 R4-3), tmc5160 (review3: stop and switch-off refused after a reset report; review1 M4: not verified on UART), alicat (review2 N3: a switch-off in an unknown state is sent only to the held settings). 4 drivers. Detection: test : for every uncertainty flag the driver has, a test sets it through the model and asserts the switch-off still writes (mutation: add the refusal back, the test fails). review : hardware-lessons-review 12c. Question: "Name each flag that can make a call return early; show the test where it is set and Off still sends." RD-06 Transfer buffers on the stack ¶ Rule: buffers handed to the bus are members of the driver object (memory a DMA engine reaches), never locals or function-local statics. // bad Result < void > Read ( Reg r ) { std :: array < uint8_t , 4 > tx {}; return port_ . Transfer ( tx . data (), rx , 4 ); } // good std :: array < uint8_t , 4 > tx_ {}; // member Hurts: DMA or TCM-stack ports fail on the first frame; the host build and a DMA-disabled example hide it. Seen: ads9324 (review2 N3), pf1550 (review3 N3), bno08x (review1 M-1, UART receive buffers, and the contract said the opposite), tmc5160 (review3 M3; its fix was killed by an address-in-object test, review4). 4 drivers. Alicat keeps its buffers in the bus object (review3). The ads9324 fix still had a survivor that pinned no ownership (review3 m2): the address test below closes that. Detection: test : the mock port records the address of every transmit and receive buffer and asserts it lies inside [&driver, &driver + sizeof(driver)) ; compile it into the shared model. review : KB-HW-019. Question: "In every function that calls the port, where does the memory of each buffer argument live?" RD-07 Chip model shares the driver's misreading ¶ Rule: the model is written from the datasheet, including frame layout, not from the driver; golden frames are transcribed from the datasheet's figures and checked by a test the driver's author did not derive from the code. // bad: driver and model both put the data in bytes 1..2 of the reply, the datasheet says bytes 0..1 of the data word // good: test_model.cpp pins a golden frame copied from the datasheet figure; model includes no driver header Hurts: green tests, wrong data on the wire; only hardware or an independent reader shows it. Seen: ads9324 (review1 B1: wrong bits of the reply, model and driver agreed), tmc5160 (review5 m2: the model set a status bit the instant the velocity was zero, the chip sets it 2^20 clocks later). 2 drivers. Detection: lint : tests/mock_*.hpp includes no driver header (planned, preflight model-standalone ); review : datasheet-conformance, independence check. Question: "Take one golden frame from the datasheet figure; which test fails if the driver and the model both decode it the other way?" RD-10 Incomplete state-machine guard ¶ Rule: every command is checked against every state the chip or the driver can be in, including pending timers, power gates, asleep and in-doubt; a start-up that leaves anything pending does not energise. // bad: waits only for velocity == 0, but the chip is still counting a stand-still delay and will drive back while ( Velocity () != 0 ) { } Enable (); // good: also checks the pending-delay flag the datasheet names while ( Velocity () != 0 || DelayActive ()) { } Enable (); Hurts: outputs energise in a state the guard did not consider; the motion or power surprise is real. Seen: tmc5160 (review5 M1: enable during a pending zero-wait), ws2812 (review2 N1: the power gate started open), pf1550 (review1 M3, M4: rail enabled with a voltage no limit checked), sfm (review1 M2: soft reset accepted while asleep), fdo2 (review1 B1). 5 drivers. Detection: test : a generated state x command table test (every public command in every modelled state, expected result and frame count), and a mutant for each guard. review : hardware-lessons-review 11, 12. Question: "Draw the states from the datasheet; for each command and state, where is the guard and which test removes it?" RD-30 Out-of-bounds or UB before a guard ¶ Rule: bounds, divisors and state are checked before they are used, on every path, including the framing layer. Hurts: abort in hardened builds, UB elsewhere. Seen: bno08x (review1 B-1: a framer returned a frame longer than its buffer), ads9324 (review2 N2: divide before the state check), tmc5160 (review1: fuzz aborts, see RD-04). 3 drivers. Detection: test : libFuzzer with ASan and UBSan in the gate ( enforced ); fuzz target feeds every public function. review : question "which divisor, index or span length comes from a caller or the chip, and where is it checked?" RD-31 Clear-on-read flags lost by a diagnostic read ¶ Rule: clear-on-read and write-1-to-clear flags collect in one driver-owned latch; a self-check or raw read never discards them. Seen: pf1550 (review1 M2: SelfCheck() and ReadRegister() read status registers the chip clears on read), tmc5160 (review1: Service() cleared the stall event, a BLOCKER, review1 B1). 2 drivers. Detection: test : model with clear-on-read bits; test reads through every diagnostic path, then asserts the latch still reports the fault. review : hardware-lessons-review 10, 12b. Datasheet and documentation classes ¶ RD-28 Datasheet misread in a decode, clear or timing ¶ Rule: every field position, clear semantic, wait and gap cites its section and has a test that pins it independently. Seen: ads9324 (review1 B1, J4), tmc5160 (review1 B1), sfm (review1 M3, M4), ws2812 (review1 M2, M3), fdo2 (review1 M3, M4). 6 drivers. Detection: review (datasheet-conformance): re-derive the five facts the change touches from the datasheet before reading the code. Question: "For this register or frame, what do the datasheet's bits say, and does the code agree before you look at the model?" RD-29 Hardware doc exceeds a datasheet limit ¶ Rule: a reference circuit, wiring table or example never exceeds an absolute maximum or ties a pin the datasheet forbids tying. Seen: ws2812 (review1 M7), fdo2 (review1 M9), ws2812 (review1 M3: documents disagree on the input threshold). 3 drivers. Detection: review : docs and diagram pass. Question: "For each net in the reference circuit, what is the highest voltage the chip pin sees, and where does the datasheet allow it?" RD-09 Docs promise behaviour the code lacks ¶ Rule: every behavioural claim in docs, Doxygen, the contract and the build report is checked against the code line that implements it and the test that pins it. /// Enables the bridge again. // doc Result < void > ClearFaults (); // code returns Busy while the motor moves and stays disabled Hurts: callers and later reviewers rely on the claim; a promised error never occurs, a promised recovery never runs. Seen: ws2812 (review1 M5, review2 N2, n9), tmc5160 (review1 M4, review5 m1), fdo2 (review1 M7), pf1550 (review1 M6), bno08x (review1 M-1), ads9324 (review1 J5-J7). 6 drivers. Detection: review via the review-round claims-vs-code check: list every "always", "never", "returns", "enables" in docs and the build report and cite the code line and test for each. Mechanical part ( lint , planned): every Error named in docs exists; every Doxygen @return lists the values the function can return. RD-08 False coverage matrix or fuzz claim ¶ Rule: a matrix row, test id or knob named in docs exists in code, and a row's test asserts the row. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J5, J6: 873 rows unproved, fuzz claims invariants it does not check), pf1550 (review2 F4: 47 rows cite symbols that do not exist; F5: knobs that do not exist; review1 M11), ws2812 (review2 n9: "each fix has a test" overstated). 3 drivers. Detection: lint (planned claims-symbols ): every backticked identifier in the datasheet coverage page, the coverage matrix and docs/ambiguities.md resolves with grep in inc/ src/ tests/ . review : row-level sample. RD-32 Docs style ¶ Rule: Markdown lines are at most 120 characters, list items are separated, text changed by a fix is updated everywhere. Seen: ws2812 (review2 n4, n5, n6), ntc (review1), mcp9700 (review2 m2-1). 3 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced : markdownlint in the preflight; line length 120). Stale text after a change is RD-09. RD-33 Another project's name or dated history ¶ Seen: ntc (review1 M5: old-history wording in eleven places). 1 driver; enforced by tools/check_standalone.py . Process and test-quality classes ¶ RD-25 Guards no test kills ¶ Rule: every guard that protects a write, a state or a value has a test that fails when the guard is removed. Seen: ads9324 (review1 mutants M22 to N66), pf1550 (review2 F3, review3 N4, review4 R4-2: 7 of 12 survivors matter, review5 R5-1), tmc5160 (review1 M6: 22 of 50 survive), bno08x (review1 M-3: 33 survive), alicat (review2, review3). 6 drivers. Detection: test : a mutation runner over the guard lines (one-edit mutants: negate, drop, swap constant), built by the reviewer in each round; target: a template tools/mutate.py run by the gate with a survivor budget of zero on guards. review : the review-round mutant check of fixes. RD-26 Fuzz target does not check the safety rules ¶ Rule: the fuzz target asserts the invariants of the safety rules (no write after a reset is seen, no switch-on in doubt, no frame after InvalidArgument), and a mutant of each invariant fails it. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J6), pf1550 (review1 M10, review3 N4: blind to a missed reset), alicat (review2 m9, review3 m9: no no-write-in-doubt invariant). 3 drivers. Detection: test : mutate the invariant check in the harness; review : question "which safety rule does the fuzz target assert, and what input would break each?" RD-34 Unspecified evaluation order in a test check ¶ Rule: a call in a test or fuzz target takes, as separate arguments, no operation that changes state together with a read of that state ( sent() , Transfers() , pending() , a flag, a counter, a clock). The order of the arguments of a call, of the operands of + - == < and of the two sides of an assignment is unspecified; GCC on x86-64 evaluates arguments right to left, Clang and GCC on aarch64 left to right. Braced-init lists, && , || , ?: and , are sequenced. Two reads of the fuzzer's input ( in.Byte() , FuzzConfig(in) ) in one expression count as well: they advance the input, so the same corpus file decodes into different calls per compiler. // bad: x86-64 GCC reads sent() before the call, so it is always 0 here Check ( d . Write ( v ), was_up , sent ()); // good: the result first, then the read; or pass the probe and read it inside the helper, after the call const auto r = d . Write ( v ); Check ( r , was_up , sent ()); Hurts: the check passes, or aborts, on one CI runner only. A "nothing was sent" promise becomes vacuous, and a positive promise ( sent >= 1 ) aborts on a correct driver; neither shows on an Apple-silicon or aarch64 rehearsal. Seen: dynamixel (first CI, sent >= 1 aborted on x86-64 GCC only), pcal9555 (three fuzz cases, latent), tle92466ed (16 fuzz cases, vacuous; 6 more with two input reads), the template's own fuzz target (5 cases). 3 drivers, all copies of the same pattern. Detection: lint ( enforced ): tools/eval_order_check.py , the eval-order preflight step, scans tests/ and examples/ . test : the fuzz replay with a one-edit mutant that must abort ( mutant_replay_* , kept out of the fuzz_* names so the libFuzzer job does not pick it up). RD-24 Missing gitlink for the scripts submodule ¶ Seen: sfm (review3 M-B), mcp9700 first push (the ESP32 examples job fails: no such directory). 2 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced ): the gate runs git ls-files -s | grep ^160000 after setting the pinned commit. RD-19 Template drift ¶ Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci2.txt : drift warning and a 160-character workflow line), alicat (review1 m6) and pf1550 (review4 m-3): the template record said unknown . 3 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced ): scaffold.py --check-drift in the gate. RD-27 Local tidy and format differ from CI ¶ Rule: the preflight runs clang-format 20 and clang-tidy over the same file list and compile database as CI, inside the container. Seen: ntc (first CI: tidy failed on a generated file absent from a configure-only database), bno08x (review1 M-2: readability-named-parameter in the install consumer), fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-failed.log : lint job, 2 files), fdo2 later (tidy on the ESP32 stub). 4 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced in the container preflight once it uses a configure-only database; check the log names the tidy file count). CI-only checks (MISRA scan, ESP-IDF, compile-fail) ¶ RD-11 Header outside the library subset ¶ Rule: #include <...> in inc/ and src/ is only from the driver subset of the handbook (KB-CPP-012). #include <numeric> // bad: not in the subset; std::accumulate -> write the OR out #include <string_view> Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci2.txt , <string_view> ), tmc5160 (review4 B1, <numeric> ). 2 drivers; the second hit makes it a lint. Detection: lint ( enforced in handbook_check; the preflight must also run the include scan or grep). RD-12 Rule 7.0.3 character arithmetic ¶ Rule: no arithmetic or comparison on a char value, including c - '0' and c == 'x' . int d = c - '0' ; // bad if ( c == 'A' ) {} // bad const int d = DigitValue ( c ); // good: lookup in a constexpr digit array via std::find Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-misra.txt , reports/fdo2-ci2.txt : the bare comparisons too), alicat (review2: about 30 computations predicted; review3 R3-M1, six conversions; m-10, tests), pf1550 (review4 m-4: a template file used in tests). 3 drivers. Detection: lint : misra_lint rule 7.0.3 (planned): char literals in arithmetic or comparison in inc src tests examples . Until then: grep '.' next to - , + , == , != . RD-13 Rule 8.0.1 missing parentheses ¶ Rule: a binary operand that is itself a binary expression of higher precedence is parenthesised, in static_assert too. static_assert ( kA == 1 && kB < 2 ); // bad static_assert (( kA == 1 ) && ( kB < 2 )); // good Seen: ads9324 ( reports/ads9324-ci-misra.txt , three lines), pf1550 (review4 m-1: static_assert s). 2 drivers. Detection: lint : misra_lint rule 8.0.1 (planned): parenthesis-depth scan of inc src tests . RD-14 Rule 9.4.1 else-less chain ¶ Rule: every if ... else if chain ends with else , with a comment when empty; in tests and models too. Seen: ads9324 ( reports/ads9324-ci-misra.txt ), fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci3.txt ), tmc5160 (review5 B1: two chains in the model). 3 drivers. Detection: lint : misra_lint rule 9.4.1 (planned). RD-15 Rule 0.1.2 unused return value ¶ Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-misra.txt : failInit ). 1 driver. Detection: lint : rule 0.1.2 (planned): a call to a non-void function as an expression statement; mark with an explicit discard where intended. RD-16 Rule 13.3.3 parameter names differ ¶ Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-misra.txt : checkOxygen ). 1 driver. Detection: lint : rule 13.3.3 (planned): declaration in inc/ against definition in src/*.ipp . RD-17 Rule 7.0.6 literal argument type ¶ Rule: a constant argument has its parameter's type ( _u32 literal), and no mixed-width arithmetic on literals. Seen: ntc (review1 M3), fdo2 (review1 M10), tmc5160 (review1 M7), ws2812 (review1: call sites). 4 drivers. Detection: lint (partial, planned): literal passed to a uint32_t or uint8_t parameter of a known function; review for the rest (the CI scan is final). Question: "Which call passes a bare integer constant to a narrower parameter?" RD-18 Advisories 6.9.2, 15.1.4, 0.0.2 ¶ Rule: these three appear on every driver and need no re-report: 6.9.2 on the unsigned long long literal-operator parameter and on the version getters, 15.1.4 on a constructor whose members have default initialisers, 0.0.2 on a condition a constant-hook port makes always the same. Seen in CI: fdo2, ads9324 ( reports/fdo2-ci-misra.txt , reports/ads9324-ci-misra.txt ); predicted by the reviewer from those runs: pf1550 (review3, review4 m-4), alicat (review3, review4), bno08x (review1). 5 drivers. Detection: lint (planned): the gate compares the CodeQL advisory list to this known list; anything else is new. Reviewers do not report the known three; whether to record them as deviations is an owner decision. RD-20 ESP-IDF REQUIRES incomplete ¶ Rule: every #include of an ESP-IDF header in examples/esp32/main has its component in REQUIRES . Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-failed.log : esp_timer.h ; the ESP32 job failed in both examples). Later reviews found it clean ( pf1550 review5). 1 driver. Detection: lint (planned): include-to-component map checked against the idf_component_register call. RD-21 ESP32 example cannot start with its defaults ¶ Rule: the example's default pins and Config start up; an optional hook returns true when the pin is absent. Seen: fdo2 (review1 M5), mcp9700 (review1 B-1: GpioSet returned false with the default -1 pin), ntc (review1 M1). 3 drivers. Detection: test : build the ESP32 port against stub ESP headers on the host and run the example's start-up with default Config . review : question "does app_main with the default pins reach the first measurement?" RD-22 Compile-fail regex wording differs by compiler ¶ Rule: an EXPECT: is a concept or type name, or the static_assert text, never compiler wording. Seen: no CI failure yet. Reviewers could not confirm GCC 13/14 and clang CI wording for alicat, pf1550, bno08x (review4, review5, review1). 0 driver hits; listed because it is unverified each time. Detection: lint (planned): every EXPECT: string is static assertion failed , an identifier, or a string from a static_assert . RD-23 Tests are also scanned by MISRA ¶ Rule: the MISRA job builds with tests on, so tests/ , models, fuzz and consumers meet the same rules as inc/ . Seen: tmc5160 (review5 B1, the model), alicat (review3 m-10: char compares in tests and the model, "if CodeQL scans tests"). 2 drivers; whether the job reports test files is not proved by the two CI runs on file. Detection: lint : every misra_lint rule scans tests/ examples/ as well as inc/ src/ .
docs.title: Recurring defects

docs.text: The defects that reached an independent reviewer or the first CI run of more than one driver, one entry per class. Review skills cite these ids; the mechanization policy says where each class is caught and when it moves up a level. Append new findings to the entry they belong to, or add an entry (see the policy). Evidence names the driver, the review round ( reviews/<driver>-review<N>.md , finding id) or the CI run ( reports/<driver>-ci-*.txt ). Code examples are generic and minimal; none quotes a datasheet or a standard. Detection levels: lint (a script in the preflight or the gate, no judgement), test (a model knob, a mutation, a fuzz property or a compile-fail case that fails when the defect is present), review (a named reviewer asks one question). Status: enforced is in the template now; planned is the target, tracked in the policy's backlog, and until it lands the level below it (test, then review) is what protects the driver.

docs.title: Index

docs.text: Rule: every way the chip can reset itself is detected from evidence the chip leaves, and no cached value is written over a chip that may have reset. // bad: the chip browned out; shadow_ holds the old setpoint, the chip is at its reset value // bad: writes the whole shadow_ (the stale rest of it) over a chip that may have reset Result < void > SetLimit ( uint8_t v ) { shadow_ . limit = v ; return WriteReg ( kLimit , Pack ( shadow_ )); } // good: check the evidence first, refuse until the application re-initialises Result < void > SetLimit ( uint8_t v ) { if ( auto r = ResetCheck (); ! r ) { return r ; } // status read, sentinel compare; pending until it passes return WriteReg ( kLimit , Pack ( WithLimit ( shadow_ , v ))); } Hurts: stale state rewritten into a chip at reset values energises outputs or sets limits the application never chose; the call returns Ok. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J1), pf1550 (review1 M8, review2 F1, review3 N1, review4 R4-1, review5 R5-2), tmc5160 (review1 M5), fdo2 (review1 B1: abort during start-up leaves the driver initialised). 4 drivers. Detection: test : model knob "reset mid-session" (registers to reset values, reset flags set) plus a fuzz property "no write after a reset is seen"; mutate the sentinel compare and the pending-check latch, each must fail a test. review : hardware-lessons-review 12a. Question: "List every way this chip resets or reloads; for each, which bit or sentinel shows it, which function reads it, and what does a setter do between the reset and that read?"
docs.title: RD-01 Write after an unseen device reset

docs.text: Rule: a read that decides a write, a state change or an identity is validated per the protocol (CRC, echo, length) and a read-modify-write uses only a validated read; a single bad read never clears state or masks a lost write. // bad: one flipped read clears identity, the next switch-off returns NotInitialized and sends nothing if ( ReadReg ( kId ) != kExpectedId ) { identified_ = false ; } // good: two agreeing reads before a state is dropped; switch-off ignores identified_ Hurts: a transient line error becomes "device reset" or "not initialised", a read-modify-write writes garbage bits back, a resync hides a lost write so the chip runs at the wrong current. Seen: pf1550 (review1 B1, M1; review4 R4-3), ads9324 (review1 J2), tmc5160 (review1 M1, lost-write masking by resync), sfm (review1 B1: any NACK after a first sample became DeviceReset), fdo2 (review1 B1). 5 drivers. Detection: test : model fault "one flipped reply at call k" swept over every call of every public function; the expected result is the call's own error, no state loss, no unsafe write. review : hardware-lessons-review 1, 12. Question: "Which reads in this driver decide something, and is there a mutant that removes each validation?"
docs.title: RD-02 Decision from one unvalidated read

docs.text: Rule: a reply a dead, shorted or floating line can produce (all zeros, all ones, the command echoed, one word repeated) is never a measurement or a ready status. // bad: an all-zero frame has a valid CRC for init 0x00, so 0 degC (or -200 degC after the offset) is returned auto t = DecodeTemperature ( words ); // good: reject by pattern before decoding, then plausibility-check the decoded value if ( IsStuck ( words )) { return Error :: NoDevice ; } Hurts: a wrong value is returned as data, which downstream control trusts. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J3), tmc5160 (review1 M8), sfm (review3 M-A: the temperature path had no stuck check while the sample path had one). 3 drivers. Detection: test : one model fault per pattern (zeros, ones, echo, repeat) applied to every read function; a table test lists each public read function and the fault, so a new read function without a row fails. review : hardware-lessons-review 4. Question: "For each read path, which of the four patterns does the CRC pass, and which line in the code refuses it?"
docs.title: RD-03 Stuck or floating line accepted as data

docs.text: Rule: a call that returns InvalidArgument (or any precondition error) sent nothing and changed nothing; validate first, transfer second. // bad: reads the position first, then rejects the argument auto pos = ReadPos (); if ( steps > kMax ) { return Error :: InvalidArgument ; } // good if ( steps > kMax ) { return Error :: InvalidArgument ; } auto pos = ReadPos (); Hurts: a rejected call moves state or leaves the driver config invalid, and the next call sends from it. Seen: tmc5160 (review1 M2: three sites, found by a fuzz abort), ads9324 (review2 N2: a division by convst_hz before the state check). 2 drivers. Detection: test : the model counts frames; every InvalidArgument test asserts the count is unchanged, and the fuzz target asserts it for every call that returned InvalidArgument . review : hardware-lessons-review 11. Question: "For each early return of an argument error, what is the first line above it that touches the port?"
docs.title: RD-04 Invalid argument still sends something

docs.text: Rule: a switch-off, a release to input and Deinitialize() are never refused for any uncertainty (reset report, failed read, unknown mode, uninitialised after reset) and always send their writes, in the smallest atomic form. // bad Result < void > Off () { if ( ! identified_ ) { return Error :: NotInitialized ; } return Write ( kEnable , 0 ); } // good: acts first, reports after Result < void > Off () { auto r = Write ( kEnable , 0 ); MarkUnverified (); return r ; } Hurts: the one command that makes the system safe is the one that fails when the system is most in doubt. Seen: ads9324 (review2 N1), pf1550 (review2 F2, review3 N2, review4 R4-3), tmc5160 (review3: stop and switch-off refused after a reset report; review1 M4: not verified on UART), alicat (review2 N3: a switch-off in an unknown state is sent only to the held settings). 4 drivers. Detection: test : for every uncertainty flag the driver has, a test sets it through the model and asserts the switch-off still writes (mutation: add the refusal back, the test fails). review : hardware-lessons-review 12c. Question: "Name each flag that can make a call return early; show the test where it is set and Off still sends."
docs.title: RD-05 Stop, switch-off or release refused

docs.text: Rule: buffers handed to the bus are members of the driver object (memory a DMA engine reaches), never locals or function-local statics. // bad Result < void > Read ( Reg r ) { std :: array < uint8_t , 4 > tx {}; return port_ . Transfer ( tx . data (), rx , 4 ); } // good std :: array < uint8_t , 4 > tx_ {}; // member Hurts: DMA or TCM-stack ports fail on the first frame; the host build and a DMA-disabled example hide it. Seen: ads9324 (review2 N3), pf1550 (review3 N3), bno08x (review1 M-1, UART receive buffers, and the contract said the opposite), tmc5160 (review3 M3; its fix was killed by an address-in-object test, review4). 4 drivers. Alicat keeps its buffers in the bus object (review3). The ads9324 fix still had a survivor that pinned no ownership (review3 m2): the address test below closes that. Detection: test : the mock port records the address of every transmit and receive buffer and asserts it lies inside [&driver, &driver + sizeof(driver)) ; compile it into the shared model. review : KB-HW-019. Question: "In every function that calls the port, where does the memory of each buffer argument live?"
docs.title: RD-06 Transfer buffers on the stack

docs.text: Rule: the model is written from the datasheet, including frame layout, not from the driver; golden frames are transcribed from the datasheet's figures and checked by a test the driver's author did not derive from the code. // bad: driver and model both put the data in bytes 1..2 of the reply, the datasheet says bytes 0..1 of the data word // good: test_model.cpp pins a golden frame copied from the datasheet figure; model includes no driver header Hurts: green tests, wrong data on the wire; only hardware or an independent reader shows it. Seen: ads9324 (review1 B1: wrong bits of the reply, model and driver agreed), tmc5160 (review5 m2: the model set a status bit the instant the velocity was zero, the chip sets it 2^20 clocks later). 2 drivers. Detection: lint : tests/mock_*.hpp includes no driver header (planned, preflight model-standalone ); review : datasheet-conformance, independence check. Question: "Take one golden frame from the datasheet figure; which test fails if the driver and the model both decode it the other way?"
docs.title: RD-07 Chip model shares the driver's misreading

docs.text: Rule: every command is checked against every state the chip or the driver can be in, including pending timers, power gates, asleep and in-doubt; a start-up that leaves anything pending does not energise. // bad: waits only for velocity == 0, but the chip is still counting a stand-still delay and will drive back while ( Velocity () != 0 ) { } Enable (); // good: also checks the pending-delay flag the datasheet names while ( Velocity () != 0 || DelayActive ()) { } Enable (); Hurts: outputs energise in a state the guard did not consider; the motion or power surprise is real. Seen: tmc5160 (review5 M1: enable during a pending zero-wait), ws2812 (review2 N1: the power gate started open), pf1550 (review1 M3, M4: rail enabled with a voltage no limit checked), sfm (review1 M2: soft reset accepted while asleep), fdo2 (review1 B1). 5 drivers. Detection: test : a generated state x command table test (every public command in every modelled state, expected result and frame count), and a mutant for each guard. review : hardware-lessons-review 11, 12. Question: "Draw the states from the datasheet; for each command and state, where is the guard and which test removes it?"
docs.title: RD-10 Incomplete state-machine guard

docs.text: Rule: bounds, divisors and state are checked before they are used, on every path, including the framing layer. Hurts: abort in hardened builds, UB elsewhere. Seen: bno08x (review1 B-1: a framer returned a frame longer than its buffer), ads9324 (review2 N2: divide before the state check), tmc5160 (review1: fuzz aborts, see RD-04). 3 drivers. Detection: test : libFuzzer with ASan and UBSan in the gate ( enforced ); fuzz target feeds every public function. review : question "which divisor, index or span length comes from a caller or the chip, and where is it checked?"
docs.title: RD-30 Out-of-bounds or UB before a guard

docs.text: Rule: clear-on-read and write-1-to-clear flags collect in one driver-owned latch; a self-check or raw read never discards them. Seen: pf1550 (review1 M2: SelfCheck() and ReadRegister() read status registers the chip clears on read), tmc5160 (review1: Service() cleared the stall event, a BLOCKER, review1 B1). 2 drivers. Detection: test : model with clear-on-read bits; test reads through every diagnostic path, then asserts the latch still reports the fault. review : hardware-lessons-review 10, 12b.
docs.title: RD-31 Clear-on-read flags lost by a diagnostic read

docs.text: Rule: every field position, clear semantic, wait and gap cites its section and has a test that pins it independently. Seen: ads9324 (review1 B1, J4), tmc5160 (review1 B1), sfm (review1 M3, M4), ws2812 (review1 M2, M3), fdo2 (review1 M3, M4). 6 drivers. Detection: review (datasheet-conformance): re-derive the five facts the change touches from the datasheet before reading the code. Question: "For this register or frame, what do the datasheet's bits say, and does the code agree before you look at the model?"
docs.title: RD-28 Datasheet misread in a decode, clear or timing

docs.text: Rule: a reference circuit, wiring table or example never exceeds an absolute maximum or ties a pin the datasheet forbids tying. Seen: ws2812 (review1 M7), fdo2 (review1 M9), ws2812 (review1 M3: documents disagree on the input threshold). 3 drivers. Detection: review : docs and diagram pass. Question: "For each net in the reference circuit, what is the highest voltage the chip pin sees, and where does the datasheet allow it?"
docs.title: RD-29 Hardware doc exceeds a datasheet limit

docs.text: Rule: every behavioural claim in docs, Doxygen, the contract and the build report is checked against the code line that implements it and the test that pins it. /// Enables the bridge again. // doc Result < void > ClearFaults (); // code returns Busy while the motor moves and stays disabled Hurts: callers and later reviewers rely on the claim; a promised error never occurs, a promised recovery never runs. Seen: ws2812 (review1 M5, review2 N2, n9), tmc5160 (review1 M4, review5 m1), fdo2 (review1 M7), pf1550 (review1 M6), bno08x (review1 M-1), ads9324 (review1 J5-J7). 6 drivers. Detection: review via the review-round claims-vs-code check: list every "always", "never", "returns", "enables" in docs and the build report and cite the code line and test for each. Mechanical part ( lint , planned): every Error named in docs exists; every Doxygen @return lists the values the function can return.
docs.title: RD-09 Docs promise behaviour the code lacks

docs.text: Rule: a matrix row, test id or knob named in docs exists in code, and a row's test asserts the row. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J5, J6: 873 rows unproved, fuzz claims invariants it does not check), pf1550 (review2 F4: 47 rows cite symbols that do not exist; F5: knobs that do not exist; review1 M11), ws2812 (review2 n9: "each fix has a test" overstated). 3 drivers. Detection: lint (planned claims-symbols ): every backticked identifier in the datasheet coverage page, the coverage matrix and docs/ambiguities.md resolves with grep in inc/ src/ tests/ . review : row-level sample.
docs.title: RD-08 False coverage matrix or fuzz claim

docs.text: Rule: Markdown lines are at most 120 characters, list items are separated, text changed by a fix is updated everywhere. Seen: ws2812 (review2 n4, n5, n6), ntc (review1), mcp9700 (review2 m2-1). 3 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced : markdownlint in the preflight; line length 120). Stale text after a change is RD-09.
docs.title: RD-32 Docs style

docs.text: Seen: ntc (review1 M5: old-history wording in eleven places). 1 driver; enforced by tools/check_standalone.py .
docs.title: RD-33 Another project's name or dated history

docs.text: Rule: every guard that protects a write, a state or a value has a test that fails when the guard is removed. Seen: ads9324 (review1 mutants M22 to N66), pf1550 (review2 F3, review3 N4, review4 R4-2: 7 of 12 survivors matter, review5 R5-1), tmc5160 (review1 M6: 22 of 50 survive), bno08x (review1 M-3: 33 survive), alicat (review2, review3). 6 drivers. Detection: test : a mutation runner over the guard lines (one-edit mutants: negate, drop, swap constant), built by the reviewer in each round; target: a template tools/mutate.py run by the gate with a survivor budget of zero on guards. review : the review-round mutant check of fixes.
docs.title: RD-25 Guards no test kills

docs.text: Rule: the fuzz target asserts the invariants of the safety rules (no write after a reset is seen, no switch-on in doubt, no frame after InvalidArgument), and a mutant of each invariant fails it. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J6), pf1550 (review1 M10, review3 N4: blind to a missed reset), alicat (review2 m9, review3 m9: no no-write-in-doubt invariant). 3 drivers. Detection: test : mutate the invariant check in the harness; review : question "which safety rule does the fuzz target assert, and what input would break each?"
docs.title: RD-26 Fuzz target does not check the safety rules

docs.text: Rule: a call in a test or fuzz target takes, as separate arguments, no operation that changes state together with a read of that state ( sent() , Transfers() , pending() , a flag, a counter, a clock). The order of the arguments of a call, of the operands of + - == < and of the two sides of an assignment is unspecified; GCC on x86-64 evaluates arguments right to left, Clang and GCC on aarch64 left to right. Braced-init lists, && , || , ?: and , are sequenced. Two reads of the fuzzer's input ( in.Byte() , FuzzConfig(in) ) in one expression count as well: they advance the input, so the same corpus file decodes into different calls per compiler. // bad: x86-64 GCC reads sent() before the call, so it is always 0 here Check ( d . Write ( v ), was_up , sent ()); // good: the result first, then the read; or pass the probe and read it inside the helper, after the call const auto r = d . Write ( v ); Check ( r , was_up , sent ()); Hurts: the check passes, or aborts, on one CI runner only. A "nothing was sent" promise becomes vacuous, and a positive promise ( sent >= 1 ) aborts on a correct driver; neither shows on an Apple-silicon or aarch64 rehearsal. Seen: dynamixel (first CI, sent >= 1 aborted on x86-64 GCC only), pcal9555 (three fuzz cases, latent), tle92466ed (16 fuzz cases, vacuous; 6 more with two input reads), the template's own fuzz target (5 cases). 3 drivers, all copies of the same pattern. Detection: lint ( enforced ): tools/eval_order_check.py , the eval-order preflight step, scans tests/ and examples/ . test : the fuzz replay with a one-edit mutant that must abort ( mutant_replay_* , kept out of the fuzz_* names so the libFuzzer job does not pick it up).
docs.title: RD-34 Unspecified evaluation order in a test check

docs.text: Seen: sfm (review3 M-B), mcp9700 first push (the ESP32 examples job fails: no such directory). 2 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced ): the gate runs git ls-files -s | grep ^160000 after setting the pinned commit.
docs.title: RD-24 Missing gitlink for the scripts submodule

docs.text: Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci2.txt : drift warning and a 160-character workflow line), alicat (review1 m6) and pf1550 (review4 m-3): the template record said unknown . 3 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced ): scaffold.py --check-drift in the gate.
docs.title: RD-19 Template drift

docs.text: Rule: the preflight runs clang-format 20 and clang-tidy over the same file list and compile database as CI, inside the container. Seen: ntc (first CI: tidy failed on a generated file absent from a configure-only database), bno08x (review1 M-2: readability-named-parameter in the install consumer), fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-failed.log : lint job, 2 files), fdo2 later (tidy on the ESP32 stub). 4 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced in the container preflight once it uses a configure-only database; check the log names the tidy file count).
docs.title: RD-27 Local tidy and format differ from CI

docs.text: Rule: #include <...> in inc/ and src/ is only from the driver subset of the handbook (KB-CPP-012). #include <numeric> // bad: not in the subset; std::accumulate -> write the OR out #include <string_view> Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci2.txt , <string_view> ), tmc5160 (review4 B1, <numeric> ). 2 drivers; the second hit makes it a lint. Detection: lint ( enforced in handbook_check; the preflight must also run the include scan or grep).
docs.title: RD-11 Header outside the library subset

docs.text: Rule: no arithmetic or comparison on a char value, including c - '0' and c == 'x' . int d = c - '0' ; // bad if ( c == 'A' ) {} // bad const int d = DigitValue ( c ); // good: lookup in a constexpr digit array via std::find Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-misra.txt , reports/fdo2-ci2.txt : the bare comparisons too), alicat (review2: about 30 computations predicted; review3 R3-M1, six conversions; m-10, tests), pf1550 (review4 m-4: a template file used in tests). 3 drivers. Detection: lint : misra_lint rule 7.0.3 (planned): char literals in arithmetic or comparison in inc src tests examples . Until then: grep '.' next to - , + , == , != .
docs.title: RD-12 Rule 7.0.3 character arithmetic

docs.text: Rule: a binary operand that is itself a binary expression of higher precedence is parenthesised, in static_assert too. static_assert ( kA == 1 && kB < 2 ); // bad static_assert (( kA == 1 ) && ( kB < 2 )); // good Seen: ads9324 ( reports/ads9324-ci-misra.txt , three lines), pf1550 (review4 m-1: static_assert s). 2 drivers. Detection: lint : misra_lint rule 8.0.1 (planned): parenthesis-depth scan of inc src tests .
docs.title: RD-13 Rule 8.0.1 missing parentheses

docs.text: Rule: every if ... else if chain ends with else , with a comment when empty; in tests and models too. Seen: ads9324 ( reports/ads9324-ci-misra.txt ), fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci3.txt ), tmc5160 (review5 B1: two chains in the model). 3 drivers. Detection: lint : misra_lint rule 9.4.1 (planned).
docs.title: RD-14 Rule 9.4.1 else-less chain

docs.text: Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-misra.txt : failInit ). 1 driver. Detection: lint : rule 0.1.2 (planned): a call to a non-void function as an expression statement; mark with an explicit discard where intended.
docs.title: RD-15 Rule 0.1.2 unused return value

docs.text: Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-misra.txt : checkOxygen ). 1 driver. Detection: lint : rule 13.3.3 (planned): declaration in inc/ against definition in src/*.ipp .
docs.title: RD-16 Rule 13.3.3 parameter names differ

docs.text: Rule: a constant argument has its parameter's type ( _u32 literal), and no mixed-width arithmetic on literals. Seen: ntc (review1 M3), fdo2 (review1 M10), tmc5160 (review1 M7), ws2812 (review1: call sites). 4 drivers. Detection: lint (partial, planned): literal passed to a uint32_t or uint8_t parameter of a known function; review for the rest (the CI scan is final). Question: "Which call passes a bare integer constant to a narrower parameter?"
docs.title: RD-17 Rule 7.0.6 literal argument type

docs.text: Rule: these three appear on every driver and need no re-report: 6.9.2 on the unsigned long long literal-operator parameter and on the version getters, 15.1.4 on a constructor whose members have default initialisers, 0.0.2 on a condition a constant-hook port makes always the same. Seen in CI: fdo2, ads9324 ( reports/fdo2-ci-misra.txt , reports/ads9324-ci-misra.txt ); predicted by the reviewer from those runs: pf1550 (review3, review4 m-4), alicat (review3, review4), bno08x (review1). 5 drivers. Detection: lint (planned): the gate compares the CodeQL advisory list to this known list; anything else is new. Reviewers do not report the known three; whether to record them as deviations is an owner decision.
docs.title: RD-18 Advisories 6.9.2, 15.1.4, 0.0.2

docs.text: Rule: every #include of an ESP-IDF header in examples/esp32/main has its component in REQUIRES . Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-failed.log : esp_timer.h ; the ESP32 job failed in both examples). Later reviews found it clean ( pf1550 review5). 1 driver. Detection: lint (planned): include-to-component map checked against the idf_component_register call.
docs.title: RD-20 ESP-IDF REQUIRES incomplete

docs.text: Rule: the example's default pins and Config start up; an optional hook returns true when the pin is absent. Seen: fdo2 (review1 M5), mcp9700 (review1 B-1: GpioSet returned false with the default -1 pin), ntc (review1 M1). 3 drivers. Detection: test : build the ESP32 port against stub ESP headers on the host and run the example's start-up with default Config . review : question "does app_main with the default pins reach the first measurement?"
docs.title: RD-21 ESP32 example cannot start with its defaults

docs.text: Rule: an EXPECT: is a concept or type name, or the static_assert text, never compiler wording. Seen: no CI failure yet. Reviewers could not confirm GCC 13/14 and clang CI wording for alicat, pf1550, bno08x (review4, review5, review1). 0 driver hits; listed because it is unverified each time. Detection: lint (planned): every EXPECT: string is static assertion failed , an identifier, or a string from a static_assert .
docs.title: RD-22 Compile-fail regex wording differs by compiler

docs.text: Rule: the MISRA job builds with tests on, so tests/ , models, fuzz and consumers meet the same rules as inc/ . Seen: tmc5160 (review5 B1, the model), alicat (review3 m-10: char compares in tests and the model, "if CodeQL scans tests"). 2 drivers; whether the job reports test files is not proved by the two CI runs on file. Detection: lint : every misra_lint rule scans tests/ examples/ as well as inc/ src/ .
docs.title: RD-23 Tests are also scanned by MISRA

docs.text: Repository setup ¶ The one-time steps an org owner runs after creating a repository from the template, and before the first PR. The scripts are in kokeb-labs/.github/org/ . Each one is a dry run unless given --apply ; --org names the organisation (a driver lives in kokeb-labs-drivers , everything else in kokeb-labs ) and --repo limits it to one repository. The rules behind them are in repo-governance.md . 1. Create and scaffold ¶ gh repo create kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-<chip> --private --template kokeb-labs/driver-template --clone cd driver-<chip> git switch -c feat/initial-driver python3 tools/setup.py tools/setup.py asks for the bus and a one-sentence description, scaffolds, builds and runs the host tests; tools/scaffold.py --help lists every option ( --platforms host,esp32 is a driver's default; a library gets host unless esp32 is asked for); it ends with a checklist of what is left to fill in. 2. Apply the org settings ¶ From a checkout of kokeb-labs/.github , after adding the repository to org/repos.json by PR. Its entry sets the About: the description is the README's first sentence ( C++20 driver for the <vendor> <parts> <what it is> (<bus>) ), and the topics are the shared kokeb-labs driver embedded cpp20 misra-cpp header-only plus the bus, the device category, the vendor and the part ( i2c pmic nxp pf1550 ): python3 org/kokeb_org.py --org kokeb-labs-drivers --repo driver-<chip> # the plan python3 org/kokeb_org.py --org kokeb-labs-drivers --repo driver-<chip> --apply # settings, Actions, labels, ... A private repository on the free plan gets the settings, Actions policy and labels; security features and rulesets need it public (the tool says which sections it skips). Run it again, with --check to see that nothing is pending, after the repository goes public (section 6). Run it without --apply first to see what changes. 3. Create the labels ¶ --apply in step 2 already creates them; this is the manual way, for a repository outside the org tool. python3 - <<'PY' import subprocess, yaml for label in yaml.safe_load(open(".github/labels.yml")): subprocess.run(["gh", "label", "create", label["name"], "--color", label["color"], "--description", label["description"], "--force"], check=True) PY 4. Require the gate ¶ After the first CI run has produced the check CI gate / gate , add it to the repository's main-review ruleset as described in The required check . 5. Wire it in ¶ Add the repository as a submodule or CMake dependency where it is consumed, in its own pin PR, then follow checklists/new-driver.md . 6. First release candidate and going public ¶ The order that works, and the reason for each step: main green first. Push, and wait for CI on main , including CI gate / gate . The docs publish to gh-pages from main before any tag does. Triage a failure with the release skill, section 5: re-run the failed jobs only when the infrastructure failed. Tag vX.Y.Z-rc.1 on that commit (the release skill). Its CI repeats the run, then the Release workflow publishes the pre-release: firmware, SBOM, checksums. A pre-release publishes its docs under its own tag and takes latest only when no other version holds it. Make it public ( gh repo edit <org>/<repo> --visibility public --accept-visibility-change-consequences ), then python3 org/kokeb_org.py --org kokeb-labs-drivers --repo driver-<chip> --apply : rulesets, secret scanning with push protection, CodeQL and private vulnerability reporting need a public repository. If the last call answers 422, run it again after a few seconds; the new visibility has not reached that endpoint yet. Enable Pages from the gh-pages branch, root, and open https://<org>.github.io/<repo>/ . --check reports 0 change(s) pending . A private repository on the free plan shares a small Actions storage quota with the rest of its organisation. A full quota fails every upload step in every repository of it at once, which looks like a broken workflow and is not one; a public repository does not count against it.
