docs.text: Testing and CI ¶ How the driver is checked: host tests against an independent model of the chip, a fuzzer that corrupts what the chip sends back, compiled documentation, an install test, ESP32 and Cortex-M builds, static analysis and measured quality gates, on every pull request. Host tests ¶ The tests build the real driver against a register model of the PF1550: the 90 documented registers with their access types (read only, write-1-to-clear status, mask, OTP-loaded, command), the ten start-up options A0 to A9 of Table 85, the state machine, the charger (VBUS, thermistor, timers, faults, watchdog), DVS stepping with a DVS-done delay, the interrupt groups with their categories and sense registers, SHIP and CORE_OFF, the power-up and power-down sequencer and the coin cell charge. Each ambiguity of the datasheet that changes behaviour is a knob of the model ( Ambiguities ). The tests build with the firmware's flags, -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti , and warnings as errors, on GCC and Clang. cmake -S . -B build -DPF1550_BUILD_TESTS = ON cmake --build build ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure File Covers tests/test_lifecycle.cpp EnsureInitialized() : identity, the as-found charger check under both policies, every start-up option, a failure at each transfer tests/test_config.cpp Validate() : limits, grids, acknowledgements, rail windows, DVS declaration, at compile time and at run time tests/test_configure.cpp Configure() : block order, the charger written parked and last, read-back, reserved bits preserved, every block tests/test_charger.cpp Charger status and fault classification, modes, restart limit, watchdog, limits re-check tests/test_rails.cpp Rail reads and writes, DVS wait and its timeout, SW3, load switch, low-power acknowledgement tests/test_power.cpp States, STANDBY, SHIP and CORE_OFF preconditions, power-down order, the sequencer functions against the model tests/test_irq.cpp Masks, categories, clear-after-copy, INTB skip, the three clearing readings tests/test_review.cpp One test per finding of the first independent review: stuck and flipped reads, the status latch, held voltages, the DVS declaration, an unsafe charger switched off, shutdown cancel, the load switch, a chip reset tests/test_round2.cpp One test per finding of the second review: switch-offs that are never refused, the read-agreement and reset checks on every call, the DVS wait, and the session run under every reading of the model's knobs tests/test_round4.cpp One test per finding of the fourth review: a cable removal while charging is put right or reported, a refused charge start leaves the charger off, the buffers of reads and writes, and the guards that survived (DVS-declaration start, charge-current limit, INTB shortcut, shutdown and cancel reads, one wrong DEVICE_ID read) tests/test_round5.cpp One test per finding of the fifth review: the guards of the cable-removal check (a limit inside Limits that is not the configured one, a refused charge start with an unacknowledged protection off, single reads), the check without watchdog.enable , a VBUSIN that stays invalid, the check order, LinearOnly, a DEVICE_ID line stuck at zero tests/test_round6.cpp One test per finding of the sixth review: no write of the input limit after an unseen chip reset (status and interrupt paths), a failed check in ServiceInterrupts() is made again and its error returned, a status read with the limit right writes nothing tests/test_round7.cpp One test per finding of the seventh review: a pending input limit check survives ClearLatchedEvents() , a bus error while collecting, a port without GpioGet() , a switch-off after an unseen reset, a failed verification read of a switch-off, the pass bound and count, the charger-group trigger, the pending flag cleared tests/test_round9.cpp One test per finding of the eighth review: a charger interrupt read by a failed service still owes its input limit check (each transfer of the call failed in turn, the count taken from a clean run, with and without ClearLatchedEvents() ), a failed mask write leaves no idle shortcut, a failed service keeps its bits in the latch, ClearLatchedEvents() empties it, a failed switch-off is a bus error, a failed VBUS_SNS read is an error tests/test_round10.cpp The ninth review: a CHG_INT byte read by ReadRegister() still starts the input limit check of the next ServiceInterrupts() (clear on read and write-one-to-clear) tests/test_round8.cpp The reset evidence of a rail control register is the bits the driver changed and verified; a bit it left alone is not a sentinel (a fuzz finding) tests/test_round3.cpp One test per finding of the third review: a cable removal is not a chip reset ( VbusRemoved() ), a switch-off after a failed re-start, the transfer buffers inside the driver object, and the guards that no earlier test reached (a flipped sentinel read, the mask of a sentinel, the reset check of SetIrqMask() and SetPowerDownSequence() , the protection read-back guard, masked INTB sources, a clear that writes only the bits read) tests/fuzz/ The fuzz target; CTest replays its corpus ( pf1550_fuzz_pf1550_corpus ), see below tests/test_errors.cpp The base Error values are 0 to 9; every chip-specific value (16 and up) is returned by some call tests/test_version.cpp The version getters follow the generated header (also against a 9.8.7 probe) tests/test_kconfig.cpp KconfigDefaults() with and without CONFIG_ values tests/compile_fail/ Code that must not compile, each for its EXPECT: diagnostic: a port without DelayUs() , a void GpioSet() , a DelayUs(uint16_t) , a hook with a narrowed parameter or without noexcept , a Config without limits, a class that is not a port tests/mock_pf1550.hpp The register model, with its own register map; the bus framing is in mock_pf1550_bus.hpp tests/test_model.cpp The model's register map against the driver's access table, and its reset values against the data sheet tools/coverage_matrix.py The coverage matrix ( docs/coverage-matrix.csv ): totals equal Coverage , every API name exists in inc/ or src/ , every test file exists ( pf1550_coverage_matrix ) tests/check_version_copy.cmake _config/Doxyfile carries the CMake version examples/host/ The host example, built with the test flags and run ( pf1550_host_example ) tests/check_install.cmake Installs into a scratch prefix and builds tests/install_consumer/ with find_package(pf1550) tests/check_doxygen.cmake Doxygen with _config/Doxyfile and warnings as errors, when doxygen is installed The model stands alone ¶ tests/mock_pf1550.hpp is written from the datasheet, not from the driver: it does not include a driver header. Its register map, field masks, reset values, option table and timing are its own, each with the datasheet table, so a wrong constant in the driver cannot hide behind the same wrong constant in the model (handbook KB-TST-030). tests/test_model.cpp compares the two: every register the driver may write is one the model does not protect, every register the driver does not document is protected in the model, and the model's reset values match Table 85. When a test fails here, one of the two maps is wrong: check it against the table the model names, and fix that one. A new register goes into both, with its check. Every behaviour found on hardware becomes a knob of the model and a test that fails on the code before the fix; the model has a virtual clock ( Elapse() , driven by the mock port's DelayUs() ) for the DVS-done delay. Fuzz tests ¶ Everything the driver reads comes from the chip over the bus, so the data read is what a noisy cable, a wrong part or a broken chip controls. tests/fuzz/fuzz_pf1550.cpp lets libFuzzer choose a start-up option, a configuration (sometimes unsafe on purpose), then up to 64 driver calls, and on every bus transfer what the bus does: pass it to the model, fail it, flip bits of the data read or replace it (and lose an acknowledged write). A corrupted read never repeats the corrupted value of the read before it from the same register: noise is not repeatable, and what does repeat on a real bus is a line stuck at one value: the fuzzer can stick one of the four protection registers (BATFET_CNFG, CHG_OPER, CHG_TMR, THM_REG_CNFG) at a chosen value and free it again, and the driver must not write a protection off from it. The unit tests inject stuck and flipped reads with MockBusState as well. A second configuration byte accepts single acknowledgements, so that each downgrade is tried alone. Between calls it changes the world: a supply, an ONKEY press, a fault, any register poked to any value, a raised interrupt, a reset. After every call it checks the driver's promises and aborts, naming the line, when one breaks: a failed call returns an Error the enum defines; before EnsureInitialized() no call makes a transfer, apart from the calls that work once DEVICE_ID has passed (switching the charger off, switching a rail off, the off step of a restart, the as-found check, cancelling a shutdown request); the driver never writes a read-only, key-protected or undocumented register; no charge voltage or current written exceeds the Limits ; no write newly switches off a protection the application did not acknowledge: battery overcurrent protection (BATFET_OC = 0), the fast-charge timer, the thermistor, DISBATFET; the reset paths and the undervoltage threshold change only with their acknowledgements; no write carries both shutdown commands; a rail enable newly written (any of the six rails, in the DVS register of the state enabled) finds the rail's held voltage inside its Limits window unless a line is stuck on that register, and the load switch bit is set only during EnableLoadSwitch() ; after DeviceReset the driver is uninitialised; SHIP and CORE_OFF are entered only after the matching call returned Ok ; after a limit-checking call that returned Ok with a clean bus ( ServiceChargerWatchdog() , ReadChargerStatus() , a ServiceInterrupts() that reported a charger event or owed a check) and the charger in Charge, the input limit is the configured one when the charger block is applied and VBUS_SNS shows VBUSIN valid (the target decodes VBUS_SNS itself, Table 153), else a valid limit inside Limits . Each ambiguity of the datasheet that changes behaviour is a knob of the model ( Ambiguities ). The tests build with the firmware's flags, -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti , and warnings as errors, on GCC and Clang. cmake -S . -B build -DPF1550_BUILD_TESTS = ON cmake --build build ctest --test-dir written parked and last, read-back, reserved bits preserved, every block tests/test_charger.cpp Charger status and fault classification, modes, restart limit, watchdog, limits re-check order, the sequencer functions against the model tests/test_irq.cpp Masks, categories, clear-after-copy, INTB skip, the three clearing readings tests/test_review.cpp One test per finding of the first independent review: stuck and flipped reads, the status latch, held voltages, the DVS declaration, an unsafe charger switched off, shutdown cancel, the load switch, a chip reset tests/test_round2.cpp One test per finding of the second review: switch-offs that are never refused, the read-agreement and reset checks on every call, the DVS wait, and the session run under every reading of the model's knobs tests/test_round4.cpp One test per finding of the fourth review: a cable removal while charging is put right or reported, a refused charge start leaves the charger off, the buffers of reads and writes, and the guards that survived (DVS-declaration start, charge-current limit, INTB shortcut, shutdown and cancel reads, one wrong DEVICE_ID read) tests/test_round5.cpp One test per finding of the fifth review: the guards of the cable-removal check (a limit inside Limits that is not the configured one, a refused charge start with an unacknowledged protection off, single reads), the check without watchdog.enable , a VBUSIN that stays invalid, the check order, LinearOnly, a DEVICE_ID line stuck at zero tests/test_round6.cpp One test per finding of the sixth review: no write of the input limit after an unseen chip reset (status and interrupt paths), a failed check in ServiceInterrupts() is made again and its error returned, a status read with the limit right writes nothing tests/test_round7.cpp One test per finding of the seventh review: a pending input limit check survives ClearLatchedEvents() , a bus error while collecting, a port without GpioGet() , a switch-off after an unseen reset, a failed verification read of a switch-off, the pass bound and count, the charger-group trigger, the pending flag cleared tests/test_round9.cpp One test per finding of the eighth review: a charger interrupt read by a failed service still owes its input limit check (each transfer of the call failed in turn, the count taken from a clean run, with and without VBUS_SNS read is an error tests/test_round10.cpp The ninth review: a CHG_INT byte read by ReadRegister() still starts the input limit check of the next ServiceInterrupts() (clear on read and write-one-to-clear) tests/test_round8.cpp The reset evidence of a rail control register is the bits the driver changed and verified; a bit it left alone is not a sentinel (a fuzz finding) tests/test_round3.cpp One test per finding of the third review: a cable removal is not a chip reset ( VbusRemoved() ), a switch-off after a failed re-start, the transfer buffers inside the driver object, and the guards that no earlier test reached (a flipped sentinel read, the mask of a sentinel, the reset check of SetIrqMask() and SetPowerDownSequence() , the protection read-back guard, masked INTB sources, a clear that writes only the bits read) tests/fuzz/ The fuzz target; CTest replays its corpus ( pf1550_fuzz_pf1550_corpus ), see below tests/test_errors.cpp The base Error values docs.text: tests/mock_pf1550.hpp is written from the datasheet, not from the driver: it does not include a driver header. Its register map, field masks, reset values, option table and timing are its own, each with the datasheet table, so a wrong constant in the driver cannot hide behind the same wrong constant in the model (handbook KB-TST-030). tests/test_model.cpp compares the two: every register the driver may write is one the model does not protect, every register the driver does not document is protected in the model, and the model's reset values match Table 85. When a test fails here, one of the two maps is wrong: check it against the table the model names, and fix that one. A new register goes into both, with its check. Every behaviour found on hardware becomes a knob of the model and a test that fails on the code before the fix; the model has a virtual clock ( Elapse() , driven by the mock port's DelayUs() ) for the DVS-done delay.

docs.text: Troubleshooting ¶ Symptoms, causes and fixes, cheapest check first. The driver never retries and never hides a failure: each symptom is an Error or a status value you can read. Datasheet sections this page relies on From NXP Semiconductors PF1550 7: Charger faults and restart: 8.9 Fault states, p. 64 Charger watchdog: 8.9.2 Watchdog timer state, p. 65 Device ID, silicon revision and OTP flavour: 12.1 Specific PMIC Registers (Offset is 0x00), p. 80 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . EnsureInitialized returns InvalidArgument ¶ The configuration was rejected before anything was sent. Limits is unset: cell_max_mv , cell_max_charge_ma and input_max_ma have no defaults. A value is off the datasheet grid: charge voltage in 20 mV steps from 3500 to 4440, charge current in 50 mA steps from 100 to 1000, one of 21 input limits, a rail voltage on its table. Call pf1550::Validate(config) on your own: it returns the same error without the bus. OutOfLimits , Unsafe and ReadOnlyRail come from the same function and tell you which rule failed ( Configuration ). EnsureInitialized returns NoDevice ¶ Nothing acknowledged the address. This needs the optional GetLastFailure() hook; without it the same condition is Bus . Is the chip powered (VSYS, VBUSIN or a battery) and is VDDIO present? Is the address right? OTP sets it to 0x08 to 0x0F ; pass it as the third constructor argument. Scan the bus with a logic analyser: which address acknowledges? Are SDA and SCL swapped, or missing their pull-ups to VDDIO? EnsureInitialized returns Bus ¶ The port reported a failure: either EnsureInitialized() returned false or a transfer did. Check that your port's EnsureInitialized() returns true on its own (log it). Check the bus pins and the clock (400 kHz at most) in your port against the board. With a logic analyser, check that the first frame (a read of register 0x00 ) appears on the bus and that the read is a write, a repeated START and a read, not a STOP in between. EnsureInitialized returns DeviceIdMismatch ¶ The chip answered, but DEVICE_ID is not 0x7C . Is another device at that address? Remove the other devices from the bus. A read that returns 0x00 or 0xFF is a floating or stuck line: check the pull-ups and the wiring. The driver reports it as Bus , not DeviceIdMismatch , and keeps a chip it identified before as identified, so a switch-off still goes out. A part of another family, or one that is not a PF1550, will not read 0x7C . EnsureInitialized returns Unsafe or OutOfLimits ¶ The charger was found on, and what it holds is not covered by your Limits and acknowledgements (or the battery path was found forced off, DISBATFET). Some pre-programmed options start with the charger on and the fast-charge timer off (Table 85), so this is the check doing its job. The driver stays uninitialised, and the charger may still be charging. Switch it off first: SetChargerMode(ChargerMode::Off) (or LinearOnly ) works after a failed start-up, as soon as DEVICE_ID has passed. CheckChargerAgainstLimits() works too: it returns what was found ( ChargerAsFound : mode, voltage, current, input limit, timer, thermistor, battery overcurrent, DISBATFET) together with the error. Either raise the limit or set the acknowledgement if your hardware really allows what the chip holds, or set as_found_policy = AsFoundPolicy::MakeSafe so the driver switches charging off (linear regulator only) and checks again. Run EnsureInitialized() again. Configure() then writes your charger settings, and SetChargerMode(Charge) enables charging. A call returns DeviceReset ¶ The chip reset in the middle of the session (UVDET, a watchdog, a REGS_DISABLE pulse): a register the driver changed reads at its start-up value again (the driver compares the bits it changed with what it wrote; PWRUP_I is no reset flag, it also rises at every standby wake-up). The charger is back in its OTP state, which may be on with no timer, and nothing that Configure() wrote is there. Nothing was written by the call that reported it. Call EnsureInitialized() and Configure() again; the as-found check runs again. GetLatchedEvents() still holds the status bits that were read before the reset was seen. A reset that repeats: look at the supply (VSYS undervoltage), the watchdog service interval and ReadPowerState() . A cable removal alone does not cause it: it puts VBUS_LIN_ILIM back to its OTP value (Table 163), which the driver does not take as a reset. The input limit is then the OTP one until the next ServiceChargerWatchdog() , which writes the configured limit again (or switches the charger off with OutOfLimits when it cannot). Configure returns VerifyFailed ¶ A register read back differently from what was just written. Another master on the bus (or the OTP reload after a reset) changed it: look for a second writer. The chip reset behind the driver's back (a brown-out, RESETBMCU): the next call that changes the chip returns DeviceReset (see below); call EnsureInitialized() and Configure() again. A read that is not stable (a noisy or floating line): the driver repeats a read until two agree, and reports VerifyFailed when a register keeps changing or reads all ones. A field the datasheet marks as loaded from OTP may behave differently from the model (ambiguity C4): note the register and the value in the bring-up log. Configure returns ChargerFault, or SetChargerMode refuses ¶ The charger reports a fault state; the parameters are written but charging is not enabled. ReadChargerStatus() and read fault : ThermistorSuspend (battery outside the temperature window or no thermistor), TimerFault (a charge timer expired), BatteryOvervoltage , BatteryMissing , ThermalShutdown , WatchdogExpired . Remove the cause, then RestartCharger() . After three attempts in a row without a charging state it returns Refused : look at the battery and the thermistor, not at the software. With watchdog.enable , a WatchdogExpired means ServiceChargerWatchdog() was not called within the watchdog time: call it every 16 s or less. OutOfLimits from ReadChargerStatus() or ServiceInterrupts() with the charger on: the input limit went back to an OTP value above Limits (a cable removal) and the charger block is not applied, so the charger was switched off. Apply the charger block, so that the configured limit is written again, and start charging. SetRailVoltage returns ReadOnlyRail ¶ SW3's voltage is read only, and the voltage registers of SW1 and SW2 are written only when you declared BuckConfig::dvs = Dvs::Enabled . The chip cannot report the OTP DVS mode (ambiguity C1): read your option's start-up table (Table 85, ReadVariant() ) and declare what it says. SetRailVoltage returns Timeout ¶ The DVS-done flag did not rise within 256 us. Is the rail enabled and loaded within its current limit? A rail that is off does not step. Is DelayUs() waiting at least the requested time? A port whose delay returns early makes the wait end early. SetRailVoltage or SetRailModes returns OutOfLimits ¶ The rail has no window in Limits::rail[...] , or the voltage is outside it. A rail the application did not describe is never enabled or set. Add {min_mv, max_mv, max_load_ma} from the load's data sheet. EnterShip or EnterCoreOff returns Refused ¶ A precondition is not met; nothing was written. EnterShip() needs state Run, Standby or Sleep, VBUS not valid and below UVLO. EnterCoreOff() needs VBUS not valid and ONKEY not pushed. Unplug the supply (or confirm the state with ReadPowerState() ) and call again. The chip enters SHIP only with VBUSIN below 1.0 V (ambiguity C6): with the input between 1 V and UVLO it ends in REGS_DISABLE. ServiceInterrupts returns nothing, though INTB was low ¶ The source is masked (the default): IrqMask{} masks all. Unmask it with SetIrqMask() or Config::irq_mask . With GpioGet() , the driver skips the bus while INTB is high. Does your GpioGet() report asserted when the pin is low? Your own code cleared it: ServiceInterrupts() clears what it reports; call it from one place. Unexpected state after a reset ¶ ReadPowerState() returns Wait , Run , Standby , Sleep or RegsDisable . A chip that reset behind the driver's back (a brown-out, a long ONKEY press, the watchdog) re-reads its OTP values: call EnsureInitialized() (after it has failed or on a new object) and Configure() again, and compare SelfCheck() . The charger reads a state the datasheet does not list ¶ ChargerState::Unknown and Fault::UnknownState mean CHG_SNS or BATT_SNS held a reserved code. Read it again: the first read after a reset may show the reset value (ambiguity C21).
docs.title: Troubleshooting

docs.text: Symptoms, causes and fixes, cheapest check first. The driver never retries and never hides a failure: each symptom is an Error or a status value you can read. Datasheet sections this page relies on From NXP Semiconductors PF1550 7: Charger faults and restart: 8.9 Fault states, p. 64 Charger watchdog: 8.9.2 Watchdog timer state, p. 65 Device ID, silicon revision and OTP flavour: 12.1 Specific PMIC Registers (Offset is 0x00), p. 80 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map .
docs.title: Troubleshooting

docs.text: The configuration was rejected before anything was sent. Limits is unset: cell_max_mv , cell_max_charge_ma and input_max_ma have no defaults. A value is off the datasheet grid: charge voltage in 20 mV steps from 3500 to 4440, charge current in 50 mA steps from 100 to 1000, one of 21 input limits, a rail voltage on its table. Call pf1550::Validate(config) on your own: it returns the same error without the bus. OutOfLimits , Unsafe and ReadOnlyRail come from the same function and tell you which rule failed ( Configuration ).
docs.title: EnsureInitialized returns InvalidArgument

docs.text: Nothing acknowledged the address. This needs the optional GetLastFailure() hook; without it the same condition is Bus . Is the chip powered (VSYS, VBUSIN or a battery) and is VDDIO present? Is the address right? OTP sets it to 0x08 to 0x0F ; pass it as the third constructor argument. Scan the bus with a logic analyser: which address acknowledges? Are SDA and SCL swapped, or missing their pull-ups to VDDIO?
docs.title: EnsureInitialized returns NoDevice

docs.text: The port reported a failure: either EnsureInitialized() returned false or a transfer did. Check that your port's EnsureInitialized() returns true on its own (log it). Check the bus pins and the clock (400 kHz at most) in your port against the board. With a logic analyser, check that the first frame (a read of register 0x00 ) appears on the bus and that the read is a write, a repeated START and a read, not a STOP in between.
docs.title: EnsureInitialized returns Bus

docs.text: The chip answered, but DEVICE_ID is not 0x7C . Is another device at that address? Remove the other devices from the bus. A read that returns 0x00 or 0xFF is a floating or stuck line: check the pull-ups and the wiring. The driver reports it as Bus , not DeviceIdMismatch , and keeps a chip it identified before as identified, so a switch-off still goes out. A part of another family, or one that is not a PF1550, will not read 0x7C .
docs.title: EnsureInitialized returns DeviceIdMismatch

docs.text: The charger was found on, and what it holds is not covered by your Limits and acknowledgements (or the battery path was found forced off, DISBATFET). Some pre-programmed options start with the charger on and the fast-charge timer off (Table 85), so this is the check doing its job. The driver stays uninitialised, and the charger may still be charging. Switch it off first: SetChargerMode(ChargerMode::Off) (or LinearOnly ) works after a failed start-up, as soon as DEVICE_ID has passed. CheckChargerAgainstLimits() works too: it returns what was found ( ChargerAsFound : mode, voltage, current, input limit, timer, thermistor, battery overcurrent, DISBATFET) together with the error. Either raise the limit or set the acknowledgement if your hardware really allows what the chip holds, or set as_found_policy = AsFoundPolicy::MakeSafe so the driver switches charging off (linear regulator only) and checks again. Run EnsureInitialized() again. Configure() then writes your charger settings, and SetChargerMode(Charge) enables charging.
docs.title: EnsureInitialized returns Unsafe or OutOfLimits

docs.text: The chip reset in the middle of the session (UVDET, a watchdog, a REGS_DISABLE pulse): a register the driver changed reads at its start-up value again (the driver compares the bits it changed with what it wrote; PWRUP_I is no reset flag, it also rises at every standby wake-up). The charger is back in its OTP state, which may be on with no timer, and nothing that Configure() wrote is there. Nothing was written by the call that reported it. Call EnsureInitialized() and Configure() again; the as-found check runs again. GetLatchedEvents() still holds the status bits that were read before the reset was seen. A reset that repeats: look at the supply (VSYS undervoltage), the watchdog service interval and ReadPowerState() . A cable removal alone does not cause it: it puts VBUS_LIN_ILIM back to its OTP value (Table 163), which the driver does not take as a reset. The input limit is then the OTP one until the next ServiceChargerWatchdog() , which writes the configured limit again (or switches the charger off with OutOfLimits when it cannot).
docs.title: A call returns DeviceReset

docs.text: A register read back differently from what was just written. Another master on the bus (or the OTP reload after a reset) changed it: look for a second writer. The chip reset behind the driver's back (a brown-out, RESETBMCU): the next call that changes the chip returns DeviceReset (see below); call EnsureInitialized() and Configure() again. A read that is not stable (a noisy or floating line): the driver repeats a read until two agree, and reports VerifyFailed when a register keeps changing or reads all ones. A field the datasheet marks as loaded from OTP may behave differently from the model (ambiguity C4): note the register and the value in the bring-up log.

Inside the PF1550 ¶ Inside the PF1550 Figure description and sources The PF1550's function blocks inside its outline. Arrows between blocks carry signals or data in the direction they point (both ways where they have two heads). The package pins stand on the left and right edges with their numbers, each wired to the block it reaches. Drawn from: docs/hardware.yml ; inc/pf1550_i2c_interface.hpp . The MCU is on the left, each of its pins level with the chip pin it connects to; above each wire is the hook of the driver's port that drives or reads it. Supply pins point up to their supply and decoupling, ground pins down. Pins on the right carry the loads and the pins tied to a supply or ground; a cross marks a pin left open. A dot is a junction; wires that cross without a dot are not connected. Drawn from: docs/hardware.yml ; inc/pf1550_i2c_interface.hpp . The arrows carry the datasheet's dimensions, the dot marks pin 1 and the pads are numbered counter-clockwise from it, coloured by the pin's electrical type (legend below). Pin 1 is marked by the dot; the numbers run counter-clockwise from it. Each pad is coloured by the pin's electrical type (legend below). Next to it is the pin's name and, in mono, the hook of the driver's port that drives or reads it; a pin without a hook is not used by the driver. The dashed square is the exposed pad. Drawn from: docs/hardware.yml ; inc/pf1550_i2c_interface.hpp . Hardware description: docs/hardware.yml Drawn from: docs/hardware.yml inc/pf1550_i2c_interface.hpp The layers, one of them yours ¶ The layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources Top to bottom, each arrow is a call. Your application calls one object, whose public calls are listed from the umbrella header in inc/. The core turns each call into register reads and writes and hands them to the port contract (the CRTP base in inc/*_interface.hpp), which forwards them, at compile time, to the hooks of the port class you write; your port moves the bytes on the bus. The notes on the right say which layers stay the same on every MCU and which one you write. A library without a port contract has only the first two layers.
